items.sum: Bill Laws' report on Belgrave's 100-runner team in the Blackheath 100 x 1 mile relay at Crystal Palace on 31 May 1981, where four juniors broke the U.K. Junior 4 x 1 mile record and the team placed 8th of 25, with every leg's time. Photos of the relay on the following page.
items.s: JUNIORS SET UK RELAY RECORD Bill Laws' report on Belgrave's 100-runner team in the Blackheath 100 x 1 mile relay at Crystal Palace on 31 May 1981, where four juniors broke the U.K. Junior 4 x 1 mile record and the team placed 8th of 25, with every leg's time. Photos of the relay on the following page. Blackheath H~ 100 x 1mile JUNIORS SET UK RELAY RECORD MAY 31st 1981 - CRYSTAL PALACE - BLACKHEATH 100 x 1 MILE RELAY The highlight of this year's race was the running of our younger members whom we sent off on the early stages. Despite racing the day before Paul Richley, Stuart Paton and John Gladwin joined with Mark Sinclair to break Sale's U.K. Junior 1 x 4 Mile record in a time of 17.48.5 - an average of 4.27 miling. Mark Waller and Dave North would have also enabled the record to be broken and it shows how hard it is to make our top junior squad at the moment. Other highlights were 14 year old Michael Blackmore's 4.56, Giles Thrush's 4.50 on no training, and 13 year old Paul Giddea's 5.36. At the other end of the age range Alan Black ran a smooth 4.36 for our fastest vet, pipping Laurie O'Hara by 1 second. Hilary Baxter was our fastest lady. The disappointing aspect was the large number who failed to appear on the day. Many of the vets were still recovering from the London Marathon!! And so at the end we had to collect all the walking wounded for the last few stages so that President Carl Lawton could at least run the last leg. For my money those unfit few who when the chips were down struggled round for the Club were worth all the absent prima donnas put together. Many thanks to you all. P.S. Have a look at Gordon Biscoe's and Bill Couzens' times. They've both started training for next year. items.s: ERNEST OBENG TO RETURN HOME Farewell to sprinter Ernest Obeng, returning to Ghana after his Reading University Masters, with a list of his 1981 race results including his Coca Cola meeting win over Alan Wells. ERNEST OBENG TO RETURN HOME Ernest Obeng along with fellow Belgravians, will look back on 1981 with pleasure. Athletically this has been his finest year with a long series of International Competitions in which he was always well placed, his efforts being flashed across our T.V. screens and culminating in that fine Coca Cola meeting win over Olympic 100m Champion Alan Wells on a balmy September evening. But Ernest's thoughts were not solely on jetting around Europe during the summer. First and foremost he needed to complete project work for his Masters Degree in Agriculture at Reading University, but in addition he found time to support 3 of our League Meetings and on one occasion after an urgent request cancelled a Norwegian trip to compete for us at High Wycombe. Inevitably we knew that Ernest would be returning to Ghana to put his academic qualifications and experience to good use. Sadly, that time has now come and in the next month or so we shall be saying 'au revoir' to the fastest Belgravian of all times. Ernest may well 'detour' to the States for some indoor races on the way home and we wish him well - wouldn't it be great to see Belgrave colours showing the way over 60m indoors! Ernest says he intends to remain a member of Belgrave and will continue to keep in touch in the same way as so many of our overseas members. He is even hopeful that he will be back in Europe next year to race and dare we hope that we will see him once more carrying our colours in a League Meeting. Whatever might transpire we all send our warmest wishes to you Ernest for a happy, productive and prosperous future. And to close a reminder of a great 1981. items.sum: Report on the summer 'Masters' coaching scheme at Battersea Park and Wimbledon, which drew new members including Irish Guards athletes but lacked assistant coaches, with a photo of Mike Winch coaching Wendy Dunsford.
items.s: Coaching Scheme Report on the summer 'Masters' coaching scheme at Battersea Park and Wimbledon, which drew new members including Irish Guards athletes but lacked assistant coaches, with a photo of Mike Winch coaching Wendy Dunsford. Coaching Scheme In the last issue of the Belgravian we gave details of the new 'Masters' coaching scheme which ran at Battersea Park and Wimbledon tracks from May to August. All sessions were well attended with the exception of the high jump where we seem to have several good competitors who do not need to train. After a brief trial period we managed to get our 'Master' coaches visiting Battersea Park on 2 Sunday mornings per month with the exception of the middle distance coaches John Bicourt (Battersea) and John Sullivan (Wimbledon Park) who organised sessions every Sunday throughout the summer. Our spring and field specialists found the advice of Malcolm Coomber (Sprints, horizontal jumps and hurdles) and Mike Winch (discus, shot and javelin) particularly helpful and the results showed in several seasonal personal best performances. In addition the Coaching Scheme attracted a considerable number of new members including many outstanding members of the athletics team from the 1st Battalion Irish Guards stationed at Chelsea Barracks. A major disappointment was the difficulty in attracting and maintaining the interest of some of our own members as Assistant Coaches. If this scheme is to be continued next year, it will be necessary to get more 'in-house' support on the management side so if you think that this is an area where you can help the club, give me a ring and we will organise all the training needed for you to operate effectively U.K. No.1 shot putter Mike Winch instructs Wendy Dunsford as part of our Master Coaching Scheme. items.s: WINTER TRAINING Notice of Tuesday-night winter circuit training at the George Shearing Centre, Battersea, led by John Jeffries and Charlie Gillet, with directions. WINTER TRAINING We have been fortunate in getting from Wandsworth Council, indoor facilities on Tuesday nights throughout the winter at the George Shearing Centre, Este Road, Battersea. John Jeffries will lead circuit training sessions from 6.30 - 8.00 p.m. and will be ably assisted by Charlie Gillet who has been leading sprint training sessions at Battersea Park on Tuesday and Thursday evenings through the summer. Both boys and girls welcome. Directions: Este Road is just north of Clapham Junction Station and is 2nd right off the Falcon Road. The George Shearing Centre is at the end of Este Road - on the right hand side. items.sum: Ladies Secretary Derek Jones reviews the women's 1981 season: 20th in Womens Southern League Div.3, said to be 4th three times and 6th once in the Lily B League (the printed Lily B results on p39 show 6th each time), Surrey relay bronze and individual successes, with thanks to helpers.
items.s: WITH THE LADIES Ladies Secretary Derek Jones reviews the women's 1981 season: 20th in Womens Southern League Div.3, said to be 4th three times and 6th once in the Lily B League (the printed Lily B results on p39 show 6th each time), Surrey relay bronze and individual successes, with thanks to helpers. WITH THE LADIES This has been a very peculiar season. On the one hand the seniors have performed really well, excelling themselves on a number of occasions, but because of our lack of juniors (especially in Southern League matches) we have been forced to accept positions which do not really show our true value. The juniors that have come along have tried their best, but unfortunately they were up against overwhelming odds and this has shown in the results. In some cases some of the teams had more non-scoring athletes than we had in the whole of our team. In the Womens Southern League, Div.3 (North & East) we managed to hold on by the skin of our teeth, finishing in 20th position. (The last 3 Clubs in each of the Div.3 sections are relegated to Division 4). However, this position does not really reflect our true worth. As you will see from the results, we were usually able to dominate the sprints up to 400m, the sprint relay the 800 and 1500m, A strings the long jump and the Shot and Javelin. We also had successes in the 100m Hurdles and 400m Hurdles. Unfortunately, an injury to Julie Barclay disrupted the smooth running of the team, but that made everybody try harder. In the Lily B League which is for Juniors (13-15) and Girls (11-13) our luck of numbers was really felt. In the 4 meetings we finished 4th on 3 occasions and because of injury and other commitments we would have had only 2 fit athletes for one meeting so we reluctantly agreed not to go, and naturally we were 6th. As there are only 3 divisions we cannot go any lower. Having said that the girls that did turn out tried very hard, but without much success. In the Surrey Championships our Sprint Relay squad was pipped on the line by Merton Ladies and had to accept the bronze medal but in a Club record time. Veronica St. Ange was also among the medals in the Middlesex Championships, coming third in the Senior Javelin up at Enfield - again with a new club record. Returning to individual performances, it was good to see the steady progress of Wendy Dunsford in the Shot. (She won 6 out of 6 meetings in the Southern League) and Veronica St. Ange in the Javelin (she won 5 out of 6). Dawn McNeil has also performed well in the Long Jump winning the City Charities for the 2nd year in succession. I did not really want to mention too many people, but I must not forget Glenda Mahoney, Elaine Wilson, Ethel Punter, Earlene Murrell, Joann Warnett and Tina Jordan too, who although she has never won a race has always been there trying. I must also mention Hilary Baxter who has always run well, and has set some first class club records in the 800 and 1500m. Last of the athletes I should like to thank Jackie Barclay for the help she has given me during this Season. At least it has taken some of the weight off my shoulders in trying to get people to come to meetings Turning to the officials side, I would also like to thank those that turned up to help either officiating or recording and also to thank Gordon Doubleday, Arthur Penny, Tom Carter, Bill Lucas, Derek Crookes for coming along to help at these meetings. Whilst we are at it as well thanks once again to Ted Weldin and Arthur St. Ange for being roped in and providing transport and Harry Porter also for being roped in and helping. A word for next summer - we may not be the best team, but we do like a bit of support. The other teams brought along Mums and Dads to help and shout encouragement. At one time our team could make more noise than the other 4 put together but not any more, so please come to the meetings and support or help. Maybe helping is not in some athletes schedules but every little bit helps. If I have missed mentioning anybody personally, then I can only apologise and say that you have my personal thanks for coming along and helping or supporting. items.s: SPOTLIGHT Spotlight profiles of long jumper Derrick Williams and middle-distance runner Stuart Paton, with their bests, progressions and training; Paton's 1500m best is printed as 3.53.2 in the text but 3.52.2 for 1981 in his progression table. SPOTLIGHT By STEVE CROSBIE DERRICK WILLIAMS Derrick Williams is single, aged 22 (25/5/59) and works as a Civil Servant. He is 6' in height and weighs 166 lbs. Apart from athletics he likes reading, music and eating. Derrick whoses' favourite events are the Long Jump, High Jump and 400m wants to improve as much as possible in these events whilst still enjoying them. Personal bests include 100m 11.1; 200m 22.6; 400m 50.0; LJ 7.38; TJ 14.10; HJ 1.90; His annual progression in the long jump has been: 1978 6.90; 1979 7.07; 1980 7.38; 1981 7.30 His most pleasing performances have been gaining his first AAA vest and jumping 7.30 in 1980 which made him aware of his athletic talents. Athletic dislikes include not being able to train or compete due to injury. In addition persons setting unrealistic targets for a competition are not appreciated. A typical weeks' training would take the following form:- M - Jumping off nine strides, 4 x 150, bounding-up stairs T - sprint drills, 4 x 150 or 3 x 300, 5 x 60 " - Weights S - Jumping off eleven strides, 6 x 60, high jumping off five strides 1.75 - 1.80. To help improve Belgrave Derrick would like to see some kind of scouting scheme so as to obtain youngsters on a continued basis to push established members, and possibly merging with another Club. For British athletics an improved coaching system with adoption of some of the tried Eastern European methods. In Derrick's own words "Athletics, for me has to be enjoyable because you can find yourself doing things you know will be very painful and repetitive. You have to have moments when its fun even though you may be very dedicated. I, myself, am not very competitive or dedicated compared with some so the enjoyment of athletics is very important to me." STUART PATON Stuart Paton, age 18, height 5' 8", weight 9 stone. He is single, enjoys music and having a laugh and works as a banker with National Westminster. Stuart's favourite events are the 800m and 1500m. Personal bests at these events are: 1.54.0 and 3.53.2. Other P.b's include a 53.7 400m and 5.53.2 2000 S/C. He is coached by Mick Dunphy and names Lasse Viren as his athletic inspiration. Winning the Scottish AAA Youth 800m in 1980 has given Stuart his most pleasing performance so far whilst losing and running on bad tracks are amongst his athletic dislikes. A typical weeks training: M - run 8 miles; T - short recovery reps; W - run 6 miles; T - Speed work; F - rest or two mile jog; S - race or run 10 miles; S - long reps on hilly terrain. Stuart would like to see improvements within Belgrave which include taking teams to major races like Gateshead and having weekend training courses for club members. In British athletics he would like to see more youth and B internationals to provide experience for up and coming athletes. Finally, Stuart believes athletics should go open or at least allow athletes to receive more sponsership. Left Derrick Williams - our talented all rounder here seen in the 100 x 1 mile relay. items.s: VETS. CORNER Vets Corner: John Wasbrough elected Vets Section Secretary at the September AGM, with news of injured and returning veterans and his phone numbers. VETS. CORNER Vets Hon Sec At the A.G.M. in September, John Wasbrough was elected Vets Section Secretary. John will be 40 in November and no doubt will be keen to get you all out during the winter. At present it is not clear how strong we will be - Pat O'Connor and Keith Sinclair are injured. Lional Maun and Laurie O'Hara are both going well and Bill Laws and Bob Kersey are back in training, so it could be interesting. Where is who? Oh, Brian's in Africa again! John's home number is [phone number withheld] and his work number is [phone number withheld], so let him know of your plans. items.s: GORMAN ATTACKED Brian Gorman tells of being stabbed three times in a midnight attack while on holiday in Sousse, Tunisia, the same day he was 2nd in a televised 7km road race; the piece gives the date of the club meeting as October 17th and the attack as October 4th. GORMAN ATTACKED Brian Gorman was on duty serving refreshments at our home C.C. League meeting on October 17th and joking about 3 stab wounds he received while on holiday in Sousse, Tunisia. Which of the vets had put out a contract on him? Joking apart, the attack which took place in a shopping precinct at midnight, could have been more serious and the police thought Brian had been lucky to get away without serious injury. Earlier the same day (October 4th) Brian had finished 2nd in an open 7km road race which had been televised. items.sum: Clive Shippen's tribute to Vice-President Rangit Bhatia, a Delhi University professor and Indian 1960 Olympian, who raced three times on a summer visit to England, won the Indian National Vets 5,000m and 10,000m titles and now serves on the Indian AAA Selection Committee.
items.s: Clive Shippen's tribute to Vice-President Rangit Bhatia, a Delhi University professor and Indian 1960 Olympian, who raced three times on a summer visit to England, won the Indian National Vets 5,000m and 10,000m titles and now serves on the Indian AAA Selection Committee. "That staunch Belgravian Rangit Bhatia, a Vice-President of the Club, was in England again this summer for a 3 weeks working holiday. He is a Professor at Delhi University and was representing India at the meetings in England of the Rhodes Scholarships Committee. Although 45 years of age he still keeps himself pretty fit and wherever he travels his Belgrave vest goes with him. This year he won the Indian National Vets titles at 5,000m and 10,000m. During this summer's visit he managed to fit in 3 races, including the Hanwell Carnival '5' and the Lambeth Festival 10 km and clearly enjoyed his return to the English road-racing scene. Although the old speed is no longer there, the style and strong finish still brought back memories of that 1957/60 period when Rangit gained his Oxford 'Blue', ran key stages in the London-Brighton Relay and set a record on our '5¾' course of 27:56. He set his seal on this purple period by representing India in the Rome Olympics at 5,000, 10,000 and marathon, though as Asia's fastest miler he had wanted the 1500 spot! He is now a member of the Indian A.A.A. Selection Committee and has been nominated for the Technical Committee of next year's Asian Games which are to be held in Delhi. He is a respected journalist too, and has been instrumental in getting leading athletes and coaches to visit Delhi to impart their knowledge. In fact a cordial welcome awaits any athlete wishing to visit that part of the world and there must be scores who regard Delhi as synonymous with Rangit Bhatia. He is held in high esteem academically, athletically, administratively and personally, and it was no surprise that he should be introduced to Prince Charles and our Prime Minister during their tours of India earlier this year. Throughout all this activity Rangit remains an ardent Belgravian, always keen to receive our latest Gazette. In turn, the Club is proud to have such a loyal Vice-President. Rangit sends his very warm regards to all members and particularly to those who were so close to him during those halcyon days of 1957/60." CLIVE SHIPPEN Rangit Bhatia Rangit Bhatia Vice-President; Professor at Delhi University; won Indian National Vets 5,000m and 10,000m 1981; Oxford Blue; represented India at Rome Olympics 1960 (5,000, 10,000, marathon); record 27:56 on the club 5¾ course; member of Indian A.A.A. items.s: DEVELOPMENT PLANS Editorial explaining that the club, now with over £6,000 in the bank after improving its hall, will re-invest in a more ambitious improvement scheme, and noting developments at the Battersea track. DEVELOPMENT PLANS Some 5 years ago and with £4,500 in the bank our Committee decided to invest everything in improving the social facilities at Belgrave. Two years later we were broke and hoping we had made the right decision. Now the Hall is a changed place and makes a fine meeting place for all members and their families. What's more, the bar revenue, plus the efforts of several loyal and hard working members have results in a situation where we find ourselves now with over £6,000 in the bank. A fine situation and yet one on which to build. So - oncė again our Committee has decided to re-invest much of this sum in an even more ambitious improvement scheme. The story may be read in the centre pages of this issue. Our efforts will not`cease there. We are aware that developments are also afoot at our home track at Battersea and we plan to maximise on that opportunity to further build on our athletic activities. items.s: OFFICIAL SHORTAGE Editorial on the shortage of officials, praising the new sectional secretaries John Wasbrough, Leo Coy and Ian Horton. OFFICIAL SHORTAGE The shortage of officials makes it debatable whether given the choice between an influx of new athletes or officials, we wouldn't opt for the latter at this time. What a pleasure, therefore, to see how well our new Sectional Secretaries have taken to their duties. John Wasbrough writes frequently to all our Vets and has organised a full programme of events. Leo Coy has made an early start to the T & F season and predicts we are in good shape for the first league match. And finally, Ian Horton has headed a small team of helpers which has encouraged a rapid improvement in the strength and fortunes of our colts, boys and youths section. Ian has also devoted his considerable talents to preparing proposals for developing Belgrave Hall which have found unanimous support from your Committee. And so while the load has not decreased for our regular band of officials, we have seen a considerable strengthening of our activities. The future looks bright. items.sum: Obituary of Harry Shields, who died on 25 October 1981 after 50 years' membership, recalling his cross country and race walking career, his administrative roles and his painting.
items.s: In Memorium HARRY SHIELDS Obituary of Harry Shields, who died on 25 October 1981 after 50 years' membership, recalling his cross country and race walking career, his administrative roles and his painting. In Memorium HARRY SHIELDS Following the tragic death of Dave King, Belgrave H. suffered its second great loss in successive months by the passing of Harry Shields early on Sunday morning, 25th October 1981, just seven weeks after completing 50 years membership of the Club. HARRY SHIELDS AT THE 'BANSTEAD' TURN DURING THE 1955 SWC CROYDON AND BACK. Jack Goswell is seen recording. From early days "athletics" and BELGRAVE in particular, and love of the English countryside played a large part in Harry's life. Rising through the ranks eventually to become a member of one of the finest Cross Country teams in the country at that time, winning English National Cross Country team medals and National London-Brighton Relay winning team medals. In the late forties he turned his talents to Race Walking and with the great tenacity for which he was noted, he became a regular stalwart of Belgrave teams in the fifties. He was member of the first Club team which won all the National Championships in one year, so becoming one of the few people, if not the only one, to hold winning team medals for English Cross Country, National Relay and National Race Walking and after a number of London - Brightons, was awarded the Centurion Medal number 235 after the Brighton and Back in 1955. Despite a busy Athletics career Harry assisted in the administration of his sport, serving for many years as Ass. Hon. Sec. to his great pal Alf Harley for the Club. He also held the same position for the South of the Thames Cross Country Assn. of which he was President in 1960/61 and represented this body on the Southern Counties C.C.A. of which he was President in 1957/58. He was also a member of the Southern Counties A.A.A. Committee for many years and also served as an R.W.A. Judge. In late 1968 Harry had a setback in health which took a couple of years to overcome, and after early retirement, and never being an "onlooker" rather a "participant" he turned his main attention to Bowls and Painting, of which his talents were amazing and had to be seen to be believed. In the last couple of years all his paintings in Art School Exhibitions were snapped up, and during his last few months the local "Kent Messenger" requested an interview after seeing some of his paintings in a London Transport Exhibition. So passes a great stalwart of Athletics, many people share with me pleasant memories of strolling days in his company. I remember he was an authority on "Trees" a subject we could always be given a lesson on if we mistook one, which needless to say were numerous. We are all poorer by his passing, but enriched by knowing him and enjoying his company over the years and our sympathy to his wife Betty and his two daughters in their great loss. Jack Goswell HARRY SHIELDS AT THE 'BANSTEAD' TURN DURING THE 1955 SWC CROYDON AND BACK. Jack Goswell is seen recording. items.s: TOM REYNOLDS Obituary of Tom Reynolds, the well-known timekeeper of Surrey W.C. and Surrey A.C., who died in October aged 82. TOM REYNOLDS We regret to record the passing of Tom Reynolds, the well-known timekeeper who died in October at the age of 82. Although not a member of our Club (he was a member of Surrey W.C. and Surrey A.C.) he was one of those people who belong to athletics and his services were at the disposal of many clubs and organisations. Amongst these was our own Club and he was a frequent visitor to the Hall, and as recently as last July he was calling times at our 20 miles Open Run. He was also in contact with many of us through his keen and devoted service to Surrey County A.A.A. for which he worked hard. These last two words sum Tom up very well - whatever he was doing for athletics he worked hard at it. Tom Reynolds Tom Reynolds timekeeper, died October 1981 aged 82; served Surrey County A.A.A. DAVE KING FUND The fund set up as a result of Dave King's death on the Brighton road last September closed at the end of the year. I would, therefore, like to take this opportunity of thanking all those who contributed to the fund. The total reached was just over £600. As planned I purchased a painting of a countryside scene, much loved by Dave, also a tree was planted at Hall Place in Bexley and the remainder given to Estelle. I have been asked by Estelle to pass on to all members of the Club her thanks for all the letters that she had following the accident. In November she gave birth to a son who she has named David and she asked me at what age we took on members. MEMBERSHIP SECRETARY'S SECTION Six months of the year has now passed since taking over this department. Originally it was a task split up into other officers jobs and hopefully now we have one person at the helm we can overcome some of the problems that arose. I would at this point like to thank Frank Webb for the work that he put in over many years as membership secretary. Regretfully, in January of this year, we have had to withdraw over 50 names from the list of members due to them being over 18 months behind. In future I intend to reduce this to those being 6 months behind. At the time of writing over 150 have not paid for this year!! Please remember that to keep the club running efficiently we must know who is where, so if you move please let us know immediately. Also the club does not work on unpaid subs, some members think that it does. Carl Lawton Frank Webb Frank Webb former membership secretary for many years Carl Lawton Carl Lawton membership secretary

items.s: A WORD FROM THE PRESIDENT The President's review of his first six months, covering walking, cross country, young athletes, ladies and track prospects and the shortage of officials. A WORD FROM THE PRESIDENT A busy six months have passed since I was elected President, and whilst I do not wish to repeat in detail results which have appeared in my feeble attempts at Newsletters, or which appear elsewhere in this magazine, I would like to take up just a few lines of the Belgravian. Our Walkers obtained 3rd place in the National 100km, 1st place in Belgrave Open 7-Mile Walk and, in fact, all the London 7s, the Southend 6-Miles and the Met. Police 11km. Carl, their busy Sectional Secretary - as well as Membership Secretary of the Club - and Barbara, his wife, are expecting Lawton - Mark III - in October, sincere congratulations!! On the Country, our Junior Team of Alistair Horton, Stuart Paton, Paul Richley and Mark Waller retained the Junior Team Race in the Surrey Country C.C. Stuart was 4th in the Scottish National and Paul 1st in Surrey Schools. We duly obtained promotion from Surrey League Div.II back to Div.I, but a black Saturday must surely have been the Southern Championships when we finished NO TEAMS AT ALL. Another season of hard work has been done by the Sectional Secretary, Gordon Biscoe. Our boys, colts and youths have made steady progress, under the guidance of Ian Horton, a definite asset to the small management band of Belgrave. He has been assisted by Colin Pearson and Luke Sexton. Our Ladies, to be honest, have enjoyed little success, but with Harry Porter joining in the administration side to help Derek Jones, who has worked single-handed for a long time, we hope for better things in the summer. Looking to the Track we have-on-paper a very good Southern League Mens Team. The question is - "Can we change paper into reality"? Luckily, we only have a limited number of fixtures at Battersea Park. Why do I say this? - Because, despite of numerous appeals, we still look like being very short of officials. Please look at your Fixture Cards and if you can make one or more of the meetings to help in an official capacity - please do so. Besides those mentioned above I would like to thank our Treasurer, Jim Heathfield, and all the other members of committee for their support so far this year and look forward to the same support for the rest of the club year. items.sum: Explanation of how the club president is chosen, with past presidents recommending a candidate to committee for the A.G.M.
items.s: HOW IS THE PRESIDENT CHOSEN Explanation of how the club president is chosen, with past presidents recommending a candidate to committee for the A.G.M. HOW IS THE PRESIDENT CHOSEN It was agreed, some years ago, that a brief explanation of how the Club President is chosen should appear in the Belgravian every few years. Basically the choice of President - as with all other Club Officers - is a matter of decision for the Annual General Meeting, but obviously any member being put up for the most important job in the Club should be well briefed before hand. Firstly - the job. This consists of being present at most of the important fixtures:- Track, Cross-country, Road, Socials on almost each weekend of the year, plus many Wednesdays in the summer, giving a speech at the Club Dinner & Dance and Chairing Club Committee Meetings. Secondly - how to choose the right man or women for the job. It is felt that the past Presidents of the club know more about the job than anyone else, so it is the custom for them to meet in June each year to discuss possible names for President and give a recommendation to committee. If committee approves the past presidents recommendation, the prospective president is approached to obtain his willingness to undertake the job and his name is put forward at the A.G.M. Of course, the choice of President is not a closed shop and members are invited to give any recommendations to the General Secretary or Present President, for discussion at the Past-Presidents Meeting. Derek Crookes (Hon. Gen. Sec.) Derek Crookes Derek Crookes Hon. Gen. Sec.

items.s: grapevine Club gossip column with births, a wedding rumour, Bernard Eglinton's marathon at 68, tributes to Harry Shields and news of Harold King, Tommy Scrimshaw and Paul Whitby. grapevine Congratulations to Val and John Bicourt on the arrival in January of their second son, Graham Stuart. Graham's birth was 8 weeks early - "Just like his dad" says John who still holds the Club record for missing cars, trains and planes. Congratulations also to Liz and Leo Lyons on the safe arrival on March 22nd of their first baby - a daughter, Amanda who weighed in at 6lb 10oz. Can it be true? We hear that Michael Manning has cancelled his filming assignment of the London Marathon on May 9th. Wedding bells on May 8th? Watch this space. Bernard Eglinton has been training hard on the front at Colwyn Bay with the object of the Marathon. At 68 years of age he has an impressive list of runs and long-distance walks to his name and he achieved his objective in a race from Queensferry to Prestatyn in which he finished in 4.45.06. Leading up to this he had runs over 10k. in 55.41 and the Half Marathon in 1.59.14. Tributes to Harry Shields came from two old friends, past President Ernie Duffett, writing from Pontypridd described him as a 100% Belgravian. Alf Taylor (Wellington, Somerset) recalled joining the Club at the same time as Harry and of their Sunday morning strolls along the Thames towing path. Walking Judge, Harold King, remembers his first climbing of the "Hills" at Wimbledon - "they very nearly killed me!" - they obviously didn't as this happened 60 years ago. Once again he made the journey from Erith to officiate at the Open Walk. We missed Tommy Scrimshaw from our opening road races - he invariably comes along to these and to have a chat with old friends. He has been on holiday in Australia and went to Brisbane to see the "mock-up" for the forthcoming Commonwealth Games. Tommy was back home in time to attend the Open Walk. Congratulations also to Paul Whitby who is to be married on May 29th. We are hoping Paul will be able to make our League Meetings after June. items.sum: Charlie Manning's account of the first Belgrave club supper on 23 January 1982, thanking the women who ran the kitchen and Colin Pearson at the bar.
items.s: BELGRAVE SUPPER - NUMBER ONE Charlie Manning's account of the first Belgrave club supper on 23 January 1982, thanking the women who ran the kitchen and Colin Pearson at the bar. BELGRAVE SUPPER - NUMBER ONE 23 January 1982. That was the day of a very special evening which could, and should, become as significant as that day in 1887 when Belgrave Harriers was born. What,you may well ask, has that got to do with "the Club Supper?". Well, it appears to me that the Club Supper showed we have reached maturity. Of course in the past we have had hundreds of social events from Theatre to Fancy Dress, from Bingo to Photographic Competitions, from Jumble Sales to Brighton Relays, from Butlins Weekends to Rambles, from Formal Club Dinners to County and Southern Dinners etc. etc. etc. But, this particular evening was a singular success. It depended on the mixture of old and young, of cantankerous and nieve, of doers and critics. It needed this amalgam which can only come with age. It was just like a family meal, noisy, boisterous, good humoured and comfortable. One felt as easy as at home - and frankly - that was what it was "at home", the Bels, at home. In the kitchen were the Mums - Gwen (Couzens), Mary (Crookes) Maureen (Pritchard) and Misses Ruth (Sinclair) and friend plus Karen (Crookes). We can't ignore what all their husbands did, plus, Colin Pearson at the Bar. I'm bound to have missed someone out, so, sorry - very sorry - and thank you very much and thanks to all of you who made such a night possible. You've taken it to the top of the charts. Its Number One. Please don't alter the formula - make it number one again and it will run as long as Belgrave Harriers. Because that was what it was, Belgrave Harriers, at Home. Charlie Manning. items.s: WALKING Introduction to the walking section reviewing the winter's team wins, the loss of officials Harry Shields, Syd Spencer and Tom Reynolds, the National 100km bronze and the need for under-20 recruits. WALKING It can hardly be said that we have had a bad winter in so far as results go. The weather during December and early January obviously did not help proceedings. Team wins at Chippenham, Luton, Enfield, Wimbledon and Bexley in the Opens and the G.L.C. 10. We only missed out at Corby due to the lack of a 4th man. Fortunately we did not have to rely on the same 4 in the team events with 7 individuals picking up the 'pots'. Unfortunately we seem to be suffering the general trend in walking, that being a reduction in the numbers of competitors and officials. On the officials side we have lost over the last few months Harry Shields and Syd Spencer, and although not a member of the club, Tom Reynolds. They were all long standing members of the walking world who, when their competing days were over, stayed around to put something back. These are people that the club is drastically short of and we need replacements. Having had the situation of starting, timekeeping, competing and recording in a recent race at Wimbledon I cannot stress the need for those that have hung up their boots and come forward and lend a hand even if only occasionally. We did eventually collect National medals last year, in the 100kms. fortunately the classification rules worked in our favour but we were still third. Thanks must go to the members of Belgrave who helped out at the feeding station in the rather deplorable conditions. On to this year, with the prospects of a full team turn out in most Nationals we can look forward to overall better performances than last year. We lost the McSweeney Trophy last year due to the failure of having any under 20 age group teams. To overcome that this year we must somewhere find some new recruits. All suggestions welcome. items.s: OCTOBER 10th 1981 - CHIPPENHAM TO CALNE Gordon Doubleday's report of the Chippenham to Calne walk on 10 October 1981, won by Phil Vesty, with Belgrave taking the C and T Harris Trophy team prize for the seventh consecutive year. OCTOBER 10th 1981 - CHIPPENHAM TO CALNE Run into debt with the Subscription Secretary and you will soon get a reminder and the debt can be paid. Run or walk yourself into an Oxygen debt, and if not soon replenished, you are literally in dead trouble. History has it that this vital substance was discovered at Calne and nowadays every October walkers come puffing in after the six miles slog from Chippenham. This years race, held on the 10th October, attracted the usual good entry and the race got under way in a fine drizzle. This year instead of dashing around to overtake the field I was in a car a few yards ahead of the start and was able to start my watch and the car got away smartly to reach the finish before the competitors had time to lose their breath. A fine win for Phil Vesty (Leic) in the second fastest time ever, followed home by Mike Parker (Brighton). Carl was first home in 6th place and Richard three places down. Fine performances from John Hall and Newnham to close the team in for yet another win of the C and T Harris Trophy. With five more Belgrave finishers the locals saw plenty of Belgrave vests. With no individual awards, Belgrave had to be satisfied with just the team win (our seventh consecutive), but still a good days work for an award any club would be glad to win. A shop window in Calne had a display of photographs of winners of some of the earlier races over this classic course. Amomgst them were the late Harry Churcher (Oct '50), and Stan Vickers ('58), both of these great walkers were not only A.A.A. and R.W.A. champions but were also Olympic and International representatives. Carl himself has notched up a record of five wins and the team ten (out of thirty two). It is good to know that we have such a fine record in the West Country. items.sum: Gordon Doubleday's report and results of the 62nd Belgrave Open 7 miles walk at Wimbledon on 28 November 1981, won by Phil Vesty with Belgrave winning the team race, introduced by a note on Harry Evans, "The Fulham Dentist", after whom the winner's cup is named.
items.s: NOVEMBER 28th 1981 - WIMBLEDON - 62ND BELGRAVE OPEN 7 MILES Gordon Doubleday's report and results of the 62nd Belgrave Open 7 miles walk at Wimbledon on 28 November 1981, won by Phil Vesty with Belgrave winning the team race, introduced by a note on Harry Evans, "The Fulham Dentist", after whom the winner's cup is named. NOVEMBER 28th 1981 - WIMBLEDON - 62ND BELGRAVE OPEN 7 MILES "THE FULHAM DENTIST" This was the nickname given to the late Harry Evans, a past President, and a leading Judge in his day. He was so called because he 'pulled' so many out. His reputation was high and his decisions firm but fair. In 1909 he won the inaugural Garnet 10 miles cup race, with the club team in second place. A baker by trade he would work overnight amongst hot ovens and would then strip off and take on the best. His memory is perpetuated in the Harry Evans Cup awarded to the individual winner of our annual Open 7 miles walk. This years event, the 62nd, was held on 28th November and, once again the weather was kind to us. 98 walkers set off at a signal from our President, Derek Crookes. After one lap of the hills Phil Vesty, Leicester's young star was leading from Dave Jarman of SWC and Adrian James of Enfield. Carl led the rest of the field with our lads battling it out to be in our scoring team. After two laps Richard was coming through, John Hall was giving his usual sound performance with the still improving John Newnham going confidently. That's how it was at the finish except that Richard had caught Carl and they came in together. The scratch team race was ours with Steyning pipping Surrey for second. Mike Scamell was our next man in and took the prize awarded to the first Belgravian not gaining another award. Following in are two faces of the past, double Olympian Eric Hall, beating the hour and Richard Tanner who has been off the scene for a couple of years. No Belgravians featured in the handicap but in the London Business Houses championship in conjunction Messrs. E and J. Hall and John Bromley were 2nd team representing the Civil Service and John Dunsford led home third team for London Transport. Once again we had a good turn out of Bels officials. Joe Coleman was Chief Judge, with Barbara Dunsford, Harold King, Bill True and Joe Wilson assisting. Charlie Jones and Derek Jones on recording and others as pointsmen. Results, of course, by Jack and Joan Goswell whose ability to produce the results so quickly is the envy of many. Behind the tea counter Brian Gorman and his small band of assistants. The biggest cheer of course to Carl, the organiser, who takes these things in his stride. There was of course the Belgrave Timekeeper who had travelled up from the West Country and was calling times with a Balham accent. items.s: MARCH 6th 1982 - BATTERSEA PARK - SOUTHERN AREA 10 MILES Gordon Doubleday's report and results of the Southern Area 10 miles walk at Battersea Park on 6 March 1982, won by Ian McCombie, with Belgrave's first eight competing together for the first time in 18 months and winning the team race. MARCH 6th 1982 - BATTERSEA PARK - SOUTHERN AREA 10 MILES Gordon Doubleday reporting: Making my way to the start of the Southern 10 Miles it was good to see Frank Simmons - although associated with sprinting he is always interested in any event where Belgrave are concerned. An absentee was Harold King who was laid low with illness. After a lap of the Park in the lead was Ian McCombie with Paul Blagg just behind, packing in was Richard Dorman and Carl Lawton and a battle for 4th place between John's Newnham and Hall. McCombie came home winner in a sub 70 minute performance, but Paul, on an off day, slipped to 4th, but with solid packing Belgrave dominated, packing 5 in 12. Meanwhile, Charlie Jones had arrived to join Frank Simmons to watch Belgrave's win. Incidentally, this was the first race for 18 months that all the 1st Eight Belgrave had competed together. items.s: BLAGG LEADS NATIONAL WIN Report and results of the National 10 miles walk at Sheffield on 27 March 1982, where Paul Blagg was third and Belgrave won the team title for the first time in 8 years, with the Inter-Counties held in conjunction. BLAGG LEADS NATIONAL WIN MARCH 27th 1982 - SHEFFIELD - NATIONAL 10M Belgrave took a walking team to Sheffield and won. Basically that summed it up. On an "undulating" 6 lap course the continual changing of road inclines led to no less than 16 disqualifications - none to Belgrave. Paul Blagg proudly wore the colours for 3rd place behind winner Steve Barry and was backed up by Dorman, Lawton and Newnham. We had gone with a chance of medals but to win was something extra - 8 years since the last National 10 Victory but team work paid off. Misfortune struck Mike Scamell who, having caught his shoe and fallen heavily, had to be taken to hospital for treatment. In the Inter Counties in conjunction Surrey dominated, winning for the 1st time since 1965. Consolation to John Hall, who would have been in the winning team even if we had lost a man in front, he picked up a County medal for Sussex. items.label: April 1982
items.sum: Ladies Secretary Derek Jones reviews the women's winter season, training at Wimbledon and Battersea Park, the need for coaches and helpers, and thanks Harry Porter and Joann Warnett.
items.s: WITH THE LADIES Ladies Secretary Derek Jones reviews the women's winter season, training at Wimbledon and Battersea Park, the need for coaches and helpers, and thanks Harry Porter and Joann Warnett. WITH THE LADIES A much better season than in 1980/1981. More people lead by Joann Warnett, our Cross Country Captain, turned up for training at Wimbledon. There was more consistency especially among the Juniors, in turning out for races. The Juniors lead by Gail Porter, who has had a really excellent season, are showing promise and with a bit more encouragement, could do really well in the coming Track season. The weather has been really bad and has lead to a disruption of winter training, especially at Battersea Park on Sunday mornings. The circuit training sessions at the George Shearing Centre in Clapham Junction were disappointing in that they were not well attended and the Hall was not really big enough. The Track athletes at Battersea Park have been suffering from the lack of a suitable coach and it is to be hoped that the attempts to get coaches which are now being made will have some success. Battersea Park looks really empty when no one is there and surely there must be someone who would be willing to help. In conclusion, I would like to thank Harry Porter for all the aid and assistance that he has given me during the winter and to Joann Warnett for her efforts in getting teams to run. Joann may not be the greatest runner there is, but she is always in there trying (very) and setting an example. We now look forward to the coming track season with a certain amount of hope in that we should have a few more Juniors than we had last year. The ladies could still use help and guidance at Battersea Park track on Sunday mornings. I can't believe that in a Club of this size there is no-one who would not be willing to help. It means a lot of hard work and spare time, but immense satisfaction in knowing that a good job has been done. Ladies Secretary Derek Jones Derek Jones Derek Jones Ladies Secretary Joann Warnett Joann Warnett ladies' Cross Country Captain Joann Warnett Joann Gail Porter Gail Porter led the Juniors; really excellent season Harry Porter Harry Porter thanked for aid and assistance during the winter Wimbledon Battersea Park George Shearing Centre Clapham Junction

items.s: SURREY C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS / NOVEMBER 14th 1981 - BROCKWELL PARK - SURREY COUNTY VETS.CROSS COUNTRY CHAMPS. John Wasbrough's report of the Surrey County Veterans Cross Country Championships at Brockwell Park on 14 November 1981, won again by Pat O'Connor, with Belgrave second over-40 team and first over-50 team. SURREY C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS NOVEMBER 14th 1981 - BROCKWELL PARK - SURREY COUNTY VETS.CROSS COUNTRY CHAMPS. Pat O'Connor followed up his win in the first official Surrey Veterans C.C. Championship last year with victory over a field of 100 at Brockwell Park. Belgrave were well represented with 12 runners. Mike Bott (2.29.56) in the London Marathon and John Froud led for the first of the three hilly laps. Then O'Connor hit the front to stay, with Froud always in close persuit. Despite Pat taking the individual title, the team honours went to Herne Hill, with their three scorers crossing the line by seventh position. Anyhow, Pat was well backed up by Frank Barrett (in his first veteran outing) and Lionel Mann for Bels to take second place. Bels 0/50's (Charlie Walker, Charlie Henn and Joe Dooley) withstood Waverley's challenge to take first place. items.h: LETTERS TO THE EDITOR / More on Battersea Park Track
items.sum: Letter from Tom Morrell recalling the cinder track at Battersea Park and the club's Spring Meetings of the 1920s, with entries for the 1927 meeting.
items.s: LETTERS TO THE EDITOR / More on Battersea Park Track Letter from Tom Morrell recalling the cinder track at Battersea Park and the club's Spring Meetings of the 1920s, with entries for the 1927 meeting. LETTERS TO THE EDITOR More on Battersea Park Track Dear Bill, May I congratulate you on the No.203 edition of the Belgravian although most of the names are unknown to me, I read every word, its really a life line to those like me, out in the sticks. I would refer in this respect to the article - Where are they now? by Gordon Doubleday. I well remember running on the three lap track at Battersea, the hundred yard straight started from the first bend, the track of cinders was like a dust bowl after two or three days dry weather. The hundred yards was laned by iron spikes having loops on top through which was threaded white tape, usually 2/3 ft.high. The club always held a Spring Meeting (open and club events) usually on the last Saturday in April, for the meeting held on April 30th 1927, we had the following races and entries - Open Hundred Yards Handicap, entries 83; Club 100 yds Handicap, 28 entries; for the 880 yds. Open Handicap, 116 entries, for a 1-Mile Open Novices, 26 entries; a 300 yd. Open Handicap, 86 entries; 26 entries for a One Mile Club Handicap; 2-Mile Club Handicap Walk, 31 entries; Club Long Jump 4 entries; altogether a total of 400 entries, the programme was priced at three pence (old money). I have the programmes for 1927/8/9. I believe the last such meeting was held in 1929. Of those members named in the pre 1938 list, they were entered into their respective events - K.B. O'Kell, A.E. Duffett, L.L.King, F.R.Webb (Ashcombe A.C.) and myself. My earliest programme is dated August 26th 1926, this is for a Club Handicap Meeting, four events, 89 entries, only three entries from the 1938 list - A.E.Duffett, L.L.King, and myself. Regards to all, Yours sincerely, TOM MORRELL Bill Bill the editor, addressed in the letter Gordon Doubleday Gordon Doubleday wrote 'Where are they now?' in issue 203 K.B. O'Kell K.B. O'Kell entered the 1927 Spring Meeting A.E. Duffett A.E. Duffett entered the 1927 Spring Meeting and the 1926 Club Handicap Meeting A.E. Duffett A.E.Duffett L.L. King L.L.King entered the 1927 Spring Meeting and the 1926 Club Handicap Meeting F.R. Webb F.R.Webb entered the 1927 Spring Meeting Tom Morrell TOM MORRELL ran at Battersea in the 1920s; holds the programmes for 1927-29 Belgrave Spring Meeting Belgrave Club Handicap Meeting Battersea Park Battersea Ashcombe A.C.

items.h: OTHER BATTERSEA PARK TIT-BITS OF THE 20's
items.sum: Recollections of 1920s Belgrave life at Battersea Park: training round the gas holder, big crowds, made-to-measure spikes from Sandy Law and Bill Fish as club factotum.
items.s: OTHER BATTERSEA PARK TIT-BITS OF THE 20's Recollections of 1920s Belgrave life at Battersea Park: training round the gas holder, big crowds, made-to-measure spikes from Sandy Law and Bill Fish as club factotum. OTHER BATTERSEA PARK TIT-BITS OF THE 20's When the track was not available, in the 1920's Belgravians would train round the gas holder, at the Battersea Gas Works, behind the Battersea Dogs Home, on a cinder path. In the 20's and 30's Belgrave always had a large crowd of spectators at all our meetings, practically all round the railings, and two or three deep along the straight. Made to measure spikes were £1.2. 6./£1.13 pence (new money). These were made by Sandy Law of Wimbledon, a shoemaker and member of the club. In the 1920's Bill Fish was general factotem of the club, preparing the track, knocking in the spikes to tape the lanes in the hundred. He would also guard the gate to prevent unauthorised people coming on to the centre of the track. He would also sell programmes. Those better off would have a massage after training, cost 1/- (5p new money). At one time the then new dressing room had three tables. Sandy Law Sandy Law shoemaker of Wimbledon and club member who made made-to-measure spikes Bill Fish Bill Fish general factotum of the club in the 1920s Battersea Park Battersea Gas Works Battersea Dogs Home Wimbledon

items.s: BELGRAVE HALL DEVELOPMENT PLAN Announcement that the committees have agreed to redevelop Belgrave Hall, with Ian Horton's axonometric drawing of the staged plans, a £25,000 cost estimate, an August 1983 target date and a 'one lap' £20,000 fund-raising target. BELGRAVE HALL DEVELOPMENT PLAN The Belgrave Hall Working Party, The Finance Committee and the full Belgrave Committee have all unanimously agreed - WE SHALL PROCEED WITH THE DEVELOPMENT OF BELGRAVE HALL. Ian Horton has prepared the plans summarised in the facing layout drawing. It is proposed to embark as quickly as is financially expedient with the construction of Stages 1 to 3 which will entail the following :- STAGE 1 Will include completing the installation of the first level floor. This will effectively divide the Hall into 2 levels which can be separately used. Access to the first floor will be via a new staircase housed in a new portico the front of the Hall. The upper level clubroom will be available for uses such as lecture hall, recreation room and dining room. It is intended to increase the daytime lettings to generate further revenues. The bar will be re-oriented and the adjacent area enlarged by removing the ladies showers and toilets to the ground floor level at the front of the Hall. STAGE 2 An entrance hall will be created with cloakroom facilities and a multi-purpose gymnasium will be formed by the construction of a dividing wall separating it from the mens changing rooms. The gym will incorporate a multi-purpose weight training facility. The provision of new access doors will allow the changing rooms to be opened for training throughout the day thereby considerably improving the benefit to members. STAGE 3 The scheme will be completed by modifying the mens showers and toilet facilities. THE COST Our best estimates indicate the total cost of Stages 1 - 3 of the scheme will be around £25,000. We hope to obtain a low interest loan of £5,000 and intend to raise £20,000 mainly via our own efforts. Our Committee has assigned £5,000 from reserves and a series of fund raising activities have been planned. THE TIMESCALE With low prices currently available for building projects of this kind early construction is desirable. However it is important not to lose revenues currently generated by lettings and so August represents the best time for building. Funds cannot be raised by August this year and so the earliest practical construction date has been set as August 1983. This is our target date. THE ONE LAP MONEY TARGET £10,000 May 82 £5,000 Start Finish £20,000 Our 'one lap' (400 m) target presents a good visual measure of the state of fund raising. At £50/metre we need one lap or 400m to reach our target of £20,000. So every £50 will move us 1 metre towards the finish. Already we're at the 100 m mark. We ask all our members to help in the fund raising activities which will be announced soon. A master 'lap' card will be on display at Belgrave Hall and any direct contributions will be entered and acknowledged. So why not buy a metre for Belgrave ? Our Treasurer, Jim Heathfield, will be pleased to receive all contributions. items.s: SPOTLIGHT - ERNEST OBENG Spotlight profile of sprinter Ernest Obeng: personal details, coach Malcolm Coomber, best times and progressions at 60m-200m, views on the sport and his weekly training through the year. SPOTLIGHT - ERNEST OBENG Born: April 1956 Height: 1.67m Weight: 65-68 kg Coach: Malcolm Coomber 1977 until present. Career: Completed M.Sc. degree in Agriculture at Reading University 1981 at present unemployed. Other Interests: Carribean influenced music. Athletic Statistics: Most pleasing performance: I'm still waiting. Annual progressions: Athletic dislikes: (a) Drug taking, pill popping, pseudo track and field athletes - (b) Athletes being manipulated by whatever form of authority for ends other than those of athletic fulfilment. Comments and advice: Would like to see more facilities and interest in Athletics particularly all weather undercover area at Battersea Park. Advice to developing athletes: Don't expect results to come easy or quickly. It will take time because you are developing anatomically physiologically and psychologically. So be patient. Also don't take too much advice from others. The sport is such that there are many new and novel ways to try. The problem lies in finding a suitable method you believe in and which works for you. Typical training: (given as kind of session intensity and frequency of session per week). Winter: Weight training - one heavy one light session/w. Jump sessions; hopping and bounding for distance form and strength, 2 sessions/w. Over distance 3 x 300m with ample recovery time in between - 1 session/w. Jogging for time not distance build up to 1½ hours 1 session/w. Mobility session, stretching active and passive various yoga exercises and manipulations - 2 sessions/w. Hill running concentrating on drive phase and spring form. 1 session/w. Harnessed running (drive and technique) 1 session/w. Technique sessions, sprint technique development and endurance at this level 2 sessions/w. Pre-Season: 150 metre runs as many reps as possible, concentrating on technique and form. 1/w. Jump sessions 2 sessions/w. Weight looking for faster movements, 2 sessions/w. Technique form and style adhered to specific areas worked on at speed, 2 sessions/w. mobility sessions 1/w. Season: Weight session - fast and explosive only at beginning of season 1 session/w. Mobility session 1/w. Technique session starts mid-race and race etc. 3 sessions/w. Jumping session explosive 1 session/w. 60m p.b. 6.73s 1978 100m p.b. 10.21s 1980,1981 200m p.b. 20.99s 1979 400m 1 relay leg! 100m 200m 1977 10.74s Not much progress 1978 10.29s 1979 10.31s 1980 10.21s 1981 10.21s The power of Ernest's sprinting is beautifully captured in this photo by Eileen Langsley. items.sum: John Bicourt's coaching article on steeplechasing: hurdling practice, progressive sessions, pacing, water-jump technique, stretching and flat training.
items.s: The Steeplechase John Bicourt's coaching article on steeplechasing: hurdling practice, progressive sessions, pacing, water-jump technique, stretching and flat training. The Steeplechase By John Bicourt Steeplechasing is a specialist event. It is essential but not sufficient to be a good flat runner. The better your technique the nearer to your potential you can run. You should be no more than 12-15 secs off your best 1,500 flat time, over the jumps (26-30 secs for 3k s/C.) If you don't practice hurdling you won't be very good at it. Do it at least twice a week. Once at the end (and beginning too) of a flat session and once as a main session where you try to run sections of the race distance at ideal racing speed. Begin by running short distances many times. As you become accustomed to the effort of clearing hurdles reduce the reps and increase the distance, e.g. 10-20 x 100m over three hurdles at race speed .... 6-12 200m over four same speed ...... 4-8 x 400m five hurdles ..... 3-6 x 600m 5 hurdles on lap ..... 2-4 x 800m ..... 1-3 x 1,000m. Recover same distance run. The aim is to run strongly and within yourself and at a constant pace. ONLY GRADUALLY INCREASE the distance over a period of weeks. Naturally you may want to run an occasional long rep. to help give you the feeling for the race. But there is no point in struggling around a 1,000m if after 400m you are hopelessly tired and your technique is blown! NEVER set off too fast in the 'chase. You will pay for it dearly in the later stages. A steady, even pace, will pay dividends at the finish. More people 'die' in the steeplechase than in any other track event. DO NOT RUN 3,000m S/c if you are a youth or first year junior you will do more harm than good. Practice water jumping only over a full water jump. Start 30m out and run 30m beyond. Be committed, accelerate into it - your increase in speed helps to carry you over the twelve feet - keep low, drive hard off the far side of the bar, leave the driving foot on the bar as long as possible (so you make a big stride in the air) and don't stop for a rest when you land! ONCE YOU CAN COMFORTABLY CLEAR THE WATER JUMP - only one foot should get wet - you can take the jump in your longer reps. Remember when clearing water jump and hurdles to keep your arms in the running action ..... don't throw them up all over the place. PRACTICE, PRACTICE, PRACTICE. Before all track sessions and particularly for hurdling do ten - 15 minutes stretching. You'll be surprised how much it helps you. Do them too at home when ever you can. Good flexibility and mobility are essential to maximum performance. Steeplechasing is a technique event just like any of the jumps or throws. Only the most exceptional flat runners have any kind of success without proper preparation. Assume that you are NOT exceptional. I cannot at this point tell you specifically how to train for the flat, but take note of some basic requirements: Even in season do plenty of steady, easy running // when running flat out have good recovery // at race-pace speeds you can reduce the recovery until you increase the distance. Make all interval/rep training progressive. YOU STRESS THE BODY TO MAKE IT ADAPT TO THE DEMANDS, ONCE IT CAN HANDLE THE DEMANDS YOU MUST INCREASE THE STRESS TO LIFT IT TO A HIGHER LEVEL OF PERFORMANCE// Always follow 'hard' sessions with one or two days easy running. Have a regular, consistant and progressive training programme with a goal in mind ... then work towards it ... good luck. John Bicourt. John Bicourt John Bicourt wrote coaching article on the steeplechase

items.s: COLTS Report on the Belgrave colts' winter: 8th in the Herne Hill League and 4th in the North Surrey League, with individual praise and selected results from Brockwell Park, Wimbledon Common, the club and Surrey championships and Canvey Island, where D. Dyson won and the colts took 4th team prize. COLTS Loyalty and team spirit have been most easily engendered in our increasing number of colts. It is not surprising, therefore, that the best team results and overall individual results have been achieved in this section, when the lads willingness to race has provided the option to compute 4 out of any 8 runners and often fielding two teams. Both leagues found us in the exalted company of talented neighbours, including Mitcham, Walton, Cambridge, Dartford, Elliot etc. All turning out their strongest teams. It was satisfying, therefore that our Colts held their own to finish 8th overall in the Herne Hill League and 4th in the North Surrey League in front of Waverly, Sutton and Cheam, Collingwood and S.L.H.C. While this was down to team performance, one should not diminish the individual efforts of Garry McGurren who finished 7th overall individual in the Surrey League, 16th in Surrey Championship, 1st in Club Championship and 1st in the Points Scheme. Adam Horton with 100% attendance throughout the season always in first 3 scoring places, second in the Club Championship and second in the Points Scheme. Finally, Justin Caines 3rd in the Club Championship and 3rd in the Points Scheme and with another year in the Colts section, he will provide a name to remember. This season we have also had our share of new promising youngsters joining this section, two of whom David Dyson and Dan Steward have already made their mark by contributing to our best result at Canvey Island. Davis and A. Lammas as 3rd. YOUTHS This section has been the least successful in terms of overall team results. A high proportion of races we were unable to choose a team due to the lack of strength in depth referred to earlier. What is more it is unlikely there will not be a dramatic improvement next year as there are no second year boys moving up to plug the gaps. Therefore, we welcome the arrival of John Warren, who will prove an important team member in our push for future club honours. There have been some good individual achievements, Michael Blackmore was 16th in the Surrey Championships, 6th in the Surrey League, Gold in the Club Championships, and in the points scheme, until injury then prevented further progress. Andrew North returned after sickness to make a late season improvement in form with good performances in league races, 2nd in the Club Championships and 1st in the Points Scheme. Simon Pritchard has run consistently to take 3rd place in the points scheme. Alan Lammas producing solid results in a number of the league races and 3rd in the Club Championships. items.sum: Gordon Biscoe's introduction to the senior road and country season, lamenting poor team turnouts despite the Surrey Junior title, and thanking Graham Macky on his return to New Zealand.
items.s: ROAD AND COUNTRY Gordon Biscoe's introduction to the senior road and country season, lamenting poor team turnouts despite the Surrey Junior title, and thanking Graham Macky on his return to New Zealand. ROAD AND COUNTRY It is hard to write enthusiastically over this last season when the sum total of our notable achievements has been winning the Surrey Junior title; second place in the Surrey League Div.II and fifth place in the South of the Thames Junior. Of course it has been good to note the steady improvements of Leo Lyons; Tony Binda; Mick Gleave and Simon Williamson, as well as the exploits of some of our Juniors as recorded elsewhere in these pages, but in the main all these efforts have been in the form of individual achievements. Our problem is still the same one which has plagued us for quite a while - we are just not getting it together as a team on the day, when it matters! While it would be foolish to say we could not do with some 'new blood' in the team, it is not through lack of ability that our performances are so poor, but perhaps a change of mental attitude that is required. Cross country running is still basically a team sport and it is a team that we were successful in in the past and should be able to do so again. When I keep receiving 'phone calls asking "what's on next week" or listening to the reasons why people can't turn out for various races, I tend to wonder just how much forward planning some runners do, or in fact just what is their training all in aid of. It seems ironic that we currently have thousands of people from all walks of life trying to 'run' marathons while a club of our size and reputation can't field more than six runners in the National or in the Bexley Road Relay! In January we lost probably the most talented Senior road and country runner to join us for a considerable while when Graham Macky returned home to New Zealand. Not only did Graham's performances in the 14 months he was with us, have that 'touch of class' but his friendly disposition and uncomplicated approach to the sport made him very popular with all Club members. I'm sure all would join me in saying 'many thanks Graham for your efforts, it was a pleasure to have you with us and can we hope to see you in Belgrave's colours again one day'! items.s: SURREY LEAGUE C.C. DIVISION II Review of Belgrave's Surrey League Division II season, runners-up to S.L.H. and promoted back to Division One after the Waverley fixture was cancelled, with Belgrave positions and team placings from Wimbledon, Richmond Park and Coulsdon and the final 1981-82 table. SURREY LEAGUE C.C. SURREY LEAGUE C.C. DIVISION II Back in Division II after last years relegation, this seasons efforts turned out as anticipated to be a "two horse" race between ourselves and S.L.H. With the competition being reduced to three races instead of the usual four, the race at Waverley being cancelled due to the appalling wintry conditions seriously affecting local road access, S.L.H. beat us on two of the three occasions in spite of good turn out in the first two races as the results below show. However, in being able to turn out a much better team than us in the final fixture any hopes we had of pulling back the points deficit was eradicated and S.L.H. ran out eventual league winners. We have, of course, regained our promotion back into the First Division, but with a little more enthusiasm we could have done it as Div.II Champions rather than as runners up. items.s: NOVEMBER 14th 1981 - BASINGSTOKE - SOUTH OF THAMES (JUNIOR) 5M C.C. Report on the South of Thames junior 5-mile cross-country at Basingstoke, Belgrave's best performance for years with three full teams and the A team 5th. NOVEMBER 14th 1981 - BASINGSTOKE - SOUTH OF THAMES (JUNIOR) 5M C.C. This turned out to be one of those all too few occasions when our achievements met up with our expectations resulting in our best performance for some years, as well as an excellent turn out in general; its quite some time since we fielded three complete teams. On a firm, fast course in autumn sunshine we saw some of our Juniors beginning to put their talents together with some fine running by Stuart Paton and Paul Richley and the way John Gladwin worked his way through the field after a comparatively slow start. Conversely David North following a good start fell victim to stomach cramp and was forced to give ground, otherwise our result could have been better. As it was, on a four to score basis, it was left to one of the 'old chaps'! in the team, Simon Williamson, to close in for us. items.s: DECEMBER 19th 1981 - GUILDFORD - HOGS BACK 11 MILES John Wasbrough's report of the record-entry Hogs Back road race at Guildford on its new 11¼-mile course, won by P. Standing, with Belgrave positions; one Belgrave position is printed as 29 between 270 and 345. DECEMBER 19th 1981 - GUILDFORD - HOGS BACK 11 MILES Hogs Back 11¼ miles at Guildford. A bright, but bitterly cold day fitted between snow falls gave the Hogs Back another record-breaking race. The entries were up to 1830, and the number of finishers 1089. The new 11¼ mile course appears to have met with approval by the majority of competitors - the first section being flatter than that of the previous 10 miles course which compensates for the somewhat steeper climb onto the Hog's Back via Wanborough Hill. Peter Standing, having set the 10 mile course record of 47.39 in 1979 will now start the record list for the new course. items.h: JUNIORS WIN AGAIN - SENIORS DISAPPOINT / JANUARY 2nd 1982 - WIMBLEDON COMMON - SURREY COUNTY C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS
items.sum: Report of the Surrey County cross-country championships hosted by Belgrave on a snowbound Wimbledon Common, where the seniors were 7th and the juniors retained the team title.
items.s: JUNIORS WIN AGAIN - SENIORS DISAPPOINT / JANUARY 2nd 1982 - WIMBLEDON COMMON - SURREY COUNTY C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS Report of the Surrey County cross-country championships hosted by Belgrave on a snowbound Wimbledon Common, where the seniors were 7th and the juniors retained the team title. JUNIORS WIN AGAIN - SENIORS DISAPPOINT JANUARY 2nd 1982 - WIMBLEDON COMMON - SURREY COUNTY C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS With Clive Shippen as the current County President we followed with tradition and acted as hosts for this year's Championship. Coming as they did in the middle of the atrocious weather and with Wimbledon Common under snow and ice, it required several course inspections by the Club President and C.C.Sec. approaching the day to work out various options should some of the proposed routes be impracticable. Fortunately a partial thaw did take place and everything was able to proceed as planned albeit in a mud bath. Special mention should be made of those who helped prepare and mark the course that day, and when you consider that several were out on the common without a break from 10.00 a.m. to nearly 5 p.m. it must raise serious doubts as to the wisdom of holding five Championships (i.e C, B, Y, J and S) on the same day! In the Senior race it was not one of Graham Macky's best performances and although our team packed well in the 50's and 60's its the wrong part of the field to be if you want to win medals, hence we could only finish 7th out of the 12 teams closing in. It was, therefore, left to our Junior team to provide our highlight of the day in a very close finish with Sutton & Cheam. Without John Gladwin and Mark Sinclair or John Searle and with Olly Foote not yet able to score for us it was left to the 'old firm' of Paton, Richley and North to form the spear-head of our scoring four with Alistair Horton rising to the occasion with an excellent run to close our team in. Thanks are also due to Mark Waller who turned out inspite of only just recovering from flu and to Giles Thrush drafted into the team at the last minute. Congratulations then to all the team for a fine effort in retaining the title won last year. Results: Seniors: 1.T.Conlon (HHH) 43.50; 2.C.Hensby (Woking) 44.18; 3.P.Eales (Mit) 44.39. items.s: JANUARY 30th 1982 - SIDCUP - SOUTH OF THAMES CHAMPIONSHIP 7½M South of Thames 7½-mile championship at Sidcup, Graham Macky's last race for Belgrave before returning to New Zealand, in which he finished 8th and Belgrave were 13th team. JANUARY 30th 1982 - SIDCUP - SOUTH OF THAMES CHAMPIONSHIP 7½M This was to be Graham Macky's last appearance for us before returning to his native N.Zealand the following day and on paper it looked as though we might have an outside chance of sending him on his way with some kind of team medal. These early hopes, however rapidly disappeared even before the start with one or two potential scorers not being available on the day. Worse was to follow in the race when after a very fine start Simon Williamson had an off day and rapidly dropped back down the field over the last half of the race, whilst an unfit John Gladwin and Jim Rimmer were unable to come to any solution. The final blow came when David North suffering from stomach problems had to drop cut. It was, therefore, left for Graham to virtually do 'a solo' which he did in fine style improving some fine places on his position last year. It was also good to see Ian Duncan running well again, particularly after having driven down from Scotland the previous night! While Leo Lyons and Tony Binda show positive improvements with each outing. items.h: MARCH 13th 1982 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE 5¾ ROAD RACE CHAMPIONSHIP
items.sum: Report and full result of the Belgrave 5¾-mile road race championship at Wimbledon, won by Oliver Foote from David North and Martyn Head, with the handicap placings.
items.s: MARCH 13th 1982 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE 5¾ ROAD RACE CHAMPIONSHIP Report and full result of the Belgrave 5¾-mile road race championship at Wimbledon, won by Oliver Foote from David North and Martyn Head, with the handicap placings. MARCH 13th 1982 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE 5¾ ROAD RACE CHAMPIONSHIP A pleasant spring afternoon, an average size field turn out for this annual battle with many private duels being fought out. Oliver Foote took his first Club Championship title since joining us with a fine win whilst David North in second place seemed unperturbed by the transistion from the mud of the National C.C. Championships to Road Running in seven days. In third place Martyn Head recorded a fine run having seemingly put behind him some of the many problems that had beset his winter programme. On the subject of problems - David North was not the only one to be beaten by Olly Foote's finishing speed, for Bill Merryman found that having cheered the winner past him at Lauriston Cottage you can't then hope to outsprint him down Lauriston Road in order to be there in time to assist the timekeepers and recorders at the other end. items.s: PATON'S WORLD C.C. CHAMPS - FINE RUN Stuart Paton, after narrowly missing a bronze in the Scottish junior championships, ran for Scotland at the Junior World Cross-Country Championships in Rome and finished 50th. Stuart Paton narrowly missed a bronze in the Scottish Junior C.C. Championships held at Irvine, but qualified for the Scottish World Championship team and travelled to Rome for the highlight (so far) of his short but spectacular athletics career. PATON'S WORLD C.C. CHAMPS - FINE RUN MARCH 21st 1982 - ROME - JUNIOR WORLD C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS Overseas travel suits some people. None less so than our 'English' Scot Stuart Paton. A flat 4 lap 5 mile course was made for Stuart who ran his best race to date finishing in 50th place in this world class field, beating in the process 2 of the England team and 3 of the Scottish team. A measure of his great run was that English Star Jon Richards could only manage 8th in 23.11 while Stuart ran 24.36. Results: 1. items.s: MARCH 6th 1982 - LEEDS - ENGLISH NATIONAL C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS English National cross-country at Leeds, where Belgrave just fielded minimum junior and senior teams, with David North the best junior and John Bicourt, at 36, the leading senior. MARCH 6th 1982 - LEEDS - ENGLISH NATIONAL C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS Following our Southern Championships disaster, there was some speculation as to whether our turn out for the National would show any improvement. Come the day we were at least able to field the bare team minimum of a scoring six in the Senior and four in the Junior events, but a miserable approach to what is supposed to be the premier event and finale of the English C.C. season. With John Gladwin ill and Stuart Paton resting after his magnificent 4th place in the Scottish Junior the previous week, our most pleasing result of the day was David North's placing with Paul Richley making a tremendous run through the field after being left at the start by some 200 yards. Race rusty Mark Sinclair and only just getting fit again Mark Waller ran as well as could be expected to put us in the respectable half of the clubs who closed in a team. In the Senior race it was John Bicourt who at 36, steeple chaser cum road runner who showed he is still by far the best one we have got over the country also. items.s: APRIL 3rd 1982 - BELGRAVE - HAIG 12 STAGE RELAY Report of the Haig-sponsored Belgrave 12-stage relay, won by Shaftesbury Harriers, with Belgrave 17th and the Belgrave stage positions and times. APRIL 3rd 1982 - BELGRAVE - HAIG 12 STAGE RELAY With Haig's generous sponsorship once again and in fine spring weather, we saw another of our successful promotions finally won by Shaftesbury Harriers wresting the title from Aldershot Farnham & Dist. after the lead had changed hands several times during the afternoon. Matching Dave Clarke's fine run for Herc/Wimbledon to record the fastest long stage of the day in 23m 49s was Ian Stewart (Invicta) who equalled Steve Ovetts two year old record for the short stage with 14m 52s. Our team this year was a blend of youth and experience, but while no-one ran badly our overall performance could do no better than to bring us home in the same positions as last year with a slightly slower time. The most pleasing performance for us came from John Gladwin, who after having been plagued with various fitness problems of late returned with some of his old sparkle to record the second fastest time on his stage. In spite of the tremendous organisation that goes on behind the scenes for this race its success finally depends on the runners staying on the right course without any accidents, so once again, to all those Club Members who helped out in any way with the course marshalling etc. a very big thank you! - we hope to see you again next year!
