items.label: April 1983
items.sum: Editorial explaining that the wider-page format has not cut the magazine below 44 pages as club activity grows, and arguing the club must review how it manages its affairs.
items.s: Catch 22 Editorial explaining that the wider-page format has not cut the magazine below 44 pages as club activity grows, and arguing the club must review how it manages its affairs. Catch 22 The introduction of the wider page 'Belgravian' was made with the hope of reducing pages and hence printing costs. By some strange coincidence the change in format occurred at a time when our whole range of activities expanded and try as I might I cannot provide an interesting and factual account of your activities in less than 44 pages. There was a time when your Hon. Editor could look forward to some kind of respite in the winter but what with the increasing interest of members in indoor competition as well as the despatch of teams onto the Continent no longer can the winter season be regarded as our quiet period. So what ? Well there is no doubt that the whole scope of our Club's work has increased and what with the new all weather Track at Battersea as well the planned improvements at Belgrave Hall things are likely to get even more demanding than hitherto. The time is not far away when we will have to review the way we manage our affairs. Anyone who has attended recent Committee meetings at which representatives of all Sections, Sub Committees , Working Parties and so on discuss and control the affairs of the Club will realise that decission making is becoming more and more drawn out as the numbers attending increase. Add to this the fact that as our membership increases so our turnover moves into the small business bracket and you will see that some thought should be given to these matters in the not too distant future. The problem is - who's got the time to sit back and produce a master plan for the future ? CATCH 22!! Battersea Belgrave Hall

items.label: April 1983
items.sum: Club gossip column: the Dormans' marriage, Oliver Foote's relay form, John Bicourt's film career, ex-Surrey AC members Jimmy Green, Walter Batson and George Williams, athletes taking time off to train, Bill Downey's illness and a walking section award.
items.s: grapevine Club gossip column: the Dormans' marriage, Oliver Foote's relay form, John Bicourt's film career, ex-Surrey AC members Jimmy Green, Walter Batson and George Williams, athletes taking time off to train, Bill Downey's illness and a walking section award. grapevine Belated congratulations to Richard and Sonia Dorman on their marriage last June. Richard, who now lives in Nottingham, has made a welcome return to racing and is already well on the way to regaining his top form. Oliver Foote went into hospital at the beginning of March to have his wisdom teeth removed. Four weeks later he was our fastest long leg runner in the Haig-Belgrave relay and by a big margin! We wonder if this technique for shedding weight will catch on. While on the subject of improving racing performances it has not gone unnoticed that John Bicourt has started shaving his legs! We can report that this new development has something to do with John's new career in films and TV. Intrigued? Watch this space! Among ex-Surrey AC members receiving the last copy of the 'Belgravian' was P.W.(Jimmy) Green. No stranger to us for he competed in Belgrave colours during World War 2. Jimmy of course needs no introduction as the man who started Athletics Weekly' after the war. Jimmy is now in his 70's but still trains local athletes. Walter Batson, competitor in the first Barking to Southend Police walk, another former Surrey AC man and now a member of Belgrave is back on the road again after illness. George Williams, a wonderful stylist, former Belgrave walker and International was recently seen in Bournemouth and sent his regards to all his 60's compratriats; Messrs Middleton, Vickers, Hall, etc.., To reach the very top in todays athletics requires not only talent but complete dedication. Both John Gladwin and Stuart Paton have shown their commitment by changing occupations to give themselves more time for training. Mark Sinclair has gone one step further and, following a house move to Dorking is taking a 6 month sabatical to concentrate on his running. We wish all our dedicated young men the very best of good fortune in their endeavours. Another member reaching for the top but in a somewhat different context is Don Anderson. Don has taken 6 weeks leave from his teaching post to undertake a training holiday in Kenya - At an altitude of 12000 Ft. We knew Don was determined to make our Southern League team! Many of our regulars at Belgrave Hall have been asking after Bill Downey. Sadly soon after last years 25 by 1 mile relay Bill contracted a hepatic condition and has only recently resumed training. We wish him a speedy recovery. Following their widespread successes in this years County Champs our Walking Section was presented by the Surrey & South London Newspapers Group wit[illegible] the Victor City Outstanding Sports Achievement Award for February. NOTICES General secretary's notices: an extra Thameside League date on 10 August 1983, a call for officials for the Inter-Counties 20 at the Belgrave 20 on 16 July, and for helpers at the Rank Xerox Marathon finish on 5 June. HON. SECS. NOTICES You will have seen elsewhere in this issue details of the new Thameside League which Belgrave has established at Battersea Park. Unfortunately the fixture card omitted one of the fixture dates so will all officials as well as boys and colts please note the extra date :---SAT. AUGUST 10TH 1983. The Belgrave 20 on 16th July will be the venue for the Inter-Counties 20. In order to ensure that everything goes smoothly may I ask for the maximum support from all officials. Please ring me on [phone number withheld] to offer assistance. While on the subject of officials; We have been asked to provide help to man the finish of the RANK XEROX Marathon which is to be held on the 5th June. A field of around 800 is expected and the finish will be at Richmond Green.The Club is to receive a donation towards our building fund so once again I would ask you to make a special effort to help out. items.s: BELGRAVE HALL DEVELOPMENT Update on the Belgrave Hall Development Fund, now around £14000 of a £27000 target after a £4000 Sports Council grant, with a loan, rising team travel costs and a possible more modest scheme, illustrated by a track-shaped fund chart. BELGRAVE HALL DEVELOPMENT The Belgrave Hall Development Fund has been boosted by a grant of £4000 from The London & South East Region Sports Council. This brings our funds to around £14000 - well short of our target of £27000. Project Manager Ian Horton has also negotiated an interest free loan from the Sports Council totalling another £4000. A loan from the Southern Counties AAA's has also been negotiated but the level of interest is such that it would present too onerous a burden bearing in mind our present income. This state of affairs is less encouraging than we had hoped mainly due to the much higher cost of running our new Teams. Treasurer Jim Heathfield estimates that the travelling costs alone for the 2 Ladies teams, the Men's British & Southern League teams, plus the 2 Youths , Boys & Colts teams will this summer be around £1800 !!!!!So your 'Donations' are even more important In order to keep the momentum going Ian Horton is looking at the possibility of a more modest scheme so that at least we can get the first floor put in this year. It will be touch and go! items.h: In Memorium — MRS E R SAVAGE
items.sum: Obituary of Mrs E. R. Savage, widow of past president Dick Savage, club helper and Vice President, former Selsonia AC member and past president of Surrey County Womens AAA.
items.s: In Memorium — MRS E R SAVAGE Obituary of Mrs E. R. Savage, widow of past president Dick Savage, club helper and Vice President, former Selsonia AC member and past president of Surrey County Womens AAA. In Memorium MRS E R SAVAGE We were saddened late in November to learn from Win Shepherd that her mother had died recently in hospital. Mrs Savage was in her 80's and had not enjoyed good health over the last few years. Nevertheless her interest in the Club never flagged and on a number of occasions during the last few years we were able to welcome her to our meetings. Married to Past President the late Dick Savage she was a great worker for the Club, travelling with and supporting our teams. She was one of a gallant band of ladies who, half a century ago, cut piles of sandwiches and brewed gallons of tea for Belgrave socials which followed Club Championships. A supporter of womens athletics she was a member of Selsonia AC now disbanded and was a Past President of Surrey County Womens AAA. Until the formation of our Ladies Section we were a mens Club but that did not prevent us from honouring her by making her a Vice President for years of service to Belgrave. A number of old friends from Belgrave attended the funeral to say 'Goodbye' to a fine lady. Our sympathies are extended to our other lady Vice President -her daughter Win- and the family. Gordon Doubleday. Mrs E. R. Savage MRS E R SAVAGE died November; club Vice President; widow of past president Dick Savage; past president of Surrey County Womens AAA; former Selsonia AC member MRS E R SAVAGE Mrs Savage Win Shepherd Win Shepherd daughter of Mrs Savage; lady Vice President Win Shepherd Win Dick Savage Dick Savage late past president Gordon Doubleday Gordon Doubleday Club Championships Selsonia AC Surrey County Womens AAA

items.s: W.C.JONES Obituary of Bill Jones, a member for over 30 years and formerly of Ashcombe AC, who died aged 82. W.C.JONES Bill Jones passed away recently at the age of 82. He was a keen member of the Club for over 30 years having previously been a member of Ashcombe AC for whom he raced with considerable success. Bill was of a very quiet nature. Although he was never involved in the running of the Club he was always willing to help out if asked. He won our Yacht 3 handicap when he was over 70 and up to 3 years ago he was running across the common on Saturday afternoons. We extend our sincere condolences to Mrs Jones , to son Dennis and daughter Sheila. Frank Webb. W.C. items.s: TOMMY GREEN CUP Stuart Paton received the Tommy Green Cup for winning the 1982 AAA Under 20 1500m in a club record, ahead of contenders Ernie Obeng, John Gladwin and Carl Lawton. TOMMY GREEN CUP For many, the highlight of our annual Dinner and Dance is the presentation of the Tommy Green Cup to the athlete achieving the most meritorious performance in the preceding year. Seldom has the choice been more difficult. First there was Ernie Obeng's fine 100m victory over Olympic Champ. Alan Wells ; Then there was John Gladwin's new 800m Club record of 1.46.46. Also in contention was Carl Lawton's great win in the 1981 London to Brighton walk. But pride of place went to Stuart Paton for his outstanding performance in winning the 1982 AAA's Under 20 1500m title in a new Club record. items.sum: Report that the annual Dinner and Dance drew about 50 fewer people than usual but the annual draw made £338, with next year's date set for 20 November at the Dog and Fox.
items.s: POOR TURNOUT AT DINNER DANCE Report that the annual Dinner and Dance drew about 50 fewer people than usual but the annual draw made £338, with next year's date set for 20 November at the Dog and Fox. POOR TURNOUT AT DINNER DANCE Some 50 people less than usual turned up for this years Dinner and Dance despite an excellent turnout by our new ex-Surrey AC members. This was a disappointment, not only for your committee, but also for Ron Langheim and his family who always work so hard to make the highlight of our social calender so successful. As usual the evening was a huge success and we hope for greater support this coming November. Particularly important for our fund raising efforts is the Annual Draw which Ron also organises and this year you all managed to sell even more tickets than usual so that despite cash prizes of more than £150 plus 10 other prizes a profit for the Club of £338 was achieved. Our thanks to Ron, his family and everyone else who contributed to a most successful evening. You may care to note now the date of this year's Dinner - Dance. It will be held at the Dog and Fox on Sat. 20th November. Your Committee is looking at ways of making it more attractive to our younger members. So if cost has proved a problem why not start saving a little regularly each week. We'd love to see you there next time!!! Ron Langheim Ron Langheim organises the Dinner and Dance and the Annual Draw Ron Langheim Ron Dinner and Dance Annual Draw Dog and Fox Surrey AC

items.sum: History feature on Tommy Green's 1932 Olympic 50km walk gold and James M.K. Lupton's newspaper letter dismissing race walking as a 'professional shuffle', later answered by Green, Harold Whitlock, Don Thompson and Ray Hall on the London to Brighton course; the original letter is reproduced.
items.s: The Lupton Shuffle History feature on Tommy Green's 1932 Olympic 50km walk gold and James M.K. Lupton's newspaper letter dismissing race walking as a 'professional shuffle', later answered by Green, Harold Whitlock, Don Thompson and Ray Hall on the London to Brighton course; the original letter is reproduced. The Lupton Shuffle At the Los Angeles Olympic Games of 1932 Tommy Green of Great Britain and Belgrave Harriers won the gold medal in the 50km walk. In the closing stages of a hard-fought race he beat the Latvian J. Dalinsch in a time of 4hrs 50mins 10 secs, after being nearly a minute down in third place at the three-quarter distance. Tommy was one of Britain's two gold medallists at that Games (Tommy Hampson was the other at 800metres) and he returned to a hero's welcome. The press hung on his every word. Prior to the 1933 London-Brighton Walk Tommy let it be known that he was out to be the first man to break the 8 hours barrier on the Brighton Road, and the Press got hold of the story. The publicity clearly upset James M.K. Lupton of London Athletic Club who could not resist writing to the Editor of the West London Observer with his views on race walking. He put himself out on a most precarious limb by describing such walking as "professional shuffles" and ridiculing the supposition that anyone could legitimately walk from London to Brighton in under eight hours. Well, Tommy won the race for the fourth time but failed by just 79 seconds to fulfill his target and prove Mr. Lupton wrong. And no one who saw Tommy Green walk competitively would question his mode of action. Two years later Mr. Lupton was made to eat his words by the impeccable stylist Harold Whitlock who clocked 7:53:50 and went on to repeat Tommy Green's achievement by taking the 50km Olympic Gold Medal the following year in Berlin - again one of only two gold medals for Britain. In 1957 the course was lengthened by ¾ mile to 53 miles 129 yards and another Olympic Gold Medallist-to-be, Don "Little Mouse" Thompson, set the sensational record of 7:35:12. If James M.K. Lupton was famous for anything, it was setting himself up to be shot down by three of this country's greatest walkers. Not to be outdone (and to make this story start and end on a Belgrave note) Past-President Ray Hall got in his own shot at Mr. Lupton in 1962 when he set a Stock Exchange record over the "Thompson" course of 7:58:38. C.S. SPORTS CORRESPONDENCE RACE WALKING, OR THE "PROFESSIONAL SHUFFLE." To the Editor, "W.L.O." Sir,—I notice in the Press that Mr. T. W. Green has expressed his determination to walk from the Clock Tower, Westminster, to Brighton Aquarium, a distance of 51 miles, 1607 yards, in eight hours in the Surrey Walking Club's race on September 9th. It makes anyone that knows what really legitimate walking is roar with laughter to think that any human being could cover the London to Brighton distance in eight hours. Fancy anyone walking a mile in six minutes, 22 seconds, the present so-called world's record, and eight miles, 438 yards, in the hour, both impossible feats. This race walking has been going on for a great number of years. It is not walking, but what used to be known in the eighties as the "Professional Shuffle." I have seen most of the so-called champions for the last half century, and I can say that I have never seen any honest walking amongst them. It is not walking, but a mix up between a walk, a run, a trot and a shuffle. It took A. F. H. Newton 5 hours, 53 minutes, 43 seconds on November 13th, 1924, to run the London to Brighton course, which at once makes any one walking the distance in eight hours an absurdity. All the walking records standing on the books to-day are nothing but "Professional Shuffles," and were never accomplished by fair and legitimate walking. It is a very great pity that the International Amateur Federation and the Amateur Athletic Association recognises this mode of progression as legitimate walking, but to those that know anything about walking, it is nothing but a burlesque.—Yours, etc., JAMES M. K. LUPTON. London Athletic Club, SPORTS CORRESPONDENCE — RACE WALKING, OR THE "PROFESSIONAL SHUFFLE." items.s: WALKING Walking section review by Carl Lawton of the 1982-83 winter season with race-by-race reports and results from September to November 1982 (Corby, Wimbledon, Leicester, Chippenham to Calne, Sleaford, Woodford Green, Bexley, Enfield, Battersea Park), with a photo of the start of the Belgrave Open 7. WALKING It has been an encouraging winter season with wins in all but one of the London "Opens" and we "drew" that one, but we lost hold of the Chippenham. Regrettably the Sectional Secretary was sidelined for three months, but he did discover that he was not indispensable. As usual thanks to those who gave assistance for the Belgrave Open 7 and especially those who donated to the prize fund. This year I shall endeavour to boost entries and I shall require more help that last year. In the middle of last summer I was contacted by Paul Warburton as he was interested in taking up walking as he had done a couple of 3kms races. His rise has been quite exceptional and as can be seen from results is now one of the team. Also we have had an assortment of individuals in team results, which bodes well for this year. With Nationals coming round again an all out effort will be required if we are to do well. Last year we slipped up for various reasons, this year things could be different if........... items.label: April 1983
items.sum: Women's section report by Ladies Secretary Derek Jones on the winter's cross country and circuit training, newcomers, the senior squad, Julia McGrath's promise and Gail Porter's three championship wins, thanks to helpers, UK ranking places for Jackie Harman and Lydia Montoute, and hopes of promotion to Division 2.
items.s: WITH THE LADIES Women's section report by Ladies Secretary Derek Jones on the winter's cross country and circuit training, newcomers, the senior squad, Julia McGrath's promise and Gail Porter's three championship wins, thanks to helpers, UK ranking places for Jackie Harman and Lydia Montoute, and hopes of promotion to Division 2. After the Euphoria of the summer season Cross Country Training got off to a very slow start, with only 4 runners turning up on occasions. However, events seem to have snowballed and whatever the weather, normally 12 girls (on one occasion 18) have turned up at Belgrave Hall on Saturday afternoons and Sunday mornings for a run over Wimbledon Common. Some of them positively dislike Cross Country Training but have persisted and have found that the training is keeping them fit. Circuit Training at Heathbrook Centre, due mainly to a late start also began slowly but more girls are coming along for training. We have had a recruitment drive going with some of the local schools and a few useful links have been forged. Some of the schools seem to think that it is a good thing that their children are benefiting from our training. Of the newcomers to Belgrave real promise has been shown in competition and training by Jackie Stone, Anita Davison, Kim Marsh, Julie Godfrey, Trudy Attrell, Sarah Wotherspoon, Sarah King, Sian Davies, Tania Morrison and Andrea Coore. Determination in training too has been shown by Nikki Marsh, Lisa Davison, Rachael Parrott, Christina Gauge, Amanda Grant and Mo O'Connell (until she was injured). Steady progress has been shown by sprinter Jessica Palmer who is one of those who dislikes Cross Country Training but looks better for the training and also competition and probably surprised herself by finishing 7th in the Club Cross Country Championships. Suzanne Jordan and Tracey Johnson have been fairly regular in their training but more determination is required in both traing and competition. Unfortunately, the Senior Squad had been conspicuous by its absence but will be strengthened by the addition of Rosemary Honeychurch and Linda Sparks (regulars at Wimbledon and Heathbrook) Jackie Barclay has been a regular at Heathbrook but since moving house has found the trip to Wimbledon a bit far. Just to prove what a good all round athlete she is Jackie ran in the Surrey Road Relay and was second in the Club Cross Country Championships. Wendy Dunsford has not minded making the long trip from Harrow to train and compete on a number of occasions. Although not a member of Belgrave for reasons which will become clear, 11 year old Julia McGrath has shown really exceptional promise, coming 4th in the Wandsworth Cross Country Championships, 11th in London Inter-Schools Cross Country and 7th in the London Inter-Boroughs. Julia has competed for us but will be moving to Birmingham shortly and we wish her well. Pride of place must go to Gail Porter. Gail is now a triple champion and has shown determination and dedication in training. Her three wins were in the Wandsworth Schools Cross Country Championships (1st in 1981 and 3rd in 1980), the London Inter-Schools Cross Country Championships (7th in 1982) and the Junior Club Cross Country Champion (1st in 1982). All the races were won from the front and in the Wandsworth Schools at Morden Park she smashed the course record and finished well over a minute in front of the second placer. From the beginning of 1983, we have had good attendances at cross country meetings and what with a number of parents showing interest and being prepared to come along in cold weather as well as finding that they have enjoyed each others company, the Belgrave contingent has grown. For instance, at the Mitcham AC/Prestige Meeting at Morden Park at the end of January, the Belgrave party totalled over 40 (compared with 9 in 1982). Also, the junior field in our own Cross Country Championships was the largest we have ever had. Some of the girls who have joined us have been shy and reserved but just by training and competing have gained in confidence and have surprised themselves with their own ability. We now look forward to the summer season with some excitement and believe that with the additions to the squad we had last year, we are quite capable of gaining promotion to Division 2. Just saying "thank you" seems a bit inadequate, but my thanks go to Harry Porter for his efforts in Cross Country Training and also in Circuit Training. Harry leads the Cross Country Pack Runs and is always urging the girls to do better and most have responded. My thanks also to Frank Simmons who although not always enjoying the best of health has been to most Wednesday and Sunday sessions and whose advice has been invaluable. We still need help, however. So instead of sitting at home watching T.V. Saturday afternoons and Sunday mornings why not come along and give a hand?. We need people to help especially at home meetings. Congratulations to 2 Belgrave girls for getting into the U.K. Ranking Lists:- Jackie Harman - 23rd in the U.K. Senior 100m (6th in the Inters). 21st in the U.K. Senior 200m (4th in the Inters). Lydia Montoute - 14th in the U.K. Junior 200m. Congratulations to Gail Porter and Julia McGrath who represented London in the English Schools Cross Country Championships on 26th March . items.s: TRACK AND FIELD Track and field section introduction on the winter's indoor and open-meeting activity and the new Track and Field Committee, with contact details of the 1983 team managers. TRACK AND FIELD Winter is traditionally a quiet period for our track and field members interrupted only by the Boxing Day handicaps. This winter, however, has seen changes with a few of our younger members participating in sub-zero Open Meetings (and producing a spate of personal best's) while Phil Lovell, Colin Gaynor and Stu Paton have taken time out for indoor competition with Phil setting a new Club polevault record and Stu winning the AAA's indoor 1500m Championships thereby earning his first Senior Indoor International Vest against France. A Track and Field Committee has been set up in recognition of the more demanding commitments we face in 1983 due to having teams in Div.5 of the Southern League. It is with pleasure that we note that Stephen Crosbie (1983 General Track and Field Secretary) and Alan Mead (1983 joint Manager of our Southern League team) have returned to back up our Track and Field management team which is a follows:- General Track and Field Secretary: Stephen Crosbie - [phone number withheld] (work), [phone number withheld] (home). items.sum: Explanation that competing in a British League match only rules an athlete out of the next Southern League meeting, not the rest of the season.
items.s: NOTES ON TEAM SELECTION Explanation that competing in a British League match only rules an athlete out of the next Southern League meeting, not the rest of the season. NOTES ON TEAM SELECTION It is sometimes believed that participation in any one of the British League matches will preclude selection from Southern League competition for the rest of the season. This is not the case. If an athlete does compete in a British League match he is only precluded from the next Southern League meeting. Therefore all team members who competed in last September's qualifying match will not be eligable for the first Southern League Match whereas all those who did not compete will be eligible. It is, however, possible for Southern League athletes to compete in a subsequent British League Match without penalty. British League Southern League

items.s: JANUARY 29th 1983 - COSFORD - AAA INDOOR CHAMPIONSHIPS. Report of the AAA Indoor Championships at Cosford, where Stu Paton won the 1500m from Gary Staines (3rd), Colin Gaynor ran in the 60m and Phil Lovell set a club pole vault record of 4.50m. JANUARY 29th 1983 - COSFORD - AAA INDOOR CHAMPIONSHIPS. We were well represented at this year's AAA's Indoor Championships and the video recorders worked overtime as Stu Paton and his training partner/ 2nd claim Belgravian Gary Staines lined up against a good class field in the 1500m which contained 3 visiting Americans. Ian Archibald stretched the field through 800m in 2 minutes. Gary tried to follow and with 400m to go Stu looked to have settled for 3rd. Ever eager to outsprint Gary Stu put in a long surge with such effect that he passed Gary at 300m out and kept the momentum going to turn a 15m deficit on Archibald at the 200m out mark into victory by 2m. Gary held on well for 3rd and only just missed the European qualifying mark. Colin Gaynor showed early season form by running 12th fastest in the 60m while new signing Phil Lovell set a club polevault record with 4.50m to clinch 8th spot . 1500m: 1. S. Paton(Bel.) 3.46.65; 2. items.s: FEBRUARY 12th 1983 - COSFORD - GB v FRANCE - INDOOR INTERNATIONAL. Report of the GB v France indoor international at Cosford, where Stu Paton ran fourth in the 1500m won by Seb Coe and Colin Gaynor was fourth in an invitation 60m. FEBRUARY 12th 1983 - COSFORD - GB v FRANCE - INDOOR INTERNATIONAL. While our remaining juniors were gaining a team bronze in the Southern C.C. Championships, Stu Paton teamed up with Seb Coe in the 1500m against France. 2nd fastest this year on paper Stu was expected to split the French runners. This was not to be. Nerves and a disturbed nights sleep proved too much and Stu could not match a fast 3rd 400m. Seb Coe showed great thoughtfulness in encouraging our man afterwards. No doubt Stu will be even keener to set new records this summer. Also making an appearance in an invitation 200m and resplendant in his Belgrave vest was Colin Gaynor who improved on his seasons best 60m time to finish in 4th place. 1500m: 1. S. items.s: FEBRUARY 23rd 1983 - COSFORD - GB v RUSSIA - INDOOR INTERNATIONAL. Report of the GB v Russia indoor international at Cosford, where Stu Paton and Gary Staines took part in Buckner's UK indoor mile record attempt. FEBRUARY 23rd 1983 - COSFORD - GB v RUSSIA - INDOOR INTERNATIONAL. Still in the middle of their preparations for the National CC Championships Stu Paton and Gary Staines were called on at short notice to participate in the much published mile UK indoor attempt by Buckner. Gary towed the leading Russian through the ½ mile in around 1.56 and soon after eased off the track - his job done. Both Buckner and Stu faded as a result of the early pace but once again the experience was all part of the learning process for our men. One day later both Stu and Gary went down with virus infections. items.s: TRACK AND FIELD RANKINGS 1982 Round-up of Belgravians' places in the 1982 Scottish, UK junior, UK senior and UK women's age-group track and field rankings. TRACK AND FIELD RANKINGS 1982 The Scottish Association of Track Statisticians were the first to publish top rankings for the 1982 season. Belgravians were well placed in many events reflecting our growing strength. Stuart Paton ranked 3rd in the Senior 800m with 1.48.9 and 4th in the Senior 1500m with 3.42.86. He topped the Scottish Junior rankings in both the 800 and 1500. Steve Smullen ranked 15th in the 800m with 1.53.89, 17th in the 1500m with 3.53.2 and 9th in the 1 mile with 4.10.5 (All these performances were achieved prior to the Surrey AC amalgamation on August 31st 1982). Mark Lindsay-Bayley ranked 9th in the 110mH with 15.3, and 13th in the 400mH with 56.9. His 6.50m long jump was good enough for 13th place in the Scottish rankings. In the UK junior mens rankings for 82 Stuart Paton's times ranked him 5th in the 800 and 1st in the 1500. John Gladwin's 48.9 ranked him 20th in the 400, his 1.46.46 putting him top of the 800 Junior rankings. But the most impressive improvement was in the number of Belgravians featuring in the UK Senior mens top 50 Rankings. In the field events new member Phil Lovell's 4.70 was good enough to put him 10th in the pole vault with Mark Shippen's 4.30 being good enough for 30th. Derrick Williams ranked 18th in the long jump with 7.40 and 32nd in the triple jump with his 14.76. David Dawson ranked 49th in the shot with 14.27 and Ken Onagaluchi was equal 20th in the discus with 48.64. Our young ladies too are beginning to make an impression. Jackie Harman's 11.81 100m was good enough for 5th place in the UK Intermediate women's lists (in fact 3 of the faster times were 11.8 windy hand timings, so in our book Jackie was good enough for second). The fast Intermediate 200m was 23.97 and Jackie was not far behind with 24.14 for 4th place. Lydia Montout ranked 14th in the Junior 200m with 25.7. Explains how, after losing the Surrey AC slot in the Ebbisham League, Belgrave (led by Derek Crookes) formed the new Thameside League for colts and boys at the Battersea track. BELGRAVE FORM NEW COLTS AND BOYS LEAGUE. When the Surrey/Belgrave merger took place last year we had hoped to use the Surrey AC slot in the Ebbisham League to provide plenty of competition for our growing band of colts and boys. Mysteriously the Ebbisham League management decided that the Surrey slot should be relinquished. Not to worry we thought,Belgrave had been waiting to join for several years and so the vacancy would come to us anyway. Not on your nelly! We were passed over and so what to do? Well, to cut a short story even shorter, Derek Crookes came up with the idea of forming a new League based on the new all-weather track at Battersea. A quick advert in A.W. and we had a good enough response to get things going. The new League is to be known as the Thameside League- at least for this year. There are even more ambitious plans ahead. Several Clubs have indicated their interest in participating next year particularly if we include girls as well. Now that has the makings of a really good idea. Such a combined competition would create greater team spirit and would eliminate the expense of running separate teams to different venues. The GLC has been approached to see if they will support such a League and their initial response has been very encouraging We ask therefore that all colts and boys take full advantage of the chances offered by this new League and turn out in force for every match! (Also refer to the Hon. Secs. Notices on P.5). Derek Crookes Derek Crookes came up with the idea of the new Thameside League Ebbisham League Thameside League Battersea Surrey AC

items.s: BATTERSEA ALL WEATHER TRACK Progress report on the new all-weather track at Battersea Park, delayed by a Tilbury dock strike and a wet April but still due to open in June. BATTERSEA ALL WEATHER TRACK Those of you who have kept a close watch on the developments at Battersea Park will have seen the excellent start made by the contractors after Christmas aided by a spell of reasonably dry weather. Hopes were high that an early opening might be possible but fate was to take a hand during the latter stages first, as a dock strike at Tilbury held up the top surface and second, as we moved into the wettest April on record. It is to the credit of the contactors that the opening date is still planned for June with a big Ceremony on the 26th Battersea Park Tilbury

EARLY SEASON SUCCESSES No sooner had Steve Williams completed his comprehensive analysis of the existing Belgrave age records than the first results of the new outdoor Track and Field season arrived and almost immediately the records started to tumble.- A really good omen for the important season ahead. In the Senior ranks Phil Lovell pushed his p.b. and our Pole Vault record to 4.75m at a S.Counties,Loughborough Univ.,London Univ.,Civil Service match held at West London on Wed. 27th April. Paul Richley, also at the same meeting, lopped an astonishing 14 sec.s off his 3000m record to reduce our Junior best down to 8.14.5. In the same race Oliver Foote ran a p.b. 8.28.8, only 3 days after winning the Surrey 10000m title. The other early season record was Dick Addison's Youth 400m time of 49.9 set while winning the Surrey title. This eliminated John Gladwin's 50.5 but John was not idle having stretched to an easy 3.56 1500m in his first outing at West London Stadium. items.s: YOUNG ATHLETES Ian Horton's review of the young athletes' winter season 1982-83, with commentary and race-by-race results for the colts (including the Surrey League first division title), boys and youths, and photographs of four young runners by Bill Laws. YOUNG ATHLETES This is the second season of the new management, mars bars and all and the following results show an improvement on overall and individual results far beyond our expectations. Before detailed analysis, I would like to thank all the young athletes for their efforts during the winter, running through often very tough conditions. I would like to thank Duncan, Reg, Ted, Rosemary and Claire for sharing the load, also the increasing band of parents for solving the transport logistics of ferrying indistinguishable boys and mud. I never thought I would attend a race where the support for the Bel-boys outnumbers even the 'host' clubs but it has happened regularly this winter. I am grateful for this and the friendly atmosphere that exits within which the boys have maintained often dramatic improvement while sustaining an obvious enjoyment of the sport. Reports by Ian Horton. COLTS We know if we want to eventually boast strong teams in each age group we must build from the base and therefore perhaps my greatest satisfaction at the completion of this season is to record we have 25 members in the colts section, the majority of whom have been active throughout the winter often fielding 3 teams. We have enjoyed 'many firsts'. We have fielded the first micro colts team and ran the first Belgrave mini colts championship, won by Adrian Ross and Second Russel Isles, both of whom (at the age of 10) have already made significant impact in the U.13 races. Teddy Davies is already an experienced campaigner and two years their junior, even so the age competition must be awarded to Stewart Booth, who at 7 ran a seasoned race at Canvey Island. The colts were the most prominent in striking firsts for the Bels, pride of place going to taking the Surrey League 1st division title, winning convincingly against distinguished clubs, including Herne Hill, Croydon, Ranelagh. The most satisfying aspect being that eight boys contributed to the scoring team, G. Allison, B. Leigh, J. Caines, D. Steward, G. Webb, D. Cunningham, A. Ross and P. Whiston. The first division individual title was won by Ben Leigh. Gareth Allison won the club championships, gained a creditable 8th in the Surrey C.C. Championship and represented Surrey County to finish 41st in the Inter-Counties 'B' race. From this base I am optimistic we can develop strong colts and boys teams next season. COLTS. So we travelled to Bournemouth with growing confidence and again were rewarded with an excellent third team place. Then on November 13th performed superbly in the Sutton & Cheam 4 x 1 mile relays with times of 4.40, 4.57, 4.50, and 4.52 averaging 4.52 miling( The course record previously averaged 5.02). Even so the team finished fourth to Bracknell. At that time we were not to know the ringing prediction in the past BELGRAVIAN (April 1982 P.29) was soon to be realised when injuries prevented this team running again for thr rest of the season. So it was left to John Warren to fly the banner often without support and it is therefore to his credit that he has put together a string of outstanding performances ( including the Club Championship and 1st in the Points League, 5th at Bournemouth, 2nd at Canvey, and 2nd in the Ranelagh Open). It is not surprising therefore that first and second year boys gave their support to maintain the combined Youths/Boys Surrey League position. Good luck to John in the next C.C. season Junior Section where a comparative effort undoubtedly will reap higher rewards. Congratulations also to David Palmer, performing well throughout his first season with the Club, gaining a second in the Club Championships and second in the points table. items.s: AROUND THE SCHOOLS Notes on Belgrave youngsters' school cross country results: Gary McGurran's Southwark and Lambeth win and Schools Inter Counties run, and John Neillis and Michael Bromley in the London Fed. of Boys Clubs and Scott Lidgett school championships. AROUND THE SCHOOLS It is not always easy to keep in touch with the performance of our youngsters in School events. So thanks to those who keep the Editor in touch with these results. Reg. Hopkins Snr. writes to say that Gary McGurran won the Southwark and Lambeth Schools C.C. Champs. at Morden Park. He was also 4th in the South London Schools C.C. Champs. at the Crystal Palace and 42nd in the Schools Inter Counties at Luton where he was the 4th London boy home. John Neillis, who ran for us during the winter with a broken arm was 10th in London Fed. of Boys Clubs C.C. Champs.and was the Scott Lidgett School Champ. items.sum: The road and country captain's review of the 1982/83 season, lamenting poor support in key races and the failure to close a senior team in the National, while praising the juniors' retained Surrey title and individual runners.
items.s: ROAD AND COUNTRY The road and country captain's review of the 1982/83 season, lamenting poor support in key races and the failure to close a senior team in the National, while praising the juniors' retained Surrey title and individual runners. ROAD AND COUNTRY A quick summary of the 1982/83 season would probably read like a typical 'end of term' report- 'Has shown promise but could do better and currently lacks the determination to do really well' Yet once again I am to record that the lack of support in some of the key races has left us with a result that is not only disappointing and frustrating to those who have turned out and tried hard, but shows us in a position that that belies our true potential. This was climaxed by our performance (or rather lack of it) in the National where we failed to complete a senior team. The honours must undoubtedly go to our Juniors for bringing home what creditable results we did have, with a special mention for the marvellous way in which they retained the Surrey title. Again though one is left wondering what might have been achieved in the latter part of the season if they could all have been fit and together at the same time As the results show, for individual honours,congratulations are due to Stu Paton & Paul Richley for a string of top class performances throughout the season. Other noteworthy points include:- - The impact made by our older Juniors and the consistant runs from ; Oliver Foote, Peter Gilbey, Don Anderson & Derek Slann without whom things would have been much worse. - Don Andersons 'run of the season' by starting some 6 minutes behind the S of Thames Senior field and still finishing in the 200's. - David North, still recovering from illness , running himself to a stop in the Southern C.C. - The consistant runs of Simon Williamson & Leo Lyons until injury struck Leo. - The emerging talents of Adam Christie & Mike Nouch and not forgetting Mark Sinclair's first (of many we hope) Club Senior C.C. title. - Vet. International John Thresher flying from Canada to make our 12 stage relay team. John's interest & enthusiasm is a tonic to all who meet him on these visits. Finally my thanks to Bill Laws & Tom Carter for helping out with the transportation of our team on so many occasions GORDON BISC[illegible] Gordon Bisc[illegible] GORDON BISC[illegible] surname cut off at the scan edge after 'BISC' Stu Paton Stu Paton string of top class performances 1982/83 Paul Richley Paul Richley string of top class performances 1982/83 Oliver Foote Oliver Foote older junior Peter Gilbey Peter Gilbey older junior Don Anderson Don Anderson 'run of the season' in South of Thames, starting 6 minutes behind the senior field and finishing in the 200s Don Anderson Don Andersons Derek Slann Derek Slann David North David North ran in Southern C.C. while recovering from illness Simon Williamson Simon Williamson Leo Lyons Leo Lyons injured during season Leo Lyons Leo Adam Christie Adam Christie Mike Nouch Mike Nouch Mark Sinclair Mark Sinclair won first Club Senior C.C. title John Thresher John Thresher veteran international; flew from Canada to run in the 12 stage relay team John Thresher John's Bill Laws Bill Laws helped transport teams Tom Carter Tom Carter helped transport teams National Cross Country Championships Surrey Cross Country Championships South of Thames Cross Country Championships Southern Cross Country Championships Club Championship National 12 Stage Road Relay Canada

items.s: NOVEMBER 13th 1982 - WINDSOR - SOUTH OF THAMES JUNIOR C.C. CHAMPS. Report and Belgrave results from the South of Thames Junior cross country championships at Windsor, where Belgrave were 4th, their highest placing for many years, but missed victory through non-attendance. NOVEMBER 13th 1982 - WINDSOR - SOUTH OF THAMES JUNIOR C.C. CHAMPS. Some first class running from Oliver Foote and Peter Gilbey anchored us for our highest placing for many years, but what a lost opportunity and disappointment for all who were there. Just one more of our non-attendees in the first twenty and victory could have been ours. It is worth noting that all of our current team is eligible for next year's race, so as it too much of a dream to hope we can take it seriously enough to win on what will probably be our own course at Wimbledon. items.h: BOXING DAY 3.2 MILE ROAD HANDICAP ---- FANCY DRESS.
items.sum: Light-hearted report by W.R.L. on the club's first Boxing Day fancy dress 3.2 mile handicap road race at Wimbledon, with the full 47-place result.
items.s: BOXING DAY 3.2 MILE ROAD HANDICAP ---- FANCY DRESS. Light-hearted report by W.R.L. on the club's first Boxing Day fancy dress 3.2 mile handicap road race at Wimbledon, with the full 47-place result. BOXING DAY 3.2 MILE ROAD HANDICAP ---- FANCY DRESS. When the idea of a Boxing Day Fancy Dress Handicap Road Race was first mooted there was little idea of the response it would attract from members. It is still not clear whether it was an excess of Xmas spirit; the desire to dress up; or just a bad bunch of programmes on the tele, but whatever the reason over 60 of our senior and junior members turned up in the most varied collection of costumes. Sigmund Freud would have had a field-day explaining the individual choices . There is little doubt of the terrific effort put in by all concerned. Indeed so good were some of the efforts that the HON. Handicapper could not identify them and Mick Gleaves cousin was heard to ask afterwards why he had not run!! The good people of Wimbledon could not believe it as 'Noddy' Biscoe set the slower entrants on their way. But soon they were joining in the fun and rushing indoors to get cameras to record the strange sights. The times were almost incidental but nonetheless the competitive edge showed as 'Father Christmas'-Paul Richley discarded his sack and 'Fly Me' stewardess John Gladwin threw away his handbag as they hauled in the early starters at sub 5 minute mile pace. Pete Gilbey as 3rd fastest was thought to have pulled a flanker as he was clad only in a nappy and large safety pin. Rubic Cube- Pete Staples got in some usefull resistance training but the Fancy Dress competition was taken apart by the Pritchard family with Simon 'JIMMY' gaining 1st prize, closely followed by big'FAIRY' Brian who again proved he is everyones favourite. Not to be outdone in suspenders and Black stockings(Yes I know this is a family mag. but you should have been there) was 'St. Trinian' - Maureen. The morning was concluded at Belgrave Hall with a hot punch bowl providing a fitting end to a really amusing event. It is rumoured that costumes are already being planned for next year. Me? Well I'm planning something, but on the other hand I might just take my camera along instead. I could make a fortune!!! W.R.L. (W) = Walker ** =Fred Bell. 1. C.Cross 19.27 2. D.Gordon 20.25 3. items.sum: David J. Mote's report on Belgrave's first appearance at the Hermes Club Oostende Wellington Medley Relays on 27 March 1983, finishing sixth of 50 teams, with a course diagram and the leg-by-leg team.
items.s: BELGRAVE CROSSES INTO EUROPE David J. Mote's report on Belgrave's first appearance at the Hermes Club Oostende Wellington Medley Relays on 27 March 1983, finishing sixth of 50 teams, with a course diagram and the leg-by-leg team. BELGRAVE CROSSES INTO EUROPE MARCH 27th 1983 - OSTENDE - WELLINGTON MEDLEY RELAYS. HERMES CLUB OOSTENDE have been organising the Wellington Medley Relays for 27 years and for the last 3 years a team from Surrey AC has crossed the Channel to compete. Hearing of our merger (how news travels) a Belgrave team was invited to compete along with 15 International Clubs to make up a total field of 50 teams. The race comprises of 12 legs ranging from 300 to 1200m. Due to the large number of competitors (600 in our race alone) the venue is a racecourse on the outskirts of Ostende and the race is held in front of the main grandstand to provide good viewing for a maximum capacity crowd and for the TV audience which follows these races with avid interest. The UK teams created much interest and apart from the Bels there were strong contingents from Blackheath and Aldershot. Our race started at 4pm with John Barry contesting the first 800m leg and he brought us in contention in 8th place. Everyone excelled themselves and the excitement rose as John Gladwin moved us into 2nd place on the 6th leg. The remaining runners tried desperately to take us into the lead as the race hotted up. For the spectators it was unbearable as the lead changed hands and after some 20 minutes only 10 seconds seperated the first 8 teams. The final surge saw Blackheath take victory in 20.08.6 with Belgrave 6th in 20.15.4 just one place ahead of Aldershot. It was great to see the team spirit as our top track speedmen lined with our middle distance specialists. We even had a small band of vocal supporters and thanks to the Couzens and Pritchards for their backing. And finally special thanks to Leo Coy and Bob Bridges who respectively managed the team and organised the travel arrangements. This year was an integration year where the team got it's feet under the table. I believe with the potential we have we can go back next year and turn the table over. Why not come and join us?? items.h: APRIL 9th 1983 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE HAIG ROAD RELAY.
items.sum: Gordon Biscoe's report on the Belgrave Haig road relay at Wimbledon on 9 April 1983, where a depleted Belgrave team finished 23rd of 41, with stage times and team results.
items.s: APRIL 9th 1983 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE HAIG ROAD RELAY. Gordon Biscoe's report on the Belgrave Haig road relay at Wimbledon on 9 April 1983, where a depleted Belgrave team finished 23rd of 41, with stage times and team results. APRIL 9th 1983 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE HAIG ROAD RELAY. Up to seven days before the race we had the makings of a good team, one that would surely get us back into the first 9 places & hence qualify for the National 12 Stage Relay again. However once again it proved to be wishful thinking and during the ensueing week no less than 6 team changes and multiple variations to the running order had to be made. Injuries and illness accounted for most of the drop outs but not all, as even a race of this standard does not seem to have the attraction it once did in the days when people would give their back teeth to be in the team! However credit must go to those who still ran although one degree under. The race itself was blessed with fine weather and a record entry and with fine opening runs on long & short legs by Olly Foote and Mark Sinclair it looked as though we would still make it. However it was not to be and we gradually dropped down the field to finish 23rd out of 41 teams some 6 places lower than in 1982 but some 2½ minutes faster! I do not propose to analyse the team performance in great detail but the highlight of the race for us was seeing John Gladwin well and truly back in action on the 6th stage in recording 15m31s, the second fastest on that leg and equal fourth fastest of the day. Finally I would like to record my thanks to all those who helped to literally get the show on the road, from Bill Couzens who let me bully him into organising all the course markers-- once again a loyal band without whom the race just could not continue. To Clive Shippen and his equally able team who hardly ever see the race but who this year excelled themselves with a truly magnificent result sheet. Hope to see you all again next year!!! items.s: APRIL 17th 1983 LONDON MARATHON. Note on Belgrave runners in the 1983 London Marathon, highlighting G. Buchler's 2:23.03 and Simon Williamson's personal best. APRIL 17th 1983 LONDON MARATHON. It takes some time for all the results of the London Marathon to be collated and circulated and as we go to the printers the full lists have yet to be produced. However we know of two stirling performances from Belgravians. New member G.Buchler clocked a highly creditable 2:23.03 in 144th place while Simon Williamson ran a p.b. in 282nd place clocking 2.29.29 to squeeze into our all time top ten rankings for the marathon. G.Buchler G.Buchler new member; 144th, 2:23.03 Simon Williamson Simon Williamson 282nd, 2.29.29, personal best, into the club all-time top ten for the marathon London Marathon London

items.s: SPONSORSHIP Note on Channel 4 televising the English Schools championships and John Gladwin's selection for Peugeot Talbot Athletics Foundation sponsorship. SPONSORSHIP Channel 4 has signed a 3 year contract to televise the English Schools Athletics Championships. This July more than 40 minutes of the events from Plymouth will be televised which no doubt pleases sponsors - The National Dairy Council. Closer to home John Gladwin appeared on television following the announcement that he had been selected for special sponsorship by a panel which included both Brenden Foster and Dave Moorcroft. Eleven young athletes have already been selected for assistance via the Peugeot Talbot Athletics Foundation and a key factor in the choice of athlete has been that of ' high standards of dedication and self-discipline'. Peugeot Talbot plan to spend £25,000 on sponsorship over the next 3 years. items.s: Photo of Philip Goedluck sprinting, with a caption listing his 1984 youth sprint results including the AAA Youths 100m title. Above; Philip Goedluck sprinted his way to some fabulous performances in open competition this summer. He was 3rd in the English Schools Intermediate Boys 100m in 11.0 and won the Southern Youths 100m in 11.25 with a 2nd place in the 200 a week later. Then after coming second in a Youth's Inter County match in 11.2 he hit the best form of his young life to win the AAA's Youths 100m title in 10.77(+3.3w) following a legal p.b. and new Club Age Record of 10.96 in the heats. Philip was also 3rd in the AAA's Youth's 200m in 22.19 - again following a p.b. and Club Youth's Record of 22.14 in the heats. Photo. Bill Laws. items.label: October 1984
items.sum: Editorial on the growing television and sponsorship money in athletics and the need for it to reach clubs, officials and grass-roots support.
items.s: CHANGES AHEAD Editorial on the growing television and sponsorship money in athletics and the need for it to reach clubs, officials and grass-roots support. CHANGES AHEAD While at grass roots level little seems to be changing in the athletics world, at International level the gradual march towards Semi-Professionalism goes on unabated. The money which will come into our sport in the years ahead will pose special problems for Clubs and it is far from clear how it will all end. Take for example the pulling power of Televised events. From 1985 onwards the AAA's and BAAB will receive over a 5 year period monies exceeding £13.5 million from TV and sponsorship deals. Somehow much of this must come through to the Clubs and the AAA's recognise that without the support of Clubs, their officials, organising expertise and not least of all the support of the athletes themselves the whole thing could go badly wrong. The year ahead should see many points resolved and it is important that Belgrave has a view and a say in these important decisions. Whatever the outcome we must realise that our top athletes will be part of a world which we have not seen before. Let us hope that their hard work, dedication and talent will be fairly rewarded. Let us also hope that they will remember their roots and continue to support all those who have supported them in the past and who will continue to support them in the future. AAA's BAAB

items.sum: Grapevine club gossip column: Tom Carter's presidential year, a birth for the Biscoes, John Gladwin's club 1500m record and drug test, members leaving for US universities, Charlie Gillett's music career and other personal news, Andy North and Michael Blackmore, and a new Gleave on the way.
items.s: grapevine Grapevine club gossip column: Tom Carter's presidential year, a birth for the Biscoes, John Gladwin's club 1500m record and drug test, members leaving for US universities, Charlie Gillett's music career and other personal news, Andy North and Michael Blackmore, and a new Gleave on the way. grapevine We were delighted to see President Tom Carter and Ethel at our British League home fixture in August. Ethel is making a rapid recovery following a stroke earlier in the year which required a brief period of hospitalisation. Although Tom must have found his Presidential year very demanding he has not missed any of our important meetings and visited members at Belgrave Hall at least 3 times per week. Getting results and news items from Gordon Biscoe has not always proved the easiest of tasks for your Editor. Not surprising, therefore, that the Belgravian of last April contained no details of a forthcoming happy event for Margaret and Gordon. On August 31st at Epsom District Hospital, Richard Dennis Edward Biscoe weighed in at a healthy 5lb 15oz. Congratulations from your many friends at Belgrave. Stuart Paton's Club 1500m record has been bettered several times this year by Stuart himself, Gary Staines and John Gladwin. When John finally reduced it to 3:39.47 at Meadowbank he also set another Belgrave first. Along with Steve Cram and Alan Wells, John was selected for drug testing. Training at the Belgrave Hall bar proved invaluable as John downed 7 lagers before obliging!! Kevin Sturman and Paul Richley departed our shores mid-summer for life at U.S. Universities. Kevin has returned to South Ilinois while Paul has gone to Iowa State with his sparring partner from Windsor - Andrew Pettigrew. Gordon Doubleday still visits us from Bath whenever possible. Gordon has recently been elected a Life Member of Somer A.C. and in September was re-elected President of "The Centurians" whose membership is confined to those walkers who have covered 100 miles in 24 hours. Our Vet sprints record holder - Charlie Gillett's hidden talents surfaced in a recent edition of The Sunday Telegraph's Colour Supplement. To quote the summary of a revealing 3 page article 'He is one of rock music's unsung heroes; an authoritative writer and broadcaster, a sharp talent spotter (he championed Elvis Costello and Dire Straights). His book, "The sound of the City", published in 1970 and now revised and re-issued, was a classic in a field which then hardly existed.' Funny how conversations with strangers often turn to running. A recent chat with a Leatherhead football club supporter revealed he had shared a bunkroom with Ted Stimpson in the 1940-41 war. 'Taffy' Jones sends his best wishes to Sargent Ted of 345 Heavy Anti Aircraft Battery - Royal Artillery. Taffy remembers "Ted was always dashing off somewhere to race a mile". Honary Coaching member Mike Dunphy and wife Ann are moving house from Welwyn Garden City to High Wycombe. Mike who has coached many of our fine middle distance men will be cutting back on some of his coaching commitments. We wish them happiness in their new house. Simon Williamson indicated to Bob Bridges that he would be unavailable for Southern League duties this summer. On being pressed he revealed that wedding bells in September were the reason. We wish the bride and groom good fortune. Remember those promising Youths -Andy North and Michael Blackmore? We hear that Andy has been invited to Michael's wedding in January but as it clashes with the Surreys we will have to lay on some high speed transport if our top Junior is to make both events. We also hear that there is another little Gleave on the way. Congrats and best wishes to Mum and Dad. items.s: MEMBERS HONOURED Report that the September AGM made Colin Pearson and Brian Gorman life members and elected Ernest Obeng, Harry Porter and Leo Coy Vice Presidents. MEMBERS HONOURED At the September AGM, Colin Pearson and Brian Gorman were voted life members for services to the Club. Colin has been active over the last 10 years or so providing support to Gordon Biscoe in running the Road and Cross Country Section. Brian Gorman is widely known for initiating new members to the joys of training over Wimbledon common. In addition he has looked after teas and sandwiches at Belgrave Hall every Saturday afternoon for many years and lays on a special spread for visiting teams. Truly one of our backroom boys' Unusually too we saw this year the election of 3 Vice Presidents at the AGM; Ernest Obeng for his services to the Club and for many years of International Standard performances, Harry Porter for his enormous work output as part of the small team building up our Ladies Section and Leo Coy who for 10 years has been responsible for compiling the U.K. 5000m, 1000m and 3000m S/C Rankings for NUTS. In addition Leo has been Results Secretary for the Southern League for the last 8 years and as joint team manager has played a major part in the building up of our 'A' track and field side which has gained promotion in each of the last 3 seasons. We are fortunate in having men of this quality taking on greater responsibilities for the future. items.s: DINNER DANCE Report on the oversubscribed club Dinner/Dance at Bourne Hall, Ewell, organised by Bill Couzens and Brian Pritchard. DINNER DANCE A new organising duo, a change of date plus a change of venue provided the backdrop for this years Dinner/Dance. It was with some trepidation therefore, that Bill Couzens and Brian Pritchard awaited the response as tickets went on sale. They need not have worried. By September the 175 places were over-subscribed with a waiting list for cancellations. So why such enthusiasm? Well the venue seemed a big attraction. Bourne Hall in Ewell provides extensive dining and separate dancing facilities in a village setting. Add to that music supplied by the popular 'Jaguars' and with the equally popular Ann and Bernie Ford as principal guests you have the formula for success. Our younger members were well represented and it was perhaps inevitable that our 3 fastest 1500m men would be among the unofficial 'cabaret' provided by the middle distance team. The raffle must surely have lost money (although 'No!' says Bill) as the glittering prizes were topped by non-other than a colour television. The evening proved a great success. Jenny and John Martin travelled all the way from Gloucestershire and Jenny's many Belgrave friends were delighted to see that she is now recovering from a period in hospital. Evelyn and Ted Stimpson were also official guests - a fitting honour in the year when Ted is honoured as President of the Middlesex AAA's. Congratulations then to Bill and Brian. We're already booking tickets for next year! items.s: COLD COMFORT Humorous note on John Rayner's triathlon in Leicester, where competitors changed in the open air after a cold quarry swim. COLD COMFORT John Rayner recently completed a couple of Triathlon's. After the first stage of an event in Leicester - a half mile swim in a deep quarry - all competitors (male and female) discarded their wet costumes together in the open air in preparation for the bike stage. At this point, one lady competitor commented that she didn't think the chaps were up to much. Apparently this was not a reference to their efforts in the swim, but rather to other factors brought about by the cold water! John Rayner John Rayner completed two triathlons Leicester

items.s: JOE COLEMAN - PRESIDENT Profile of new club President Joe Coleman, a member since 1927, walker and Grade 1 judge, with a photo of the Walking Section congratulating him. JOE COLEMAN - PRESIDENT Joe Coleman was elected a member on the 6th October 1927. From early days he was involved in all aspects of the Club and performed with distinction at Track and Field. In the mid thirty's he was scoring in our top Walking teams. He gained a first class standard in the 1938 AAA's Championships and won the coveted 'Fowler Dixon' style award. In 38 and 39 he was 3rd in our Open walk behind Harry Churcher. He achieved National 'fame' in 1939 when he and brother Len deadheated in the RWA National 10 mile Championship, and led Belgrave to a team win. Like many top class athletes his career was interrupted by the 2nd World War but he came back to score again in many of our Walking teams. In 1952 Joe was elected a Vice President of Surrey CAAA for whom he had competed in the Inter County Championships in earlier years. His experience and knowledge was passed on to many young athletes when he became a Grade 1 Judge in the early 1950's. Since then Joe has enhanced the reputation of Belgrave in the Walking World as he has travelled the Country judging top class events. A life time spent with the club and now the holder of its highest Office we can be certain that Belgravians will benefit from his vast experience and knowledge of the athletic world in the year ahead. items.s: From the President New President Joe Coleman's message thanking members for his election and calling for effort to revive the cross-country team and support the Ladies section. From the President Fellow Belgravians, Firstly, let me thank the council of P.P's who sorted me out for nomination and to the members at the A.G.M. who confirmed their nomination of me as the President of Belgrave Harriers for the coming year. I value this office very much, and since joining the Club in 1927 I have had great pleasure in rubbing shoulders with many fine men as athletes, officials and supporters of our club. We have enjoyed many successes, individually and teamwise in both running and walking sections of the club, and whilst the walkers have managed to maintain their winning ways, the X-Country men have not managed to match our pre-war and early post-war achievements not for the lack of endeavour but I do feel that if we made a real effort to harness our resources we could get the Bels singing again. The Track men have had some fine results likewise the younger age groups but Ladies section requires all the help and support we can give. The Roll of Presidents on the board at Belgrave Hall is an impressive one, and I will try to live up to the traditions that these men have set. Here's to the coming year, let us make it one to remember. Good Luck and every success to all members and sections of the Club. Joe Coleman. Joe Coleman Joe Coleman new club President; joined the club in 1927 AGM Belgrave Hall

items.label: October 1984
items.sum: Tribute to W.G. 'Bill' Webb on his 90th birthday, recalling his cross-country running for Belgrave from 1927, with a photo of him holding a decanter.
items.s: W.G. 'BILL' WEBB - 90 YEARS YOUNG Tribute to W.G. 'Bill' Webb on his 90th birthday, recalling his cross-country running for Belgrave from 1927, with a photo of him holding a decanter. W.G. 'BILL' WEBB - 90 YEARS YOUNG On 9 August 1984 Bill Webb celebrated his 90th birthday. As he himself said, "There is nothing particularly meritorious in reaching 90, I just happened to be born with the right genes!" But he was also born with a charm which has endeared him to successive generations of Belgravians. Bill Webb joined Belgrave in 1927, following a period of six years at Polytechnic Harriers and several traumatic wasted years in the first World War. At 33 years of age he was a mature newcomer who made his mark immediately by finishing 8th in the Yacht '3' that year with 15:55 (off 25 secs). In only his second match for Belgrave he closed-in our scoring team just behind first-team regulars Wally Bayliss and Micky Pyer. The Belgravian Scribe was induced to write "The runners have lately been joined by W.G.Webb and A.Robertshaw and I suggest that the presence of these valuable men gives our team a new impetus of enthusiasm." Webb and Robertshaw were just the injection Belgrave needed and they celebrated by gaining bronze team medals in the South of Thames Senior of 1928 - our first medals in the event for 24 years! Bill went on to be our second scorer in the "Southern" and our first man home in the "National" at Leamington. A final flourish in the London-Brighton Relay and he had in one season established himself as a remarkably consistent runner who would always respond to the occasion. Within a year he was elected Captain. Bill Webb's charming disposition concealed a very determined athlete, but it also revealed a willing Belgravian prepared to step into the shoes of W.H.Hare who had done so much to improve our finances. In 1943 he was elected Honorary Treasurer, a post he held for 14 years, the longest on record. His service to the Club was first acknowledged in 1948 when he was elected President for two years. His 90th birthday was the occasion for fellow-Belgravians to make a further acknowledgement. At Belgrave Hall on Saturday 11 August a large gathering of members enjoyed a social evening in the company of Bill Webb who enraptured his audience with a lucid account of those early days. To mark the occasion our President, Tom Carter, presented him with a cut-glass decanter bearing a silver necklace engraved with the good wishes of the Club to which he has remained so loyal. W.G. items.label: October 1984
items.sum: Letter from Bill Webb to the President thanking fellow Belgravians for the gifts and gathering marking his 90th birthday.
items.s: Letter from Bill Webb to the President thanking fellow Belgravians for the gifts and gathering marking his 90th birthday. Dear Mr. President, I am only now recovering from the series of events occasioned by my reaching the age of 90 on the 9th August, 1984. I was overwhelmed with kindness, congratulations and good wishes which helped to make my day a very happy one. None more so than those wishes sent by fellow Belgravians, and the more tangible symbol of those wishes which you so graciously presented to me, on their behalf, at the special social gathering at the Belgrave Hall. It was a memorable and most emotive evening to me, and one which will be inscribed indelibly in my memory. Through you, Mr. President, I should like to express my humble and sincere thanks to all who so kindly and generously contributed to this most wonderful and truly Belgravian gesture. I do not apologise for having reached this specific age. Belgrave is partly responsible. I came to the club at the relative old age of 38, following what had been a traumatic period of my life. The club accepted me, rehabilitated me and made me feel younger and younger. I was proud to play a small part in a wonderful team whose ultimate goal was to win the highest honours in the field of athletics, and to own their own headquarters. They achieved both. I am happy to observe the quality and efficiency of our existing teams, to whom we all owe a debt of gratitude for the continuity of the Belgrave Tradition of "service to the club to the advantage of the whole". They will leave a bright light shining to guide their successors on their way. Bidding continued success to the Club. Sincerely, W.G. (Bill) Webb W.G. 'Bill' Webb W.G. (Bill) Webb reached 90 on 9 August 1984; says he joined the club aged 38 Belgrave Hall

items.s: MEMBERSHIP SECRETARY'S NOTES Membership Secretary's notes on club growth past 700 members and a plea for prompt subscriptions and address changes. MEMBERSHIP SECRETARY'S NOTES The growth of the Club has been quite noticeable during the last few years. Obviously with the influx of marathons we have picked up members on this front, but having done their "one off" retire to oblivion and are eventually deleted from our records. Despite this we have breached the genuine 700 members mark and are now heading to 800. I have, since taking over the job, requested efficiency in sending in subscriptions, change of address etc. but like most clubs, suffer from some who think reminders and requests do not apply to them. With that in mind, I should like every member to consider himself or herself as a link in the chain and not just a pebble on the beach.

items.label: October 1984
items.sum: Report on the club's new committee and sub-committee structure approved at an EGM, and the changes of officers at the September AGM, with profiles of retiring Hon. Gen. Sec. Derek Crookes and his successor Bill Laws, and of retiring Hon. Treasurer Jim Heathfield and his successor Ron Severn.
items.s: OFFICIAL CHANGES Report on the club's new committee and sub-committee structure approved at an EGM, and the changes of officers at the September AGM, with profiles of retiring Hon. Gen. Sec. Derek Crookes and his successor Bill Laws, and of retiring Hon. Treasurer Jim Heathfield and his successor Ron Severn. OFFICIAL CHANGES Structure Our growing membership has resulted in greater activity in all sections and over the last few years it has become increasingly difficult to handle all Club business at monthly Committee meetings. Derek Crookes has been looking at ways of streamlining operations and his master plan was put to an EGM in the summer which approved the new arrangements. From now on the Committee will comprise of all Sectional Secretaries (or nominees) plus the Club's Trustees and 5 members elected at the AGM. Past Presidents may attend in a non-voting capacity and there will be many occasions when their specific past experiences and knowledge will be sought. In parallel with this re-organisation a series of Sub-Committees will be set up based on separate Sectional activities and interests. These groups will be charged with promoting their Sections activities and will produce plans, targets and budgets. It is intended that as our finances move back into a healthier state following the Belgrave Hall re-development programme, each Section will be provided with its own monies following approval by the Committee of individual Section's targets and budget plans. In this way individual Sectional Secretaries and Team Managers will have greater freedom in day to day operations and financial matters. Naturally proper accounting will be required and at the end of each year results will be compared with targets. It will be up to each Section to argue its case and get the funding it needs. We will need to feel our way into these new arrangements. New people are coming into the Management side. There will be difficulties but with our usual tolerance and understanding problems will be quickly ironed out and we can move to a simpler and more effective management system. People Each year at the September AGM we say farewell to the retiring President and welcome the new one. A hearty vote of thanks was given to Tom Carter for all his work during a year of office made particularly difficult by Ethel's illness. The meeting was particularly sad as both Derek Crookes and Jim Heathfield stepped down from office following terms of service spanning a period of time during which Belgrave's fortunes have seen a quite remarkable upturn. HON. GEN. SEC. Derek Crookes took over the post of Hon. Gen.Sec. in September 1978 and played an active and major part in the amalgamation plans. It was mainly Derek's efforts which resulted in the influx of the fine athletes and officials from Surrey A.C. who now play an important part in our expanding activities. During his 6 year period as Hon.Gen.Sec. Derek was elected President in 1981 and the following year served as joint President with Geoff Davis. In his final year of office he took the initiative in proposing and developing the re-organised Management Structure which has now come into operation. His services will not be lost completely as he has taken on the vacant post of Coaching Secretary. We can expect that there will soon be improvements to our Club Coaching arrangements once Derek has turned his full attention to the problems which currently exist. (For further details of Derek refer to the October 81 Belgravian). Bill Laws takes over as Ho.Gen.Sec. on the promise that the new Organisational Structure will make the job less onerous. Bill joined Belgrave in 1952 while at Emanuel School. His membership lapsed when he moved North and he rejoined in 1963. He became a Committee member in 1974 and organised the Dinner/Dance for 5 years. His forte is looking after special projects. He negotiated the Sports Council Grants for the 1976 Hall improvement and the G.L.C. Grants for the latest Hall developments. In 1982 Bill spent quite a lot of time persuading the GLC to invest in putting the all weather track at our home track in Battersea Park. Bill gained a first in Mech. Engineering at Brunel University. He is a Chartered Engineer and is a Fellow of the Institute of Mechanical Engineers and a Fellow of the Institute of Energy. He was Project Manager for Belgrave on the latest Hall Development. In his spare time he has Edited the Belgravian since September 1979 and after producing the last 10 Editions is looking for someone else to ease into the job over the next year or so. HON. TREASURER Jim Heathfield took over the job of Hon. Treasurer in September 1979 and under his careful control funds soon grew to a level which permitted the recent Hall development project to proceed. Whereas most Club Officials perform duties different from their business activities, with Jim Belgrave work was very much an additional burden as he is an Accountant within the Ministry of Defence! With turnover now well into 5 figures keeping all the Accounts and cash flows under control, is practically a full time occupation, and it is much to Jim's credit that he managed to convey an air of complete calm during periods of difficulty. Unlike many Accountants, Jim was always anxious that our hard won savings should be put to work for the Club's future and his wholehearted support for our development projects has been an essential part of the success story. Sadly Jim is 'resting down' due to pressure of work but hopes to become involved again in the not to distant future. We thank him for all his efforts on our behalf. Ron Severn has taken up the mantle of Hon. Treasurer and it would be difficult to find someone better qualified. A lawyer and Accountant by profession he has already made an impact in the short period he has been with Belgrave (see the April 84 Belgravian for a full C.V.!). Ron has been posing the sort of questions about our aims and aspirations which someone fresh to the scene can do. We welcome Ron to his first Belgrave Office and wish him good luck in the year ahead.
