items.sum: Report on the completed redevelopment of Belgrave Hall: the refurbished upstairs club room, remodelled changing rooms and busy new gymnasium, with thanks to the volunteers, the architect and donors to the Appeal Fund.
items.s: BELGRAVE HALL DEVELOPMENT Report on the completed redevelopment of Belgrave Hall: the refurbished upstairs club room, remodelled changing rooms and busy new gymnasium, with thanks to the volunteers, the architect and donors to the Appeal Fund. BELGRAVE HALL DEVELOPMENT Well, its finished! And everyone who visits Belgrave Hall is amazed at the transformation of our Headquarters. Upstairs we have created one of the finest club rooms you could wish to find. With; new windows faithfully repeating the original pattern, a £6000 maple floor lovingly sanded and polished by Harry Porter, new gas fired radiators plus velvet curtains and carpets in club colours, we have a most fitting setting for the Club Honours Boards. Add to this delicate colouring scheme to augment the soft furnishings and it is no wonder that Bill Couzens has been inundated with requests to hire the new facility. Already bookings from Art and Exercise classes are near capacity and our investment is beginning to show the cash returns which the Finance Committee was predicting two years ago. Downstairs the mens changing facilities have been remodelled to give a slightly larger floor area following the removal of the old staircase. The interest in the new Gymnasium has been fantastic. Within three weeks of opening Mike Winch and Judy Oakes reported full capacity with opening on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays from 2 p.m. to 9 p.m. International athletes from as far afield as St. Albans make the trek to Belgrave Hall to obtain the benefit of the new facilities. Many of our members including nine of our British League team now train regularly in the Gymnasium with Mike and we look forward to big improvements in their 1985 performances. Interspersed with the specialist training sessions are strength and fitness classes for ladies and other members of the public. All this is again providing a big boost to our income. Now that the operating patterns are getting sorted out following the inevitable teething problems, we can look forward to a good social calendar and hopefully you will come along and take advantage of your Club's facilities. We are indeed fortunate that a major scheme of this nature can be planned, financed and progressed solely through the voluntary work so freely given by a few of our loyal members. Let us, therefore, through the pages of the Belgravian thank all who gave so much of their time and efforts and in particular; Ian Horton whose original conceptual designs formed the basis for the scheme as it has evolved, Tom Carter who has acted as Clerk of the Works making frequent site visits to check progress, Bill Couzens who has been responsible for specifying and procuring the various services, Bill Laws who was Project Manager and finally Harry Porter who has saved the Club so much money by putting the finishing touches to the Contractor's structural work. We also owe a big debt of thanks to our Architect - David Lawton, R.I.B.A. who fulfilled the targets we set with great dedication and professionalism and at a fee especially reduced as his contribution to this worthwhile project. And finally a big thank you to all those who have contributed to the Development by responding to our Appeal Fund. Over the two years to June 1984 donations totalled £1,496 but were swelled in September following a direct appeal by Past President Charlie Manning which added a further £1,085 to the funds for the Hall development. items.s: 1983/84 ACCOUNTS Summary of the club's 1983/84 annual accounts, with a table showing net income of £10,587 against expenses of £9,709 and a surplus of £878 (the text itself calls £10,587 the year's running expenses). 1983/84 ACCOUNTS At one time our Annual Accounts could be summarised on two sheets of paper. This year it took four sheets including five separate schedules to detail Jim Heathfield's report to the 1984 A.G.M. During the year to July 1st 1984 our total running expenses had reached a record £10,587 while income from subscriptions achieved a record - but far from adequate - £3,417. The shortfall as usual was met from income derived by those hardworking members who freely devote so much of their time to club activities. The only area where there was a reduction in income this year was that of Hall Hire. Revenue from letting reduced to zero during the re-building of Belgrave Hall which started in March 1984. The 1984 Accounts can be summarized as follows:- Leaving a surplus for the year of £878 on the Revenue Account. A most satisfactory achievement considering the cash flow requirements associated with the Hall Development. items.sum: Gordon Doubleday's note on meeting veteran member Edmund Donovan, O.B.E., a Belgravian since before the First World War, on a visit to London from New York.
items.s: Gordon Doubleday's note on meeting veteran member Edmund Donovan, O.B.E., a Belgravian since before the First World War, on a visit to London from New York. Gordon Doubleday recently made a lightning trip from Bath to London to meet Edmund Donovan who is visiting London from the U.S.A. with wife Daye. Gordon writes - "One of our oldest members, Edmund Donovan, O.B.E. was recently over here from New York where he lives. He was a Belgravian before the 1914-18 War, afterwards he went to the U.S.A. Unfortunately an accident to his hip has left him mostly confined to an invalid chair. His interest in the Club is undiminished and he always looks forward to reading the "Belgravian". He was accompanied by his charming wife Daye who originated from Fulham. Edmund is intensely proud of being a Belgravian and sings our praises in the U.S.A. He recalled C.C. runs from the "Spenser Arms" and the "Green Man" from former Club H.Q's and of course, Battersea Park. He sends his regards to all, particularly those who he knows." items.sum: Carl Lawton's review of the walking section's year: a National 10 win and other team placings, Graham Seatter's Leicester Mercury win, British vests for Richard Dorman and Stephen Marshall, and the Ladies Section led by Rachel Parrott.
items.s: WALKING Carl Lawton's review of the walking section's year: a National 10 win and other team placings, Graham Seatter's Leicester Mercury win, British vests for Richard Dorman and Stephen Marshall, and the Ladies Section led by Rachel Parrott. WALKING Casting ones thoughts back to the beginning of the year, we visualised having the strongest distance team for many years. But it did not materialize. We were unable to have our fittest teams out when needed and things did not work out. However, we did have partial success - the win in the National 10 was followed by 2nd in the 20kms and 2nd in the 35kms, but 7th in the 50kms with a team average age of 45 was not something to write home about. Regretably we ended up having to have only John Keown flying the flag for us in the Hastings and the Brighton which I fear is no credit to us by not being able to turn out teams. Maybe next year will be different. Paul Warburton has returned to England after his 12 months in America and he hopefully replaces, in person, if not speed, Graham Seatter who has helped Belgrave to various placings during the year, and not forgetting his win in the Leicester Mercury in 2:26.56. Congratulations to Richard Dorman and Stephen Marshall on gaining British Vests during the year. Regretably Stephen has had his year torn apart due to work commitments. One must not forget that we have a Ladies Section and although not quite as prolific as the men we have been turning out teams and individuals at various events with Rachel Parrott cleaning up all age club records. items.s: TRACK AND FIELD Introduction to the track and field section, noting promotion of the 'A' team to Division 3 of the British Athletics League and the 'B' team to Division 2 of the Southern League, and naming the report writers. TRACK AND FIELD Our track and field management teams seem to be coping well with the burgeoning* activities of our Track and Field activities. You will see from the following reports that on all fronts our Senior Men are setting new high standards and we have seen for the first time promotion of our 'A' team to Division 3 of the GRE sponsored British Athletics League plus the promotion of our 'B' team to Division 2 of the Southern League following an astounding year when they have gained maximum possible match points. The British League and GRE Cup reports have been prepared by joint team managers Leo Coy and Bill Laws, the Southern League reports by joint team managers Bob Bridges and Alan Mead. Add to this the 'Steve Williams' roundup and we think you will find entertaining reading. * This is Stuart Paton's 'Word of the month'!!!! items.s: BRITISH LEAGUE ROUNDUP British Athletics League match 1 at Cleckheaton, where a depleted Belgrave team finished fourth, 13 points behind winners Windsor, with full results. BRITISH LEAGUE ROUNDUP 12th MAY 1984 CLECKHEATON GRE/BAL MATCH 1 The prospect of a 500 mile return trip must have proved unpalatable for 5 of our Team who missed the luxury coach booked for this fixture near Leeds. As it was the decimated team of 18 of our 'A' team men plus Andy Paton drafted in from the large group of supporters only missed winning this first fixture by 13 points, but so close was the match that we finished in 4th place. Windsor who had travelled up the night before, turned out as victors and there is little doubt for future long journeys, we must plan an overnight stay. Pat Lyttle was our only recognised sprinter but having competed for a point in the 'B' hammer, fatigue took its toll and our sprint results were poor. Ken Onuaguluchi, Phil Lovell, Mark Shippen, Aham Amadi and Derrick Williams added respectability to the field events while in the middle distance, Stu Paton won the 400 and John Gladwin got outkicked by a certain Steve Crabb! Andy Paton, Chris Cornwall made their debut in the BAL. Note: Aham beat Derrick in the triple by 14 cms. Read on ..... items.sum: British Athletics League match 2 at Enfield, a wet day of mishaps in which Belgrave finished third, with full results.
items.s: 17th JUNE 1984 ENFIELD GRE/BAL MATCH 2 British Athletics League match 2 at Enfield, a wet day of mishaps in which Belgrave finished third, with full results. 17th JUNE 1984 ENFIELD GRE/BAL MATCH 2 Following our fourth place at Cleckheaton, the Bels. Team had a much better look for Match 2. The day turned out wet and thundery and matched the appearance of the team managers as we had a years quota of disasters in one match. We got off to a flying start with new member Tony Pamah winning the 400m in style and Mark backing up well in the 'B' with 2nd place. Dave Armstrong's blocks slipped in the 100, Phil Lovell fell foul of an over zealous judge and the weather in the pole vault and failed his opening height, and John Aska despite a dash by taxi just missed the hammer. Apart from the disasters this meeting was one of the best that we have been involved in to date - the competition was fierce, especially the 400 and 400 relay with John Gladwin running 49.1 and finishing 5th. In the 400 relay we recorded one of our best times for years and finished last. Our other wins came from Gary (800m), Stu (1500), John (5000 B), Derek and Aham (Triple), Ken (discus and shot) also worth recording was Vince Cornibert, who threw a marvellous 60 metres in the Javelin and Phillip Goedluck who ran a great 200m and short relay. Andrew Rodney, Dave Armstrong, Phillip Goedluck, Tony Pamah, Derek Brown and Snowy Brooks (15 years since his debut in the British League) all made their first appearance. Note: Derrick beat Aham in the triple jump by 2 cms. Read on ..... items.s: 8th July 1984 WINDSOR GRE/BAL MATCH 3 British Athletics League match 3 at Windsor, which Belgrave won with 273 points in probably their best ever team performance, assuring promotion to Division 3; with full results. 8th July 1984 WINDSOR GRE/BAL MATCH 3 After Enfield we were in 3rd spot in the League and if we stayed there then we would be in Division three in 1985. At Windsor we aimed to consolidate this position. As it turned out this was probably the greatest team ever fielded by Belgrave and the best result in any T & F Match in our long history. Colin Gaynor returned to strengthen our sprints despite having problems with his hamstring. This made an enormous difference to our sprints. The remainder of the team were superb. It is worth reading the results in detail. Andrew Rodney, Phillip Goedluck won the 'B' sprints in style - Jeremy Levine gave a boost to the high jump - Vince won the javelin, beating in style those who had been in front of him all season. Jeremy Levine, Steve Smullen and Henry Cooper all made their British League debut. Promotion to Div.3 was assured as a result of this victory, and there remained an outside chance of victory. items.s: 18th AUGUST 1984 BATTERSEA PARK GRE/BAL MATCH 4 British Athletics League match 4, a Belgrave home promotion at Battersea Park, where a weakened team recorded a record 15 event wins but finished second to Windsor; with full results. 18th AUGUST 1984 BATTERSEA PARK GRE/BAL MATCH 4 After our great win at Windsor, the last round match was a Belgrave home promotion at Battersea and what a great day it was - Geoff Davis did an amazing job - we had more officials than in the Coliseum, L.A. The GLC also did us proud with Battersea looking in great shape. Our Team was in great shape too, but with the Nike Classic claiming Stu Paton, John Gladwin and Ernest Obeng and holidays accounting for Ken Onuaguluchi and Vince Cornibert, plus Paul Richley off to the U.S. we were just a bit short of our top men. Nevertheless we recorded 15 wins, our highest ever, but we were pipped by Windsor on the day. Mark Sinclair chased Gary in the 1500 and both recorded good times - Mark ran a P.B. just missing sub 3.50. John Bicourt won the S/C in 9:05.5 a brilliant run for a 38 year old youngster! Neil Phillips won the 'B' discus as did Snowy in the 'B' shot. A great day with the Bels. still on the up - Div. 3 next year! Thanks to all athletes, officials, recorders, groundsmen and helpers for a meeting that was typically Belgrave - just perfect. Neil Phillips made his debut in the BAL team. Note: Aham beat Derrick in the triple jump by 1cm! to make it 3:1 for the series. items.s: For Your Diary. BRITISH LEAGUE FIXTURES FOR 1985 Notice of the 1985 British Athletics League Division 3 fixtures and the GRE Cup semi-final and final dates. For Your Diary. BRITISH LEAGUE FIXTURES FOR 1985 As we go to the printers we learn of the fixtures and venues for the 1985 B.A.L. Div.3 Matches. These dates may seem a long way off but for all our 'A' team men please note in particular the first date - 11th May at Enfield. We know from this summer that we will need to make a better start in Div.3 if we are to have any chance of promotion to Div.2. (* or Battersea Park if Tooting isn't ready) Please note there's a 6 week gap in July/August between matches and hopefully holidays can be fitted in to avoid these important B.A.L. fixtures. The GRE Cup Semi-Finals will be held on Sunday, 4th August with the final on Saturday 31st August/Sunday 1st September at Copthal Stadium. Match 1 Enfield 11th May Match 2 Windsor 1st June Match 3 Brighton 30th June(Sunday) Match 4 * Tooting 10th or 11th Aug. items.s: GRE CUP ROUNDUP Round-up of Belgrave's 1984 GRE Cup campaign, second in the second round at Battersea Park but a disappointing seventh in the semi-final at Copthall, with event-by-event results from both matches. GRE CUP ROUNDUP While our quarter final match at Battersea provided a result which promised well for the semi's, we failed to make the finals finishing a dismal 7th at Copthall following the late withdrawal of several of our top performers. Our throws were depleted with with Kenny 'O' taking a well deserved holiday in Nigeria and Derrick Williams was forced to withdraw from the jumps as a result of being knocked over by a car the day before. The main problem with Cup Matches is that with only one athlete per event it is difficult to get travelling reserves to attend away matches. Consequently when our sprint representative failed to appear for the 200 and sprint relay we were hard pressed to make up the numbers. 28th MAY 1984 BATTERSEA PARK GRE CUP 2ND ROUND 100m 2.A.Rodney 11.2; 200m 3.S.Richards 22.9; 400m 3.G.Sagar 50.4; 800m 4.P.Richley 1:57.0; 1500m 1.P.Ric[illegible]ley 3:55.5; 5000m 5.M.Lake 15:41.4; 10,000m 3.D.Jenkins 33:43.8; 3000m S/C 1.M.Hayes 9:17.2; 110H 1.A.Pamah 15.5; 400H 1.A.Pamah 54.8; DT 1.K.Onuaguluchi 52.68; SP 1.K.Onuaguluchi 14.06; HT 4.H.Cooper 39.10; JT 3.D.Mole 50.64; HJ =3 C.Cornwell 1.75; TJ 6.D.Hollingworth 11.65; PV 1.P.Lovell 4.60; 4x100 2.BELS. 44.3; 4x400 2.BELS 3:26.0. items.label: October 1984
items.sum: Review of Belgrave's 1984 Southern League season, in which the team won every match to gain promotion straight back to Division 2.
items.s: SOUTHERN LEAGUE ROUNDUP Review of Belgrave's 1984 Southern League season, in which the team won every match to gain promotion straight back to Division 2. SOUTHERN LEAGUE ROUNDUP After the disappointing 1983 season when the 'B' team slipped to Division 3 in the Southern League, the Bels came roaring back in 1984 to win every single match and have bounced straight into Division 2. Not only did every match result in victory but the points scores were phenomenal - our highest being a massive 160 out of a possible 180 (which would need a win in every event, 'A' and 'B'). Our average score over the season was as high as we have ever attained in any single Southern League match over the past 15 years. Why the change in our Fortunes? The reason surely is our increasing depth of good performers in virtually all events, and here we must thank Eddie Bojtler for pushing so many athletes in our direction. Now that our 4th, 5th and 6th ranked men can produce 40 metre hammer throws, run sub-23 200 metres etc., it means that even with athletes barred through 'A' team duty in the National League side, or on holiday or injured, we can still turn out an impressive 'B' side. Now it's time to think of 1985. Can we go straight through Division 2 to the Southern League's premier competition? Its possible. And with members now having to prove themselves to get an outing with our 'B' side, perhaps we should start thinking seriously about a 'C' team - if we can find the officials to get it going! Eddie Bojtler Eddie Bojtler thanked for bringing many athletes to the club Southern League

items.s: 26th AUGUST 1984 NORMAN PARK INTER-CLUB Report and results of an inter-club meeting at Norman Park, hosted by Blackheath, against visiting Belgian club Hermes Oostende. 26th AUGUST 1984 NORMAN PARK INTER-CLUB When we sent a 12 man team to Ostend last March we knew that Hermes Oostende would be visiting the U.K. for a Track and Field meeting. Blackheath were hosts this year and at short notice we managed to pull together a respectable team which turned in some good performances. Our new 16 year old sprinter Marcus Adam ran well in his first outing in Belgrave colours, while in the field events new member Tony Featherstone set some markers, which reflected his lack of competition for the last 2 years, and no doubt he will be seeking to annihilate them next year. TRACK AND FIELD ROUNDUP - NON LEAGUE MEETS BY STEVE WILLIAMS Some Early Season Odds and Ends 1 Feb TVH 3000m 1 J Gladwin 8.19.3 25 Apr SCAAA Rep Match TJ D Williams 14.60 DT K Onuaguluchi 50.00 SCAAA 3000m Champs. P Richley 8.20.90 29 Apr Enf 400mh A Pamah 55.2 2 May SCAAA Rep Match 800m 1 J Gladwin 1.48.6 DT K Onuaguluchi 51.14 1500m Gst. M Sinclair 3.51.5 6 May UAU Champs 200m C Gaynor 22.0 9 May BMC 1500m 1 J Gladwin 3.49.0, M Sinclair 3.53.1 16 May Lough v Bor Rd 100/200 E Obeng 10.5/21.4 PV P Lovell 4.60 LJ D Williams 7.01 23 May Civ Serv Rep LJ/TJ D Williams 6.98/14.66 27 May UK Champs 1500m S Paton 3.52.72Ht G Staines 4.00.45Ht SCAAA CHAMPIONSHIPS - C/PALACE - 1/2 JUNE - STUART PATON - 800M CHAMPION There was an excellent turn out for this year's 'Southern' and plenty of good performances with Stuart Paton topping the bill by taking his first Southern Championship in his 'second' event - the 800m. Stuart always looked the danger man in what was a slow race early on as he covered every move of the leader. As they entered the final straight Stu' quickly opened a gap on the rest and comfortably held it to the line for an impressive win. In the field, there were fine silver medals for Phil Lovell, who duplicated his performance of last year, and Ken Onuaguluchi, whose Discus series included 53.80 for a further improvement in our club record. Other pb's came from Mike Hayes- who made virtually all the running to win the 'standards' steeplechase (why he didn't meet the championship 'cut off' is something of a mystery) and from Aham Amadi in the Triple Jump. 400m P Lyttle 51.26ht G Sagar 50.17ht,50.44sf 800m 1 S Paton 1.50.49 1500m 11 G Staines 3.54.61 (3.48.49ht) P Richley 3.49.72ht M Sinclair 3.52.70ht 3000mSc(Standards) 1 M Hayes 9.13.76 400mh A Pamah 55.94ht PV 2 P Lovell 4.60 5= M Shippen 4.20 TJ 9 A Amadi 14.63 DT 2 K Onuaguluchi 53.80. HFC OLYMPIC TRIALS - C/PALACE - 6 JUNE:- Qualifying conditions were certainly tough for our two men-John Gladwin and Phil Lovell-but rightly so with Olympic places at stake. John faced an 800m final 2 1/4 hours after running 1.47.46 in the heats to qualify as a fastest loser- and that after a recent bout of illness. Sadly, he had little left to offer for the final and finished 8th in 1.49.46. Meanwhile,Phil faced an opening height of 4.80 in the vault- only 10cm below his best of last year. He gave it three good shots but made his exit. AAA CHAMPIONSHIPS - C/PALACE - 23/24 JUNE - STUART PATON TAKES 1500M RECORD DOWN A NOTCH 100m- Ernest Obeng had been running into form with 10.47/21.25 for Loughbro' v AAA on 17 June and 10.55 to win an invitation meet in Belfast two days later, but he was below par here and didn't make the final. 11.07ht, 10.80sf. 800m- John Gladwin's heat time of 1.47.51 saw him through to the final as a fastest loser. The next day, John seemed without confidence at the start and he brought up the rear until the final straight when he found a way past Brown and Billy on the inside - but the medals were beyond recall. (1 Cram 1.46.84 6 J Gladwin 1.47.47.) 1500m- In the public eye, this event was notable for Elliott's defeat of the eventual Olympic Champion but for Belgrave supporters, attention was focused on Stuart Paton's attempt to make up for his disappointment of last year when not fully fit. With only 2 to go through from each heat by right, making the final was tough enough but Stu' was well placed throughout and produced the fastest finish to snatch first place on the line from Williamson - it may only have been a heat but nobody was sparing themselves at the end. The time - a new club record of 3.42.69. Of course it all had to be done again the next day and Stu' couldn't get up to the sharp end of a very tactical race. Nevertheless he recorded another 3.42 - and no doubt gained a lot from the experience. ( 1 Elliott 3.39.66 2 Coe 3.39.79 10 S Paton 3.42.98.) Pole Vault- Phil Lovell seemed stuck on 4.60 upto this stage of the season and that was again the height he achieved here in 7th place. Nevertheless a fine placing in a national championship. Discus- Ken Onuaguluchi was seen lofting out his warm up throws a long way but he couldn't catch a really big one in the competition. His best was a solid 52.58 and put him also in 7th place. --------------------- Paul Richley made a long trip up to Stretford worthwhile on 26 June by running an excellent 3.48.7 in a BMC 1500m while Gary Staines took his 800m pb down to 1.50.0 in a BMC race at West London on 4 July. INTER COUNTIES CHAMPIONSHIPS - BIRMINGHAM - 1 JULY - THREE CHAMPIONS More Belgravians than ever before found their way to these championships as County selections. Titles were taken by Ernie Obeng(Sy)100m in 10.25w, a CBP and Ernie's 5th win in 7 years - a magnificent record; by Gary Staines(Herts)- the Mile in 4.09.53 - and Phil Lovell, finding some improved form (4.75) in the Pole Vault. Good points were also earned by Tony Pamah(Kent) 4th in the 400mh in 55.4 and Ken Onuaguluchi(Sy) 2nd in the Discus with 52.16. After a 4.11.15 heat in the mile, Stu' Paton dropped to 4.16.90 in the final for 9th place. LAURISTON MILE - BATTERSEA PARK - 4 JULY:- This annual event saw three Bels way ahead of the field. Mark Sinclair took the lead straight away aiming for a fast run and John Warren made every use of the pace on Mark's shoulder. John had to let Mark go just before the bell as Mark kicked on to win in a useful 4.13.6 but John was rewarded with a pb of 4.18.7 in 2nd. Dave North completed the trio with 4.21.4. ENGLAND v SPAIN v SWEDEN - GATESHEAD 6 JULY - JOHN (AND GARY) TAKE STUART'S RECORD John Gladwin won further International selection for England over 1500m in this match and Gary Staines received a late invitation to run as a guest following his Inter-Counties win. So there was special interest as these two clashed for the first time. As usual, Gary got stuck in with the leaders straight away with John tucked in behind. In the final sprint, John squeezed past Gary but four others were just ahead in a blanket finish. Both men dipped under Stu's recent mark and the middle distance record spree was truly underway.(1 Theriot 3.41.28 2 Hutchings 3.41.33 5 J Gladwin 3.41.45 6 G Staines 3.41.76).Ernie Obeng ran as a guest in the 100m placing 2nd to McFarlane in 10.5. PEUGEOT/TALBOT GAMES - C/PALACE - 13 JULY - 1000m RECORD:- John Gladwin took our club record for 1000m down to 2.19.14 although not helped by some uneven pacemaking, while Stu' Paton was also inside the previous best - which he held - with 2.21.37. Ernie Obeng was ahead of a former World record holder (Williams) and a former Olympic champion (Crawford) as he took 3rd place in the 100m in 10.69. EDINBURGH GAMES - MEADOWBANK - 17 JULY - JOHN GOES UNDER 3.40 WITH STUART JUST BEHIND Four days after their meeting in London, John and Stuart were brought together again for an invitation 1500m on Stu's 'home' track and both men again earned pb's - a couple of classy times (shown at the top of the All Time list) and forward placings in a large field behind the World Record holder who won in 3.36.90. Both men finished well and will go faster when hanging on further up the front of one of these pace made races. Ernest Obeng was 3rd behind Wells and Krulee in the 100m in 10.46. ----------------- 1 Aug SCAAA Rep Match, C/Pal - 3000mSc 5 J Bicourt 9.06.4 PV 1 P Lovell 4.75 NIKE CLASSIC - C/PALACE - 18 AUGUST - There were two more quality performances from the Gladwin-Paton duo at this post Olympic Invitation meeting. John missed his and our 800 best by 2/100ths with 1.46.48 while Stuart nearly repossessed the 1000 record with 2.19.36. items.h: GARY EQUALS 1 MILE RECORD WHILE JOHN GOES ROUND THE WORLD
items.sum: Notes on Gary Staines equalling the club mile record at West London Stadium and running well in a gale at Jarrow, and John Gladwin winning an international 1500m in Taipei.
items.s: GARY EQUALS 1 MILE RECORD WHILE JOHN GOES ROUND THE WORLD Notes on Gary Staines equalling the club mile record at West London Stadium and running well in a gale at Jarrow, and John Gladwin winning an international 1500m in Taipei. GARY EQUALS 1 MILE RECORD WHILE JOHN GOES ROUND THE WORLD GARY STAINES equalled the club mile record at West London Stadium on 5 September when winning the Open Graded 'A' race in 4.02.1 on one of the first cold evenings of the late Summer. But those weather conditions were nothing compared to the gale force winds he had to contend with four days later at a meeting to open the new Jarrow track. That Gary should run 4.03.67 was therefore an exceptional effort. Cram and Walker were less than 6, and 5, seconds ahead, respectively and if you reckon on them being worth 3.49/3.50 normally , it shows the true merit of Gary's run. ------------ Members of this club have competed in many parts of the World but new ground must have been broken by John Gladwin when he won an International 1500m in Taipei in September in 3.52.25 and took second place in the 800 in 1.48.92. So if you get offered a job lot of training shoes - made in Taiwan - you'll know where they came from! items.h: ERNEST OBENG'S LATE SEASON UPS AND DOWNS
items.sum: Account of Ernest Obeng's 1984 season, including his expulsion from the Los Angeles Olympics by Ghanaian officials and his late-season return to form, with a photograph from the Peugeot Games.
items.s: ERNEST OBENG'S LATE SEASON UPS AND DOWNS Account of Ernest Obeng's 1984 season, including his expulsion from the Los Angeles Olympics by Ghanaian officials and his late-season return to form, with a photograph from the Peugeot Games. ERNEST OBENG'S LATE SEASON UPS AND DOWNS 1984 was a year of mixed fortune for our leading sprinter. He struggled to find his best form early on but it was Olympic year and, having missed out on Moscow, Ernie was encouraged enough to pay his own way to LA for probably his last chance to compete in the great event. Well no doubt you know the story of Ernie's expulsion from the Games by Ghanaian officials in what seems an incredible case of victimisation. It was obviously a great disappointment to him not to be able to compete and the character assassination that went with the affair added insult to injury. It was perhaps some small consolation to Ernie that he should hit some of his best ever form in August - as if to show that he would have performed with great credit to his country in LA. For following a couple of ordinary clockings at the Nike Classic and in Budapest when still coping with jet lag, he flew to a 10.25 timing (his 3rd fastest legal mark) in Zurich on 22 August, only headed by Olympic Bronze Medallist Ben Johnson and Osvaldo Lara - winner of the Eastern Block 'Friendship' Games. Then in Rieti,Italy on 2 September he recorded 10.32 (+0.7) behind Penalver and Lara. At the IAC/Coca-Cola meeting on 7 September, Ernie gave us at home the first glimpse of this return to form. He snapped away from the blocks to win his heat easing up in 10.45 into a slight headwind - but what a pity the start of the final was such a shambles with McFarlane getting a clear flyer and the race not being recalled by the starter. Although Lara's pick-up enabled him to win, Ernie,at a disadvantage with his own fast start pre-empted, couldn't quite make up the deficit and he finished 3rd in 10.38. Ernest Obeng's Belgrave Honours badge well to the fore in the Peugeot Games held at the Crystal Palace on July 13th, - probably the last occasion he will wear Ghana's colours as he has vowed not to compete again for the Country which treated him so shabbily in Los Angeles Olympics. Wells won in 10.46. Press Association Photo. items.sum: Bill Laws' report on the 1984 Nike 25 x 1 mile relay at Crystal Palace, where Belgrave's A team finished second nationally to Sale, with the leg times of all four Belgrave teams.
items.s: Nike Blackheath H~ 25 x 1mile Bill Laws' report on the 1984 Nike 25 x 1 mile relay at Crystal Palace, where Belgrave's A team finished second nationally to Sale, with the leg times of all four Belgrave teams. Nike Blackheath H~ 25 x 1mile 29th SEPTEMBER 1984 CRYSTAL PALACE NIKE 25x1 MILE RELAY Last year's first ever win in this Nationwide event led us to hope that with a better team (on paper) we could repeat our success. Sale running at Manchester had other ideas and as our 'A' team turned in times just marginally slower than we had anticipated Sale improved on their efforts of last year. We ran as usual at the Crystal Palace venue while 80 or so teams competed at 8 other venues. The race was close right up to the 18 mile mark when Pat Chester running for TVH ran a 4.08 effort to snatch the lead from the Bels. Nigel Clarke got a bit carried away on the next leg as the excitement built and ran his first 400 in 57.7! It was left to Peter Gilbey to take us into a lead which increased to 3 minutes over TVH over the next 5 miles. Everyone had been blaming the cold windy conditions for the 'slow' times, but either they were wrong or Gary Staines' 4.06 on the last leg was really something special. Running at even pace Gary finished in great style and even had to contend with being baulked by 2 Croydon runners who ran right in front of him as they changed the baton at the 2 lap mark. Several of our 'A' team men had just returned from holidays and it showed in their times. Our youngsters though ran superbly with Youths John Booth and Glyn Tiernan performing well as did Junior Richard O'Hara who is beginning to look a class runner. In the 'B' team Francis Ward, who has returned from 2 years in the U.S.A. proved fastest with Andy Moore close behind. Our 'D' team comprised young members having an average age of 13 years and their general high level of performance promises well for the future. Our thanks to Bill Couzens, Brian Pritchard and Derek Jones plus their families who put up with the trying conditions while organising and recording through the morning and afternoon sessions. Jim and Dave Mote organised the Young Athletes and yours truly the 'A'. Bill Laws Result: 1.Sale H 1:53.42; 2.BELGRAVE (A) 1:54.19; 3.Aldershot F & D 1:56.41; 4.T.V.H. 1:56.46; 5.S.L.H. 1:58.38. items.s: ROSENHEIM LEAGUE Review of Belgrave's 1984 Rosenheim League season, with seniors and Youths results from four matches and the Youths' second place in the final behind Herne Hill. ROSENHEIM LEAGUE (Non-scoring performances in brackets) The Rosenheim League again provided some essential competition for rising and falling stars alike (and those who never made it). The Senior team was always short of one or two of our better men to compete with the likes of Herne Hill and South London who take the League more seriously than ourselves but the Youths performed with credit to make the final where they finished second to Herne Hill despite being without a specialist sprinter. Notable performances over the season came from Pat Lyttle (22.0) Steve Smullen (3.53.6) and Mark Sinclair (8.21.2). Also Mike Hayes and John Bicourt, under 6 minutes for the 2km chase. First year Youth, Clive Gardner ran a fast 23.6 200m while Glyn Tiernan, the same age, looked impressive in the middle distances. Youths field eventers, Julian Mole and Festos Ogwuda, were both over 12 metres in the triple jump - which is good jumping. But perhaps the best performance of all came from 12 year old Adrian Ross who zipped round one lap in 61.1 for a remarkable new club colts record. items.sum: Anecdote about sprinter Pat Lyttle's mis-recorded time in the 25 x 1 mile relay, which led him to run again in the B team.
items.s: Anecdote about sprinter Pat Lyttle's mis-recorded time in the 25 x 1 mile relay, which led him to run again in the B team. Sprinter Pat Lyttle couldn't accept his 6.57 timing in the 25 x 1 mile relay C team. It seemed there was an arithmetic error but the mistake wasn't apparent. So Pat stayed for the afternoon's B team and ran 5.51!! The morning's figures were then re-checked and sure enough it was 5.57. Sorry Pat - they said. Anyway Pat got 2 p.b's in 1 day. Not bad! There will be no excuses for not running a 48.5, 400m next season. Pat Lyttle Pat Lyttle ran 5.51 for 1 mile in the B team after a mis-timed 5.57 in the C team Nike 25x1 Mile Relay

items.label: October 1984
items.sum: Note on Gary Staines' week in July 1984 in which he ran five top races, including winning the Inter-Counties mile and racing for England at Gateshead.
items.s: GARY STAINES' EXTRAORDINARY WEEK. Note on Gary Staines' week in July 1984 in which he ran five top races, including winning the Inter-Counties mile and racing for England at Gateshead. GARY STAINES' EXTRAORDINARY WEEK. Team spirit has been a particular part of our continueing upward path in the British Athletics League. Perhaps the most remarkable example was the case of Gary Staines who in one hectic week in July ran 5 top class races. On the Sunday he ran a heat and won the final of the Inter-Counties 1 mile. On the Wednesday in an Open Meeting he ran a p.b. 800m in 1.50.0. On the Friday he worked in the morning and then dashed up to Gateshead to guest in the England v Spain v Sweden International where he ducked under Stuart's 1500m Club record and was prominant on Television as he led for 3 laps . And on the Saturday he travelled with the BAL team to Windsor and won the 800m as we achieved a massive points win over our rivals. With support like that our Officials know that all the hard work behind the scenes is worthwhile! Gary Staines Gary Staines won Inter-Counties 1 mile; 800m p.b. 1.50.0; broke club 1500m record in England v Spain v Sweden at Gateshead; won BAL 800m at Windsor Stuart Stuart previous holder of club 1500m record British Athletics League Inter-Counties England v Spain v Sweden Gateshead Windsor

items.h: OLIVER GOES SECOND ON ALL TIME LIST
items.sum: Report and full results of the Yacht 3 handicap at Wimbledon on 6 October 1984, won from scratch by Oliver Foote with the 4th fastest time ever on the course behind Gerry North's three.
items.s: OLIVER GOES SECOND ON ALL TIME LIST Report and full results of the Yacht 3 handicap at Wimbledon on 6 October 1984, won from scratch by Oliver Foote with the 4th fastest time ever on the course behind Gerry North's three. OLIVER GOES SECOND ON ALL TIME LIST 6th OCTOBER 1984 WIMBLEDON YACHT 3 HANDICAP It is very seldom that the speedy scratch markers take the handicapper to the cleaners in this event. Generally a few of our slower runners manage to leg it off an over-generous mark. This year it was different due to some exceptionally fine runs from our faster men. Chris Millbank showed what progress a year's training can provide as he knocked a remarkable 2½ minutes off last years debut time. First year Junior, Richard O'Hara translated his recent track form to a fine first run round this course as too did Marcello Bizio. Leo Lyons showed a return to form after prolonged injury while 15 year old Gary McGurren ran an exceptional 16.16 in his first attempt at this event. But pride of place must go to Oliver Foote who took the field apart as he moved from scratch through to take the lead at Wimbledon Village after which he coasted to a 9 sec. lead. His time of 14.34 was the 4th fastest ever round this traditional Club course, the first three all being recorded by Gerry North (14.15, 14.21, and 14.21). Gerry's 14.15 clocking was in 1962 - the year he won the English Senior National Cross Country Champs. As Steve Williams remarked - "This was Oliver's finest win to date". Several ladies competed in this years race, fastest of whom was new member Jill Davies. H = Handicap or watch time A = Actual Time B = Boy, Y = Youth, J = Junior, L = Lady H A H A H A 1. SURREY CROSS COUNTRY LEAGUE - DIVISION 1 13th OCTOBER 1984 WIMBLEDON SURREY C.C. LEAGUE - DIV.I A marginally better performance than last year's opening disaster. Gary Staines cut his foot and was forced to retire while Oliver Foote fell over and did well to get up to 8th place. Andy North turned in a good performance and is beginning to make a few people sit up and take notice as too is Martin Lake. The race was notable for the number of top class second claim members running for other teams. Julian Goater (Shafts) finished 5th in AFD colours while Omega had drafted in two top Welsh runners. Its about time this league was restricted to bona fide clubmen. With only 91 pts. separating the bottom 5 Clubs, the next 3 matches assume even greater importance so lets hope Gordon can get a strong team out next time. items.h: FIRST RELAY SUCCESS AS BELGRAVE WIN INAUGURAL LONDON RELAY
items.sum: Report and results of Belgrave's win in the inaugural 'Zatopek' 6 x 4½km Thames Relay in the City of London on 21 October 1984, organised by Ron Clarke and Dave Bedford, with a photo of anchor John Gladwin.
items.s: FIRST RELAY SUCCESS AS BELGRAVE WIN INAUGURAL LONDON RELAY Report and results of Belgrave's win in the inaugural 'Zatopek' 6 x 4½km Thames Relay in the City of London on 21 October 1984, organised by Ron Clarke and Dave Bedford, with a photo of anchor John Gladwin. FIRST RELAY SUCCESS AS BELGRAVE WIN INAUGURAL LONDON RELAY 21st OCTOBER 1984 CITY OF LONDON 'ZATOPEK' 6x4½km THAMES RELAY This inaugural race organised by ex 10,000m world record holders Ron Clarke and Dave Bedford was well publicised in the Local and National press and despite the previous day's National 6 stage relay received a great response from athletes and spectators. The course, chosen to keep clear of traffic, was not up to Championship Standards involving as it did several flights of steps. Nevertheless the atmosphere was there with commentary by Capital Radio's Kelly Temple and this coupled with free lunch and a drink plus party made the day memorable particularly for the loyal lady supporters. But to the race. This was the first time we had got our strongest 6 together. Not all were fully fit and with many still beginning a gradual build up we weren't certain if the established relay stars would prove too strong for us. The start saw 60 runners streaming over Southwark Bridge with Oliver Foote tucked in in about 12th place. As the fast pace began to bite a group of 3 broke away and at the first change over Oliver was only 3 seconds down on Enfield's leader Keith Doulton. Dave North took it steadily moving into second spot as a gap of around 8 seconds opened between him and the leader. Looking more relaxed than usual and picking up the pace our man gradually pulled back the difference to hand over to Gary Staines in the lead. Gary moved off fast opened up a gap of 15 seconds, relaxed and then had a fright as Andy Catton of Ilford stormed past at the 2 mile mark. Not to be put off Gary knuckled down to some hard work and needed his sprint finish to put us back in the lead. Stuart Paton looked to be moving well as he opened the gap to around 25 seconds which Mark Sinclair needed as Kevin Steer of Ilford took off after him on the 5th leg. The race bubbled at this point as Kevin gradually reduced the gap to get within 3 seconds of Mark 600m out. It was at this point that Mark kicked and the Ilford mans efforts had been in vain. John Gladwin took off as though he was in a fast 1500 and broke Ilfords last stage runner to such an extent that they drifted back to 4th as Keith Palmer ran the fastest leg of the day to bring Highgate into second place 50 seconds adrift. Our'B' team men put up some good times to make a great day for Belgrave. CORNER Vets Corner column on Belgrave veterans' 1984 season, including Laurie O'Hara's UK over-50 1500m record and Southern 10 miles over-50 title, and results of several veterans' road races. VETS. CORNER There were varying fortunes for our Vets on the track and road. With the European Vets T & F Championships being held in Brighton this year we could have expected some medal successes, but it was not to be. Laurie O'Hara who earlier in the year had established a U.K. over 50's 1500m record with 4:13.9 only managed 4th at Brighton as he recorded 4:15.1 just 0.1 sec. off the bronze in a close finish. If he had opted for the 5000m there would have been gold but with an entry fee of £5 plus £5 per event it didn't encourage doubling up. Snowy Brooker also travelled hopefully to Brighton, having put in some excellent performances in our British League team but despite some first class marks in the early events he managed 3 'no-throws' in the discus and was eliminated. Laurie later went on to win the Southern 10 Miles Vets Champs. with a remarkable 53.36 as he led our Vets to a team Silver. 26th MAY 1984 WIMBLEDON VETS A.C. 10 MILES Course now accurately measured to ten miles. 1.F.Bell (Woking) 54.15; 2.J.Froud (Woking) 54.26; 3.T.Ryan (N.London) 54.51. items.s: DUNLOP YOUNG ATHLETES LEAGUE Report on Belgrave's four 1984 Dunlop Young Athletes League matches (Battersea Park, Guildford, Redhill, Portsmouth), with outstanding performances, match results and final league positions (Belgrave third). YOUNG ATHLETES DUNLOP YOUNG ATHLETES LEAGUE This years league competition has been an up and down affair, with successes being sandwiched between disappointments. The following are short reports covering our four matches, highlighting the outstanding performances from these meetings. 6th MAY 1984 BATTERSEA PARK MATCH 1 As our first meeting dawned we found ourselves in disarray after the long winter break. Our weaknesses were startingly apparent in the technical field events where absences let down our extremely strong track team. At the end of the day we scored 17 wins, 16 seconds, 4 thirds and 17 other places, leaving 18 events not covered. The failure to cover these events caused our immediate loss of a minimum of 18 points. Outstanding performances - P.Goedluck Y.200 (23.3) & 100 (11.5); G.Warr Y(B) 200 (24.7) & 100 (11.9) R.Iles C(A) 1500 (5.08.7); D.Ward B(A) 1500 (4.42.1); D.Steward B(B) 1500 (4.35.2); S.Richards Y(A) 400 (54.8); D.Ashford B(A) 3000 (10.28.1); J.Caines B(B) 3000 (11.24); B.Zreik B(B) HJ:(1.50) & B(A) 800 (2:17.5); A.Ross C(A) 800 (2:25.3); C.Gardener Y(A) 100H (15.1). Youths 4x100 (46.2). Results: 1.Sutton & Cheam 248; 2.Surrey Beagles 228; 3.Fareham 202 4.BELGRAVE 186; 5.Walton 147. 3rd JUNE 1984 GUILDFORD MATCH 2 A warm but blustery day greeted us at Guildford. Our team had been dramatically strengthened since the match at Battersea Park and particularly in the field we felt in a far better state to face the competition. The match was very close with several athletes doubling up to cover empty places in some events, and at the end of the day it was these commendable actions added to the other impressive individual results which gave us the day by ½ a point. On this occasion we notched up 18 wins, 15 seconds, 11 thirds and 20 other places leaving only 8 events empty. Outstanding performances - B.Zriek B(A) 400 (56.7) & (A) LJ (5.44); S.Richards Y(A) 200 (24.3); G.Warr Y(B) 200 (25.4) & (B) 100 (12.1); R.Iles C(A) 1500 (5:09.4); C.Cornwell Y(A) HJ (1.75); M.Reece Y(B) HJ (1.70); D.Sewell B(A) SP (11.75); S.Warr B(B) SP (7.58); D.Rose Y(B) LJ (4.78); C.Gardiner Y(A) 100H (15.1); J.Mole Y(B) 100H (17.3); O.Olufuneo B(B) HJ (1.40); M.Dooley Y(A) LJ (5.32) & Y(A) 100 (11.9); G.Allison B(A) HJ (1.60); Youths 4x100 (46.5). Results: 1.BELGRAVE 219; 2.Camberley 218½; 3.Sutton & Cheam 210½; 4.Fareham 190½; 5.Guildford 189½. 24th JUNE 1984 REDHILL MATCH 3 Redhill was the first meeting at which we fielded a team selected by the newly formed Young Athletes Committee. The weather was warm and the athletics hot. With athletes now able to concentrate on their specialist events results were impressive with 23 wins, 19 seconds, 12 thirds and 12 other places. 6 events were still empty but this was understandable when one realises that 12 of the team were representing Surrey and London in the School's Triangular match and were therefore unable to compete for us. Outstanding performances - D.Ashford B(A) PV (1.75); D.McCarthy B(B) PB (1.30) & (B) JT (20.60); G.Warr Y(A) 200 (24.0) & (A) 100 (11.7); G.Pastana Y(B) 200 (24.5); D.Maloney B(B) 200 (27.0); I.Gilley C(A) 200 (27.7); A.Ross C(B) 200 (28.4) & (A) 100 (13.8); J.Mole Y(A) TJ (11.42); G.Tiernan Y(A) 1500 (4:35.7); G.Allison B(A) 80H (12.8) & (A) HJ (1.50); J.Beasty Y(A) 3000 (10.14.4); K.McDonagh Y(B) 3000 (10:15.4) & (B) 1500SC (5:34.7); D.Rose Y(B) 100H (18.6); S.Sbicca B(B) HJ (1.30); S.Beaumont Y(A) 800 (2.10.1). Colts 4x100 (57.2) Youths 4x100 (50.2) & 4x400 (3:52.4). These results gave us our second win, this time by a clear 24 points. Results: 1.BELGRAVE 258; 2.Surrey Beagles 222; 3.Guildford 211; 4.Camberley 165; 5.Walton 121. This moved us up into second place in the league behind Sutton & Cheam. All we needed was an average team performance in our last meeting and we would be guaranteed a place in the promotion qualifying meeting at our home track, Battersea Park. As we left Redhill, hopes were high that we could join our senior teams in their promotion celebrations. 29th JULY 1984 PORTSMOUTH MATCH 4 Tomorrow never comes. Our team for Portsmouth, devastatingly depleted by unavoidable holidays and sickness, was just a poor shadow of the team at Redhill. Our athletes pushed themselves to the maximum, almost all competing in their statutory 4 events. Team morale remained high though unfortunately morale alone doesn't win meetings and with no competitors in 23 out of 72 events a poor result was unavoidable. However all credit must go to the athletes and parents who attended on what was a beautiful day at an excellent facility. Outstanding performances - I.Gilley C(A) 200 (27.7); G.Warr Y(A) 200 (24.5) & (A) 100 (12.4); D.Sewell B(A) ST (12.06) & (A) JAV (76.58); G.Allison B(A) 80H (13.0) & (A) 800 (2.17.6); J.Mole Y(B) TJ (11.80). Results: 1.Sutton & Cheam 405; 2.Fareham 304; 3.Guildford 271; 4.Camberley 267; 5.BELGRAVE 242; 6.Surrey Beagles 202; 7.Walton 159. This put Fareham into the qualifying match, beating us by one point and left Belgrave with the commitment to show their true match dominating colours in 1985. items.s: THAMESIDE LEAGUE Report on the 1984 Thameside League for boys and colts, expanded to include women's teams, with final positions and special mention of Gavin Warr and Gareth Allison. THAMESIDE LEAGUE This Belgrave brainchild, created ostensibly to provide competition for boys up to 14 years of age, was successfully expanded this year to incorporate five women's teams, whose exploits are reported in the Women's Section. In addition to the inter-club events it includes numerous non-scoring competitions in a relaxed atmosphere, where boys can experiment with new events. When reporting the results of our Boys and Colts in this competition it must be said that they appear disappointing because both teams finished near to the bottom of their leagues. This is because, in many cases, this year the emphasis has been to provide club competition for those boys who only occasionally have the opportunity to take part in the Young Athletes League, while at the same time providing a series of non-scoring races for others. Both these objectives were achieved, but at the expense of the league position. It was gratifying also to see the popularity of this venture grow with each meeting with the numbers of competitors in June and July, before the holidays began to thin the ranks, threatening to swamp the organisers. All in all it has been a happy and (with the aforementioned qualification) successful season. With all competing clubs already booking their places for next year we look forward to even greater achievements. Our congratulations go to Croydon Harriers Boys and Camberley A.C. Colts, but warn them, we shall be after the trophies next year. The individual performances are too numerous to mention in this report, but the final league tables were as follows THAMESIDE LEAGUE - FINAL POSITIONS. COLTS; 1. Camberley 22pts., 2. Croydon 18pts., 3. Twick.& Ran. 15pts., 4. HHH 14pts., 5. BELGRAVE 8pts., 6. Queens Park H 7pts. BOYS; 1. Croydon 22pts., 2. HHH 21pts., 3. Camberley 17pts., 4. BELGRAVE 10pts., 5. Queens Pk 8pts., 6. Twick.& Ran. 6pts. In summing up the season special mention must be made of the exploits of Gavin Warr (Youth) and Gareth Allison (Boy). Gavin competed in every Young Athletes League and won every race in which he competed. Gareth competed in both Young Athletes and Thameside Leagues and proved to be the club's only high-jumping middle-distance hurdler. Finally the Young Athletes sub committee wish to thank all the parents and officials who supported us so consistently throughout the season. Reports by Jim & Dave Mote. items.sum: Ladies Secretary Derek Jones's review of the women's 1984 season: 7th in the Womens Southern League, Midweek League win, county vests and medals, individual progress, and thanks to helpers.
items.s: WITH THE LADIES Ladies Secretary Derek Jones's review of the women's 1984 season: 7th in the Womens Southern League, Midweek League win, county vests and medals, individual progress, and thanks to helpers. WITH THE LADIES It has been quite an exciting season, with us finishing in 7th position in the Womens Southern League. This was our best position since 1980. In this League after 4 3rd placings we were lying 12th and we won the last 2. The last meeting was against strong opposition and we beat Aldershot, a team we had never beaten before so that was really pleasing. The Thameside League was a good replacement for the Lily B League and we hope that this will be continued for next season, especially as the athletes seemed to enjoy the competition. After a period of 6 years we re-entered the Midweek League (very similar in content to the Rosenheim League) and as we won every match we won the League very convincingly. There were plenty of places for the Non-scorers and everyone who came along was able to get competition. Our Junior relay team was unbeaten in all 6 Southern League, all 4 Thameside League and all 6 Midweek League races which is another good record. During the Season Club records were broken on at least 40 occasions. Three of our athletes gained their county vests. Wendy Dunsford represented Middlesex in a meeting in May held at Motspur Park, whilst Veronica St. Ange competed for Surrey in a representative match in July at Copthall and Rosemary Honeychurch represented Surrey in the Southern Womens Inter Counties Championships in August held at Crystal Palace. Three of our athletes also won Gold in County Championships. Rosemary Honeychurch won the 3000m in the Surrey Championships, whilst Cindy James and Angela Abrams won the 100m and Hurdles in the Middlesex Championships. Our total tally of medals in both County Championships was 12, with 6 Silvers and 3 Bronzes. So congratulations to all the medal winners and all those who took part. This was our best haul of medals in County Championships as well. Our walkers were well represented in the English Schools Walking Championships with London being represented by Gail Porter, Kim Marsh, Isobel Young and Charlotte Chirstou and Surrey and Essex being represented by Rachael Parrott and Joanne McGroder respectively. Picking out individuals it is worth noting that Jessica Palmer has continued the improvement she showed from last season and was joined in the Sprints by Yvette Edward Cindy James, Angela Abrams and Andrea Abrams, Nina Christou and Tracy Ritson. Angela Abrams and Nina Christou, both improved their Hurdles technique and had good backing from Cindy James. Cindy proved to be a good all-round athlete with improvements to her Shot and Discus. We were a bit short of junior middle distance runners, but those who did the events tried their best but the improvement shown by Jackie Stone was very encouraging as well as winning Silver in the Surrey Championships. Angela Abrams and her twin sister Andrea improved their marks in the Long Jump and Andrea began to do better in the high jump but must learn to concentrate harder. The record book has been re-written by Rachael Parrott in the walks and now holds all the Girls records as well as improving upon the Girls Javelin record. In the Seniors the middle distance team of Rosemary Honeychurch who has knocked over a minute off her 3000m record this season and there is probably more to come, Vicky Mitchell, Gail Porter ably backed by Davina Cameron and Georgina Tura did well. The Sprinters did not do as well as the Middle Distance runners but Andrea Coore, Shirley Daure, Penny Garnons-Williams well backed by Dezrine Conard, Adele Peck, and when they were able to come to meetings Erica Goldson and Susan Wilkinson Our Throwing team of Wendy Dunsford, Debbie Roberts, Veronica St. Ange as well as Perrican Bayar when she was available proved almost unbeatable. They won through although not always at their best and Veronica competed with broken bones in her foot. It is perhaps worth noting that we have competed in 40 Southern League fixtures since 1977 and Wendy has only missed 2 of them. She has been ever-present since June 1979 and in the Shot in the 30 matches since we were promoted to Division 3 has scored 139 points out of a possible 150. Our Walkers have kept Belgrave vests to the fore and these have been led very well by Rachael Parrott ably backed by Isobel Young, Charlotte Christou and were ably backed by Kelly Owen, Julie Field and Teresa Thirlwall. For all these results thanks must go to a great number of people who have helped me no end this season. Among those who should be mentioned are Ted Weldin, Dave Wenham, and Graham Thom for their help in the Hurdles, Jumps and Sprints. Also for his efforts in the Walks, thanks must go to Dave Sharpe, who has turned up at Battersea Park from Dagenham despite having a number of problems during the summer. Thanks to Derek Crookes too for also helping with the Middle Distance girls during the back end of the season. Last, but not least my thanks must go to Harry Porter and Frank Simmons for the work they do and their help and advice during the Season. Thanks to all the parents who come along and help and support and have made friends with each other and thanks to Sue Parrott for taking over the Press Representative's job. It is very pleasant to have so many people eager and willing to help and to those who come along to help judge at meetings as well. We could have done with a few more of these. After all we are here to help and encourage athletes and athletics and this cannot be done by not supporting BELGRAVE. We need help especially at Home Matches and even recording helps as Wyn Sheppard who was at all our home matches doing just that, or serving teas. Every little helps, so why not come and enjoy a day out seeing youngsters enjoy themselves. If I have missed anybody in my thanks during the season, then the omission was not really intentional. Thanks to all who have helped and encouraged or brought their children along to meetings by car. items.s: WOMEN'S SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION 3 SOUTH Report and results of the Women's Southern League Division 3 South match at Battersea Park on 14 April 1984, Belgrave third, with four club records. WOMEN'S SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIVISION 3 SOUTH 14th APRIL 1984 BATTERSEA PARK SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV.3 SOUTH Teams: 1.Ashford A.C. 183; 2.Redhill & Reigate A.C. 172; 3.BELGRAVE 161½; 4.Eastbourne Rovers 93½; 5.Walton A.C. 83. A fine day, sunny and warm and Battersea Park looking really splendid. This was always going to be a tough match, with Ashford having been relegated and Redhill just missing promotion. There were some really great performances, with 4 new club records,1 club record being equalled and about 20 personal best performances being set. Excellent runs in the 1500m and 3000m by Rosemary Honeychurch, breaking her own 3000m record by some 24 seconds. Our Turkish national champion Perrican Bayar improved the Discus record by over 9 metres, Veronica St. Ange broke the Javelin record and Andrea Coore broke the Inters High Jump record and equalled the Senior record. It is perhaps worth noting that this was Wendy Dunsford's 28th consecutive Southern League meeting since June 1979. items.s: SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV.3 SOUTH Report and results of the Women's Southern League Division 3 South match at Crawley on 5 May 1984, Belgrave equal third, with three more club records. 5th MAY 1984 CRAWLEY SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV.3 SOUTH Teams: 1.Medway A.C. 161½; 2.E.Grinstead & Dist.A.C. 159;=3.BELGRAVE 134; =3.Bournemouth A.C. 134; 5.Salisbury AC 99½; This was a match that we possibly should have won if everybody had been available. The English Schools Walking Championships took place on the same day and that took away some, whilst others were injured and some waited for the coach in the wrong place. However, some arm twisting by Rosemary Honeychurch on the journey down meant that we were covered in most Junior events and 2 of the Seniors ended up doing 4 individual events and a relay. 3 more Club records fell and 18 more personal bests were set and some were doing events unfamiliar to them, but with those results what more could have been asked of anybody. Fresh from her triumphs in the Surrey Championships Rosemary Honeychurch broke her club record still further and ran a personal best in the 1500m. The Senior Discus and Junior Discus records were both broken. items.s: SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV.3 SOUTH Report and results of the Women's Southern League Division 3 South match at Yeovil on 21 July 1984, Belgrave third after a coach breakdown; the second senior relay is printed as 4x100m though its time and team suggest 4x400m. 21st JULY 1984 YEOVIL SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV.3 SOUTH 1.Yeovil Olympiades A.C. 182; 2.Bognor Reg. & Chich.A.C. 160; 3.BELGRAVE 141½; 4.Boro.of Kingston A.C. 129; 5.Horsham Blue Star Harriers 103½. Such are the peculiarities of these leagues that we had to travel down to Somerset to meet near neighbours Kingston, whom we had already met three days earlier in another league. Quite an eventful trip with an articulated lorry jack-knifing in front of us and the coach breaking down about 2 miles from the track. As luck had it, the Kingston coach passed us just as we were starting to walk and came back for us. We repaid this kindness by pushing them into 4th spot. Andrea Coore broke the Intermediate 400m Hurdle record at only her second attempt at the distance. items.s: SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV.3 SOUTH Report and results of the Women's Southern League Division 3 South match at Portsmouth on 11 August 1984, won by Belgrave with six club records. 11th AUGUST 1984 PORTSMOUTH SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV.3 SOUTH 1.BELGRAVE 166; 2.Hastings A.C. 164; 3.Weymouth St.Pauls 156; 4.Winchester & Dist.A.C. 103½; 5.Portsmouth Atalanta A.C. 101½. This is a match we should have won as after the fourth match we were above the other teams we met here. However, with 6 new club records being set and 7 personal best performances, this was the time to give of their best. Commiserations to Andrea Coore who broke the Intermediate 400m Hurdles record only to see it snatched away 2 minutes later by Vicky Mitchell. The other records came from Cindy James in the Discus (also breaking the Intermediate record) Tracy Ritson in the Girls Javelin (this erases a record that had stood for 7 years) and a fine win in the 4 x 400m Relay to knock 3 seconds off the old record. items.s: SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV.3 (S) Report and results of the Women's Southern League Division 3 South match at Dartford on 1 September 1984, won by Belgrave, securing 7th place in the division; it calls this the first win over Aldershot, though the season review says the same of an earlier match. 1st SEPTEMBER 1984 DARTFORD SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV.3 (S) Results: 1.BELGRAVE 178; 2.Ald.Farn.& Dist. 176½; 3.Dartford H.148; 4.Basingstoke A.C. 145½; 5.Fleet & Crookham A.C. 37. This was a really splendid result for us as two of the teams we beat were in 5th and 6th position in the Division. This also was the first time that we have beaten Aldershot so that result was even more pleasing. This result meant that we finished in 7th position in the Division which is the best that we have done since 1980. It also means that we finish well above Hercules Wimbledon and with the last result just pushed Kingston back into 8th place. items.label: October 1985
items.sum: The editor's farewell after six years and twelve editions, contrasting the club's thin results of six years earlier with its present growth and success.
items.s: 'MAMMOTH' FAREWELL The editor's farewell after six years and twelve editions, contrasting the club's thin results of six years earlier with its present growth and success. This mammoth edition of the Belgravian represents for your Editor a final fling. For after 6 years and 12 editions it is time for a new face. As we progress towards our Centenary year we are moving into a period when naturally there will be a great deal of reminiscing about past glories. But in the role as Editor, where every aspect of Club activities is scrutinised and sifted before being recorded, it has become apparent that the Belgrave of today is in many ways far removed from that of 30 or even 10 years ago. I well remember 6 years ago searching desparately for decent copy on athletic achievements. Apart from the up and coming young squad of Dave North, Mark Sinclair, Mark Waller, Paul Richley, Stuart Paton and John Gladwin, plus the ever successful walkers , there was very little to give hope for the future. Our track team was about to be relegated to Div. 2 of the Southern League and the Road and Country team were desparately short of star performers. Today all that has been transformed. The problem with producing the Club magazine now is that in all Sections there has been a massive increase in active members and an incredible increase in athletic performances. Unfortunately because costs and Editorial time have to be kept within reasonable limits many items now have to be omitted. Behind all this success has been a growing team of enthusiastic officials and helpers all willing to give generously of their time to help our young, active and up and coming members. It is because of them that we can look forward to a well planned and exciting future. A future that will see many of our members rising to the top levels of International competition with all the financial rewards which such achievements deserve. I hope that the Belgravian will continue to record these successes and will provide interesting and stimulating reading for all members whether young or old, rabbits or stars. I wish my successor well. The place of our magazine in Club life cannot be overestimated. Dave North Dave North Mark Sinclair Mark Sinclair Mark Waller Mark Waller Paul Richley Paul Richley Stuart Paton Stuart Paton John Gladwin John Gladwin Southern League

items.sum: Club gossip notes: members' radio appearances, marriages, engagements, injuries, a Toga party and a Valentine's Day aerial stunt.
items.s: grapevine Club gossip notes: members' radio appearances, marriages, engagements, injuries, a Toga party and a Valentine's Day aerial stunt. grapevine Leo Coy hit the airwaves in January when he appeared as the final questioner on Radio 4's Sports Review and Quiz. Graham Macky has written from New Zealand. He and Debbie were married last year and it suits him. After a fine second place in the N.Z. Marathon Championship he ran in the IAAF World Championship in Hiroshima on 14th April and finished 46th in 2:16.17. We also hear that there will be a new addition to the family early in 1986. Congratulations. Dave Mote's tendon operation proved successful and he has now to decide whether to resume his athletes career or become a full time dilettante. The omens are not good. His 25th birthday Toga party at Belgrave Hall showed all the usual signs of creeping decadence. The North brothers also displayed a couple of dirty habits despite which their Fan Club organised by our younger Ladies seems to be growing! John Aska at Walton track in September. Nothing strange you may think. But no' Our field events man has transformed into a top American Football star. Nicknamed 'Crusher' he helped a G.B. team defeat France 7-0 in the first International between these two countries. Doesn't qualify for the International Honours Board though! Remember Paul Richley and Kevin Sturman left our shores for U.S. Universities in August '84. Almost immediately both suffered injuries which put them out of action for the season. Thereafter their lives followed strangely similar patterns. Kevin married Anita in May 1985 and its doubtful if we will see them back here on a permanent basis. Paul returned early in 1985 and announced his engagement to Tina Couzens. Congratulations and best wishes to all. You'll read elsewhere of Mike Alleynes great 400m improvements this year. It may be a coincidence but at the middle of the year he got engaged. We wish him and Erica all happiness in the future. But in 1984 the wedding was that of Chris Everett to founding member of our Ladies Section, Jane Pritchard. Most of us can't remember exactly what happened at the celebrations and its costing an arm and a leg to suppress Brian's video. Chris has moved to the Bahamas to further his career as a croupier. Jane joined him in the summer. Maggie Thatcher and The Queen followed in October! February 14th - Valentine's Day saw a light aircraft circling South London/N.E.Surrey with an appropriate message in tow. The local press finally tracked down the instigator. Yes you've guessed - Charlie Manning! Can we afford for this boy to take charge of our Centenary Year promotional campaign? GORDON DOUBLEDAY Gordon Doubleday, now happily ensconced (S.P's word of the month!) in Bath frequently writes to let us know what a great place it is. Gordon is very active timekeeping at local meetings. Here we see Gordon warming up for a big local event. He is caught in this shot red-handed with one of the local beauties - none other Diana Moran - more famous as TV's keep fit star the 'Green Goddess'. There had to be some perks! Since moving to Bath -Gordon has been very much involved with Somer A.C. which was founded in 1981. His vast experience has been put to wide use in aid of local athletics and recently his services to Somer has been formally recognised by granting to him Life Membership. Gordon reports that several ex-Belgravians are active in the County of Avon and that the leading light behind Somer is non other than a man who was competing for us in the late 1960's - Bob James who sends his best wishes to those whose memories can stretch back that far. items.label: October 1985
items.sum: Humorous account of Oliver Foote being bitten by a dog on the Kingston-By-Pass, his £28 compensation, and his faster finishing since.
items.s: A BUM DEAL! Humorous account of Oliver Foote being bitten by a dog on the Kingston-By-Pass, his £28 compensation, and his faster finishing since. A BUM DEAL! Have you noticed that since the jogging boom dogs have become a lot more tolerant towards your average runner. There remain a few who find the nippier mortal irresistable and one of these had a good go at our top distance man Oliver Foote just at the start of the track season. The setting was the Kingston-By-Pass, Oliver was working up a nice pace mid-way between the Coombe Lane Bridge and the Robin Hood Roundabout when a particular ferocious specimen hurtled out of the riding stables and sank its nashers into his rear end. Our hero limped along to Kingston Hospital where the injury was much admired by the duty nurses as they drew lots to administer the compulsory anti-tetanus injection. Next on to the local cop shop where the matter was investigated by the boys in blue who eventually located the animal plus its owner. Negotiations for compensation began. No doubt Seb Coe would have commanded a good fee. our man settled for £28. As it turned out the adventure had its brighter side. We now notice that Oliver has acquired a noticeable acceleration - a change of pace which led to a 58 sec. last lap as he gained the Surrey 5000m Silver medal in mid-May (and in a p.b.). This fact has not gone unnoticed by some of our middle distance coaches and it is rumoured that as dust falls on Wimbledon Common, some can be heard practising their barking and growling techniques - based on second hand instruction books by Percy Edwards. So next time you think you're being chased by a Doberman - check twice - it might be Jim Webster!!!!! Oliver Foote Oliver Foote bitten by a dog while training; Surrey 5000m silver medal in a p.b. items.sum: Obituary of Leslie J. Cohen, Belgrave middle distance runner from 1934 and leading athletics administrator who became club president and a life vice president of the AAA.
items.s: LESLIE J. COHEN Obituary of Leslie J. Cohen, Belgrave middle distance runner from 1934 and leading athletics administrator who became club president and a life vice president of the AAA. In Memorium LESLIE J. COHEN Long, lean and hungry looking and striding purposefully over a cross country course dressed in 'Wellies' and oilskins - that is how I prefer to remember him, for that was when he was at his happiest. Born in South London in October 1908, he first graced the athletic scene in the '20s as a member of Ashcombe (later to be Ashcombe St. Georges AC), but it was as a Belgrave Harrier (from 1934) that he flourished into an excellent middle distance runner of near international standard with pre-war successes on track, road and country. After the War he threw himself into athletic administration with such enthusiasm and energy that he was known to everyone in the sport for his organising ability. For many years he was secretary and/or championship secretary to the AAA, Southern AAA, Southern Cross Country Association, South of the Thames Cross Country Association, CAU and London Business Houses AA, besides other appointments associated with those organisations and with Belgrave Harriers, who are forever grateful for his fund raising initiative, which led to the development of their headquarters in Wimbledon to the standard they are today. All this work led him, perhaps a little reluctantly, to the presidencies of Belgrave, South of the Thames, Southern AAA, Southern CCA, ECCU, and ultimately to a life vice presidency of the AAA. It is a privilege to have been associated with this man and to have competed and served with him over a long period of time. We have missed him during the past few years when his health prevented him from carrying on in his usual energetic and spirited way, but he was not forgotten. Wherever his colleagues met his name cropped up and will continue to do so - we will remember him. Our sympathies and condolences go to his wife Mary (nee Hutchins), who in her early days was also a distinguished athlete with Spartan Ladies. W.E. Lucas, Leslie J. Cohen LESLIE J. items.sum: Obituary of Ethel M. Carter, long-time Belgrave supporter and wife of Tom Carter, who died on 10 October.
items.s: ETHEL M. CARTER Obituary of Ethel M. Carter, long-time Belgrave supporter and wife of Tom Carter, who died on 10 October. ETHEL M. CARTER On 10th October we lost one of our dearest and best loved supporters. Ethel who two years ago suffered a partial stroke and had been making a steady recovery, passed away peacefully. We have lost a great friend. Ethel was keenly interested in all of Belgrave's activities starting back in the 1930's when she first met Tom and encouraged him in his many successes. Tom and Ethel have been a part of the Belgrave scene for over 50 years providing a constant source of help and encouragement to generations of young athletes. Floral tributes both from the Club and from over 40 Belgravians said far more than words to convey our deep respect and love for Ethel. Our thoughts and support are with Tom at this sad time. Ethel M. Carter ETHEL M. CARTER supporter for over 50 years; died 10 October 1985 ETHEL M. CARTER Ethel Tom Tom Ethel Carter's husband

items.sum: Obituary of Bas Collins, former Surrey AC and Belgrave road runner, who died aged 44 while out training.
items.s: BAS. COLLINS Obituary of Bas Collins, former Surrey AC and Belgrave road runner, who died aged 44 while out training. BAS. COLLINS Our Road Racing team members of the late 60's are now dispersed to many parts of the world. All will be saddened to learn of the death, while out on a training run, of Bas Collins. As a member of Surrey AC Bas. won the Surrey Senior CC title in 1964 and in 1967 in the AAA's Marathon Championship he finished 4th in 2:19.22. Bas joined H.W. in 1968 and was part of the teams which provided us with so many close relay races. After a lay off Bas re-started racing as a Vet. Many of his friends questioned his wisdom as it was rumoured he had a heart problem. But his love of the sport won. As David Cocksedge wrote in Athletes Weekly - at the age of 44 he died in the way he probably would have wanted. Bas Collins BAS.
