items.label: October 1985
items.sum: Profile of new club President Gordon Biscoe: his running career from 1953, road running, his long service as Road and Cross Country Secretary, and his organising of club races.
items.s: GORDON BISCOE - PRESIDENT Profile of new club President Gordon Biscoe: his running career from 1953, road running, his long service as Road and Cross Country Secretary, and his organising of club races. GORDON BISCOE - PRESIDENT Gordon Biscoe joined Belgrave in 1953 after a period of service with the R.A.F. His athletics career began at school and continued during R.A.F. Service where he shared in many team successes over the country, including the winning of the Shropshire Championship in 1952. Although Gordon's career with Belgrave never hit the dizzy heights of individual stardom, he was one of the engine room men sharing in the successes of the 50's and 60's teams, when you had to fight to get into the Surrey, Southern,National and major relays. Gordon's first love was always the road, achieving much better success than in the track where his best times were 2.06 for 880 yds, 4.35 for the Mile and just inside 15m for 3 Miles. In humerous vein he lists amongst his achievements on the road as being the only known person to run the famous 'Bridges Race' on the Thames Embankment in two left shoes; and being selected the most number of times as first reserve for the Brighton Relay! His first official role in the Club was as Road Running Captain from 1964 to 1967, a period when our senior teams were the scourge of the road, when he then took over from Derek Crooks as Road Secretary. In 1969 he then took over from Bill Laws as Cross Country Secretary, a position he has now held for 17 years. In addition during the late 60's he was Social Secretary for 2 years, when he organised a number of successful socials. Gordon has always preferred to devote what time he has got to Belgrave rather than seek honours in the outside world of athletics, but he has served on the general committee of the Surrey AAA as well as the South of the Thames C.C.A. for many years, culminating this service by being elected President of the South of the Thames in 1983/84. He He is also a graded timekeeper. His organisational abilities are now well known having built up a large experience (and store of amusing anecdotes) over the years, from organising ordinary club races to major championships on behalf of the Club. He organised our 20m Road Race for 6 years with the 1975 event being his most memorable one, as being the occasion he first met Margaret, now his wife, who at the time was Centre Organiser of the Wimbledon Red Cross who always attend this event. When they were married in 1979 Gordon confessed that it was then he realised he wasn't running fast enough any more! Like many Belgrave wives Margaret now helps out in many 'behind the scenes' activities, such as making cross country marker flags, or collating race entries etc. Gordon's longest running epic is now the Belgrave 12 Stage Road Relay which he has masterminded for 17 years in to the premier race that it is today carrying Southern Counties AAA Championship status and commercial sponsorship. Away from Belgrave, Gordon is a Chartered Electrical Engineer working for a research association. In his spare time, what there is left from Belgrave duties, business commitments (often abroad) and helping look after a young son, Richard of fourteen months, Gordon lists amongst his hobbies, gardening and Jazz - having been a very keen follower of Chris Barber and Humphrey Lyttleton. items.label: October 1985
items.sum: New President Gordon Biscoe's message thanking members and calling for a stronger, financially secure and united club ahead of the centenary.
items.s: From the President New President Gordon Biscoe's message thanking members and calling for a stronger, financially secure and united club ahead of the centenary. From the President May I first take this opportunity to say a sincere thank you to you all for the honour of being elected President of this great club; it is one which I shall always cherish. In my seventeen years as Cross Country Secretary some previous Presidents have called for efforts to be made to achieve some athletic goal during their term of office, like winning the National Cross Country Championship, but while these goals are of course always desirable, they have sometimes been unrealistic. During this coming year I would, therefore, like to set a goal for all members, which is perhaps less spectacular in the short term, but is very desirable, very necessary and at the same time achievable - it is for us all to work harder and closer together to make Belgrave even greater. It is desirable in that we will be in our 99th year and what better way to celebrate the following centenary year and fulfil all the plans being made than with a thriving club. It is necessary for, as most of you know, in the world of athletics times are changing fast and in order to keep pace with these changes it must be our objective to work for a stronger and more financially secure club with ever improving facilities to meet the needs of all our athletes. It will mean forgetting some of the parochial attitudes that sometimes exist between the various sections, and working for the Club as a whole; it will mean recruiting 'new blood' to our organizational and management ranks to ease the burden of some of these already in office; and for our active athletes, particularly 'A Team' members, it will sometimes mean putting Club requirements before personal desires, in order to get team success. It is as teams that we will invariably get our victories and we are capable of far more than we do, if only our teams were properly supported. Success breeds success! and surely our efforts in the British League this summer are a fitting example. Good Luck and best wishes in all your efforts in the year ahead. GORDON BISCOE Gordon Biscoe GORDON BISCOE President; Cross Country Secretary for seventeen years National Cross Country Championships British League

items.sum: Anecdote of Marcello Bizio, laid up with a hernia after three road race wins in Italy, being urged by Colin to run anyway.
items.s: CRACKER! Anecdote of Marcello Bizio, laid up with a hernia after three road race wins in Italy, being urged by Colin to run anyway. CRACKER! There's a story doing the rounds that may well be apocryphal but is worth telling nonetheless. Following a substantial reduction in weight and victories in three road races in Italy, Marcello Bizio has become hot property. If one of the first team men is missing Marcello is your man. Unfortunately all this activity brought on a groin strain which has required surgery. Just before the operation Marcello was contacted by our Assistant Cross Country Sec. who urged him to turn out for the following weeks race. Now Marcello's English is improving by leaps and bounds. "Sorry", said our hero, "I can't run, I am with Hernia". "Don't worry old son", says Colin, "First claim membership of a foreign Club doesn't count!". What a cracker! Anyway what we're trying to say is "Get well soon Marcello? The team needs you back as soon as possible" Marcello Bizio Marcello Bizio won three road races in Italy; groin surgery Marcello Bizio Marcello Colin Colin Assistant Cross Country Secretary Italy

items.sum: Report on the official opening of the rebuilt Belgrave Hall and new gym, conducted by AAA Secretary Mike Farrell, with thanks to Peter Pitt for a GLC grant.
items.s: BELGRAVE HALL Report on the official opening of the rebuilt Belgrave Hall and new gym, conducted by AAA Secretary Mike Farrell, with thanks to Peter Pitt for a GLC grant. BELGRAVE HALL Although Mike Winch and Judy Oakes had started operations at the new Gym as far back as October 1984 it wasn't until February that the rest of the Hall had been finished to a standard ready for the official opening.The Official Opening Ceremony was conducted by AAA's Secretary - Mike Farrell who was able to confirm that the AAA's would be contributing specialist equipment for strength training.Local dignitaries including the Major and Majoress of Wimbledon were in attendance and we were particularly pleased to welcome representatives of the Southern AAA's, the London and South East Regional Sports Council,the London and Surrey playing Fields Association. Present too was our biggest supporter - Peter Pitt-who you will recall stepped in at the last minute to provide a GLC grant of £14000 when the development project was foundering due to cost escallation and the introduction of VAT mid way through the the building programme. Past Presidents travelled from all over the UK to see the conclusion of a project that many had helped start with the purchase of the Hall way back in the 1930's. All were able to admire the new developments which have resulted in the Hall now being used for some 70 hours per week and open for training 7 days each week. items.s: OFFICIAL CHANGES Changes of officials at the AGM, including Joe Coleman as General Secretary, and a tribute to Bill Couzens on stepping down after building up the bar and hall lettings. OFFICIAL CHANGES This years Annual General Meeting saw a substantial change round in our Official line-up. Joe Coleman fresh from an active Presidential year has taken over the mantle of Gen. Hon. Sec. while Eric Crutcher backed by Keith Duckett has taken over the role of Gen. Hon. Sec. Social. Harry Porter has extended his involvement with the Ladies Section taking over the Track and Field Sec. job as well as the Country while on the Vets side Keith Sinclair has moved into the Secretaries seat and we are delighted to see a new face on the management side. Elected members included on the Committee are; Dave Mote, Andy Paton,Keith Duckett,Sue Parrott and Bill Laws. Bill Couzens. With Bill Couzens stepping down from the Gen. Sec. Admin. job we see an end of an era. It is difficult to overstate Bill's contribution to the improvement in Belgrave's fortunes over the last 5 years. It was he alone who built up the bar activities and the hall letting from nothing to a point where they provided a major contribution to the overall monies coming into the Club. In addition to running the business side Bill also undertook all the odd jobs needed to keep the facilities in good repair. It was not unusual for him to be called out of bed during the small hors of the morning and most Saturday mornings until quite recently he could be seen cleaning the Hall and generally undertaking those thousand and one jobs needed to keep everything running smoothly. Spare moments at home were taken up with book-keeping but probably Bill's best efforts were reserved the beer itself. Without doubt the best drop of Guiness in South London can be had at the Hall and that does not happen by accident. It is a measure of Bill's contribution that his job has been split into four parts because it would be practically impossible to find anyone who could devote enough time to what in reality could be considered a full time job. The Club owes Bill a great deal - and you can bet he would be the first to deny it. But we know Better!! Thanks Bill. Joe Coleman Joe Coleman Gen. Hon. FINANCIAL MATTERS Ron Severn reported on his first year as Hon Treasurer at the September AGM. Last year we had been warned that because the Hall would be out of action for 6 months during the rebuild and because we would need to start repaying the loans in 1985 there would be little likelihood of a profit. Surprise therefore when we learned of a substantial surplus of £2,095 for the year. The signs for 1986 are even better with lettings near to capacity. Things really seem to be in good shape and in capable hands. Ron Severn Ron Severn Hon Treasurer Belgrave Hall

items.s: INDIAN SUMMER Leo Coy's visit to Ranjit Bhatia in Delhi and Bhatia's run in a 250km multi-day race from Agra to Delhi. INDIAN SUMMER Leo Coy has recently returned from a business trip to India and while in Delhi was royaly entertained by Ranjit Bhatia. Ranjit is expecting another Belgravian in the near future when Bob Taylor travels to India in November on holiday. Super Vet Ranjit moved into the area of ultra long distance competition recently when he competed in the 250km race from Agra to Delhi. The race started at 7am on October 4th 1985 and 40km was covered before lunch with a further 25km in the afternoon. In the following days they covered 55km, 55km,65km, finishing with a short sprint of 15km into Delhi. Out of 256 starters over 200 finished the course and the event attracted Nationwide T.V. coverage. items.s: WALKING Carl Lawton's review of the Belgrave walking section, on squad depth, the 20-30 age gap and the season of individual walkers including Graham Seatter's National and Inter-Counties medals. One of the advantages of being a member of a strong section is that even if you are a 'good' club man' usually finishing in 7th or 8th in the team there is always the chance that you may get the odd 4th spot when some cannot turn out and still get in the prizes. With a weak section you may always be in the team but the team is not good enough to gain prizes. With this in mind a glance through the results will show how many have been in the scoring teams during the winter months, especially the London 10 miles. We still, however, must endeavour to encourage more people, not just to come into the sport but to stay in. The wastage of 'talent' is something we should all be concerned about, there is at the moment a gap in the 20-30 age group. Why else do you see a lot of the same faces heading fields that were there 10 years ago? Meanwhile to the present. A good winter, but so was last year. Wins at Cambridge, Pewsey Cup, Belgrave and Imber Court, generally with good packing and never our best team out. Graham Seatter finished off his year back with us turning out when he could and showing Murray Day the ropes. During the year Graham collected two National medals and an Inter Counties team medal, not a bad achievement for someone who had given up walking for the last three years. Richard Dorman had his good raves, not as good as he had hoped but he is still a 'youngster', and his trips down from Nottingham for races should be an example to us all. Paul Warburton, back from his years sabatical in America, wasted little time in getting back into team placings, although the change in climate here did not suit him. Richard Tanner has almost returned to his standard of 7 years ago, not bad for someone who did not expect to take up walking again. John Newnham has not been at his best for a while but has still collected the odd team prize. Which brings me to the 'youngsters', Neil Foster, 3rd in the SCAAA 10kms and 2nd in the Club 10m, Michael Feighan (likened in style to Stan Vickers, but not quite the speed yet) and Murray Day. There is little one needs to say of Murray. Results say all that. And there is Stephen Marshall too, who, having had his work commitments reduced should be back in the spotlight. John Hall has had to lie low for a while due to varicose vein problems but is now back on the road. Individual winner was Phil Vesty, winner two years ago, although not so fast. As it was it was fortunate for us that Leicester did not bring a strong 4th man as they had 3 in 6. 1.P.Vesty (Leics) 51.12; 2.M.Easton 51.34; 3.J.Ball (Soton) 52.05; 4.M.Day 52.31; 8.R.Dorman 54.18; 12.C.Lawton 55.10; 13.G.Seatter 55.12; 15.R.Tanner 55.47; 19.J.Hall 56.35; 27.J.Llewellin 58.14; 31.J.Newnham 58.53; 36.M.Feighan 60.17; 48.R.Middleton 62.40; 71.D.Sharpe 69.00; 74.J.Keown 69.28; 80.J.Morris 71.42; 85.G.Beecham 73.47; Team: 1.BELGRAVE 'A' 37; 2.Steyning 62; 3.Surrey W.C. 64; 10.BELGRAVE 'B' 203. items.s: PEWSEY CUP 7m Results of the Pewsey Cup 7 mile walk at Calne on 1 December 1984, where Belgrave's two teams were first and third (both printed as 'B' team). 1st DECEMBER 1984 CALNE PEWSEY CUP 7m Our previous trip to Calne in October had been, to say the least, a disaster. So as to prove we may have been down but not out, we ventured west once more with a little apprehension. The Pewsey Cup is not quite such a big race as the Chippenham to Calne but it was to be a race where everyone was to be on his Best Behaviour. 6 men travelling, 2 teams entered, 3 per team, so we could not lose anyone by the wayside. As it turned out all went well ending up with 1st and 3rd, we could have been 1st and 2nd if we could have known the finishing order beforehand, but you can't win them all, and on top of that there was another good 'B' team still at home. 1.J.Ball (Soton) 49.41; 2.C.Maddocks (Dawlish) 50.18; 3.K.Baker (Weymouth) 51.31; 4.M.Day 51.47; 5.C.Lawton 52.19; 6.G.Seatter 52.42; 7.R.Tanner 53.24; 14.P.Warburton 55.10; 15.J.Newnham 55.20; Team: 1.BELGRAVE 'B' 18; 2.Steyning 30; 3.BELGRAVE 'B' 33. items.s: GRAHAM RETURNS TO NZ Report of the Cambridge Harriers league walk at Bexley on 5 January 1985, Graham Seatter's last race before returning to New Zealand, where he was second. GRAHAM RETURNS TO NZ 5th JANUARY 1985 BEXLEY CAMBRIDGE H. LEAGUE MEETING This race was Graham Seatter's final 'fling' on English soil. As it was he virtually flew the flag on his own for Belgrave. It turned out to be one of the coldest days and probably Graham's coldest race, but he survived to take 2nd place. In the girls events Gail Porter managed a personal best and Rachael Parrott a 3rd. items.sum: Report and results of the snow-hit London 10 mile walk championship at Battersea Park on 9 February 1985, won by Richard Tanner with Belgrave the winning team.
items.s: LONDON 10M CHAMPIONSHIP Report and results of the snow-hit London 10 mile walk championship at Battersea Park on 9 February 1985, won by Richard Tanner with Belgrave the winning team. 9th FEBRUARY 1985 BATTERSEA PARK LONDON 10M CHAMPIONSHIP This almost proved to be a non-event. Snow during the previous night reduced the number of starters to an embarrassingly low number of 16. Whether it should have been held is debatable, but had it been cancelled then it would have been unjust to those who turned up, many of whom had travelled from the outer limits of the boundary. Any way it was held with teams reduced to 3 a side, enabling 3 teams to start, Belgrave were the only team to start 4, but within a mile Paul Warburron was on the side-lines, having discovered that some walkers cannot cope with slippery surface. So it was left to Richard Tanner to not only bring home the team but to win overall with John Hall 2nd and Doug Fotheringham 5th. (The latter both did times faster than in the Belgrave). So it was another win for Belgrave, much to the pleasure of the Wandsworth Mayor who presented the awards. Commiserations to Richard Dorman who, having travelled down from Nottingham the previous evening, failed to make Battersea from Wimbledon due to train cancellations. 1.R.Tanner 79.41; 2.J.Hall 83.14; 3.N.Carmody (C.H.) 85.33; 5.D.Fotheringham 87.48. Team: 1.BELGRAVE 8; 2.Cambridge H. 25; 3.Ilford 30. In the Ladies 5kms, again a reduced field, Gail Porter finished 4th in 29.46. Fortunately the course used was virtually snow free and if more courses could be found that are as traffic free some of our races would not be having the problems that they are. Belgrave's turnout was not too hot, a complete change of team to that which won the London 10 miles, but this time with Steyning out in force we had little chance, but a late burst from Carl Lawton helped us into 2nd place with John's Newnham and Dunsford (the latter with an arm in plaster) pulling their weight. 1.J.Ball (Soton) 73.28; 4.C.Lawton 76.47; 9.J.Newnham 82.12; 20.J.Dunsford 90.59; Team: 1.Steyning 15; 3.BELGRAVE 30; 3.Dawlish 31. In the Essex the first three were all 'old Lags' who have been competing for 16 to 20 years. Surrey had two youngsters there, but Middlesex had only one newcomer. items.s: DOUG FOTHERINGHAM'S SEASON Tribute to veteran walker Doug Fotheringham's season: team medals, two European veterans silver medals in Rome and the Veterans A.C. 5 mile Grand Prix. Doug Fotheringham, one of Belgrave's Super Vets has undoubtedly had one of his best seasons, in various races Doug has collected winning team medals, GLC, Southern 20 miles, Southern 20 Kms and Track Competition. In addition to this he won two Silver medals in the European Championships in Rome and as a result of the Veterans A.C. 5 mile meetings at Battersea during the summer, came away as overall Grand Prise winner. items.label: October 1985
items.sum: Ian Horton's review of the young athletes' season, in which the boys reached the 1981 five-year plan target of being the most successful Y.A. club in Surrey, with three team medals at the Surrey Championships.
items.s: YOUNG ATHLETES Ian Horton's review of the young athletes' season, in which the boys reached the 1981 five-year plan target of being the most successful Y.A. club in Surrey, with three team medals at the Surrey Championships. Last year I referred to the fact that we had completed the third term of a five year plan. I can now unveil the plan launched in 1981 in the knowledge that the boys have achieved that target this winter "to be regarded as the most successful Y.A. Club in Surrey". In 1981 this was ambitious as we had only 6 cross country runners in all age groups! But the most satisfying aspect is that 5 are still running and one of those has won an English Vest. A glance at the following will confirm the outstanding results recorded in the three leagues in all age groups. Then the perfect peak culminating in the Surrey Championships when we took Silver, Bronze and Gold Team Medals respectively, to confirm the best overall performance by any Surrey Club. Incidentally 'Belgrave Historians' have said this is the best result in the history of Belgrave. The athletes still credit their collective success to the Mars Bars, but all credit for this effort must go to the boys after many years of hard work and they are duly recognised in their respective sections. At the same time I know the boys would also wish to thank the increasing band of supporters, braving all weather conditions to make timely appearances around the course which strengthened everybodies resolve when the going got really tough. Also thanks to those who helped organise, transport and carry out co-operative duties. Not least appreciation to Rosemary for 100% attendance, recognised as the number pinning, track suit hanger, Mars Bar Lady. Thanks to every body, above all to the boys who made this season the most enjoyable yet. And for the future - readers can be confident we have amended our plan. IAN HORTON Ian Horton IAN HORTON Rosemary Rosemary 100% attendance; number pinning, track suit hanger, 'Mars Bar Lady' Surrey Cross Country Championships

MINI COLTS The efforts of these youngsters force their own place of recognition. In preparation to receive the mantle from the successful Colts for next season there are no faint hearts in this squad. Battling on the often bleak Epsom Downs they took second place in the League. A special note of Babs Khan and Teddy Davies for their consistently high performances, also rapidly improving Reece Wilkins and Stewart Booth. Welcome to Neil Webster and Ben Brown who clearly showed talent that will make next season exciting. Also a special mention to Ben Cooper who, as our youngest runner (8), closed the team at the Ranelagh Open to secure his first ever Team Medal and with three more years as a Mini-Colt certainly not the last. 10th NOVEMBER 1984 SUTTON & CHEAM OPEN 1 MILE (4 to score) 1.R.Fletcher (Reigate) 6.15; 9.B.Khan 6.50; 20.T.Davies 7.07; 47.S.Booth 7.42; 56.G.Cox 7.54. items.s: COLTS Colts section of the young athletes' review: their best season, with the Downs League and a third successive Surrey League title, Surrey Championships silver, 5th in the Herne Hill League, and 1984-85 cross country results. COLTS Predictably the Colts had by far their best season with four of the squad representing their county in the Inter-Counties. Very early signs of their imminent success showed at the Collingwood Open when they finished a close 3rd to Woking and Shaftsbury. They went on to win the Downs League with Matthew Egerickx taking the individual title. Frankly it must be said there was little opposition to the Colts taking the Surrey League title for the third consecutive year. So to the best day in the Bels Y.A. history when at the Surrey Championships this squad ran out of their skins to take the Silver close behind Woking with all 4 scorers in top 15. They finished 5th in the Herne Hill League, which is generally recognised as one of the highest quality leagues in the south. Congratulations to Matthew, Steven, Alexander, Aaron, Dan W., Robert, all gaining representative honours. 13th OCTOBER 1984 WIMBLEDON COMMON SURREY LEAGUE (1) 2¼ MILES (5 to score) 1.E.Barker (Ranelagh) 16.51; 2.A.Ross 17.05; 3.S.Lambert 17.14; 4.A.Bacon 17.44; 6.D.Winson 18.14; 7.B.Ambrose 18.19; Also ran 8.D.Parr; 11.B.Khan; 12.M.Harrod; 18.T.Davies. items.s: BOYS Boys section of the young athletes' review: a young squad that won the Downs League, took Surrey Championships bronze and won the Ranelagh Open, with 1984-85 cross country results. BOYS The Boys were expected to struggle as a consequence of virtually all the regular runners being in their first year. Their character was under-estimated as any concern proved unjustified by the results. Due mainly to some superb runs by Duncan Ward, consistently supported by David Ashford. Gareth Allison also Dean Cunningham and the notable improvement of Nadir Khan and Saul Herbert. These combined to take the Downs League Title, eighth in the Herne Hill League and Bronze Medal in the Surrey Championships, with a superb individual second place by Duncan Ward (robbed of the title by some indifferent marshalling when he was sent off course while leading, but to go on to take 18th place in the Southern Counties. The boys closed their season with a clear victory in the Ranelagh Open. items.s: YOUTHS Youths section of the young athletes' review: a mainly first-year squad that won the Surrey Championship team title, took Herne Hill League bronze and 2nd in the Ranelagh Open, with 1984-85 cross country results. YOUTHS This squad reached the level of achievement expected of them this season. Coincidentally as with the boys shouldering the imbalance of being predominantly a 'first year team' (it was hardly noticeable!) Even so, I do not overlook the invaluable contribution John Booth made, especially early season. Welcome also to Graham Adams and Simon Maynard, too late to effectively strengthen the squad, but a glance at the December 8th Surrey League result showed what is possible. Good luck to these three next season as Juniors. The most significant team result was stealing a highly contested Surrey Championship title with a fine individual 4th from Garry McGurren, backed by Matthew Kinane (flying in from Switzerland hours before), Simon Beaumont and Glynn Tiernan. Not to be outdone the 'B string' runners showed consistent form to nail the Bronze in the Herne Hill League, largely from the efforts of Matthew Smith, Adam Horton and Robert Mann. It was not surprising that the same trio together with Brian Carlton should also take 2nd place in the Ranelagh Open. items.sum: New members welcomed: profiles of Simon Smith, Graham Adams, Simon Maynard and Steven Webster, four athletes who moved from Mitcham A.C. in late 1984, with photos.
items.s: NEW MEMBERS WELCOMED New members welcomed: profiles of Simon Smith, Graham Adams, Simon Maynard and Steven Webster, four athletes who moved from Mitcham A.C. in late 1984, with photos. NEW MEMBERS WELCOMED SIMON SMITH: Aged 18 yrs. D.O.B. 18.8.66. Simons athletic interests encompass a number of disciplines and to encourage his wide base interest he came to Belgrave in December 1984 from Mitcham A.C. Personal bests include a 2710 Pentathlon score: 1.75 HJ; 5.37 LJ; 33m JT; 37.5 2kg Discus; 2.05' 800; 4.30.6 1500; 10.37 3000 S/C. He trains and competes regularly over the country and has a Surrey County Youth Team Bronze from Road Relays. The athletic energy demands being so high for simon it is most fortunate for his family that he is a 1st Commis Chef at the Royal Lancaster Hotel, Hyde Park a la carte Restaurant where he gets first class fare to match. GRAHAM ADAMS: Aged 16 yrs. D.O.B. 10.6.68. Graham is a young athlete of great potential with a range from 400H to Cross Country and Road. He joined Belgrave in December 1984, an ex Mitcham A.C. member. An excellent steeplechaser he won the Surrey Youth title in 1983 as a 14 year old. A favourite to retain the championship in 1984 he unfortunately had to miss the event, and the bulk of the track season, with a mystery virus condition effecting the blood. We have to look back to 1983 and to early 1984 for his best track and country performances. These include placing, 4th as a first year youth, in the county event and an excellent 71st in the National at Newark. 1983 Personal bests of 2.06.5 800; 4.19.8 1500; 9.16.6 3000 mark his existing potential, and his success over the steeplechase barriers is matched with useful prowess over 400H where he has notched 61 sec. SIMON MAYNARD: Aged 17 yrs. D.O.B. 8.12.67. Following a move from Mitcham A.C. in December 1984 Simon almost immediately showed his worth with a 3rd placing in the Surrey County Youths X.C. Champs at a time when training, which started late in November, pointed to only 90% readyness. February and March saw him fully fit but frustrated over his ineligibility to enter major events, such as Southerns and Nationals, owing to a first claim rule that keeps him off the Belgrave score sheet until 4.9.85. County vests at cross country and track, have been an annual bonus for a lad who has a superlative record in every age group, mini colt upwards. He is also a Steeplechaser of note with a County Youths Silver Medal in recognition. Best performances have so far come on the country and over the barriers, but he hopes to soon improve his 1984 3000 p.b. of 9.07 and expects in 1985 to get close to 2 min. for 800 and 4 min. at 1500. The following Cross Country season will be welcomed, particularly the prospect of high class team competition with his new friends at Belgrave. STEVEN WEBSTER: Aged 14 yrs. D.O.B. 27.5.70. Steve joined Belgrave in November 1984, the youngest of four athletes moving over from Mitcham A.C. A schoolboy at Wilsons he feels he is treading a familiar athletic path at a school that has produced the Paton brothers; Dave Swain (E & E); Aidrian Izatt (SLH) in recent years. There has been some early success including a win at the I.A.C. Cross Country (Crystal Palace) 1982: The year in which he ranked 4th in the U.K. 1500 Colts list. October 1983 saw him corner a small piece of athletic history when he became the youngest ever male recipient of a AAA Championship Gold medal. A member of the successful Mitcham A.C. team in the inaugural AAA Championship (at this age group) road relays at Sutton Park West Midlands, Steve entered the record books in some style recording the fastest anchor leg in the event, and 4th fastest overall. 1984 brought a sixth place in the SCAAA Boys 1500 final at Crystal Palace in a time of 4.20.63. He also posted a 9.19.3 3000 on a freezing late February evening at Crystal Palace. In the lead. Simon Maynard(l) & Graham Adams(r). Photo.Bill Laws. Steven Webster in the Surrey C.C.Champs. items.sum: Anecdote of Steven Webster's Capital Radio prize flight with Simon Maynard being called off for weather, after which Maynard won the club 5000m senior championship in a personal best.
items.s: Anecdote of Steven Webster's Capital Radio prize flight with Simon Maynard being called off for weather, after which Maynard won the club 5000m senior championship in a personal best. Back in May Steven won a Boys race in Battersea Park organised by Capital Radio. The prize was a trip in the Company's Flying Eye early morning traffic jam spotter plane. The only problem was the starting time - 6.30am. Anyway, it was too good to miss and as the prize included for a friend to go along also it was at 5.30 am that Steven and Simon Maynard set off with Jim Webster acting as chauffer. The destination was Levesden airport near Watford. Gale force winds and torrential rain looked as though they would provide a bumpy flight and it was with mixed feelings that the lads received the news that there would be a delay in proceedings. And so it went on. The flight would have to be another day. So back to south London and for Simon it was time to prepare himself for his first Club Championship - the 5000m Senior Champs at Battersea Park. And what a consolation! Yes the day turned out fine for Simon for he beat all our Seniors to win the 5000 in a personal best time of 15.21.6. items.h: IAN GILLEY SETS EXTRAORDINARY COLTS RECORDS
items.sum: Report on South African-born Ian Gilley's colts club records set during a summer stay in England, and even better marks since his return to South Africa.
items.s: IAN GILLEY SETS EXTRAORDINARY COLTS RECORDS Report on South African-born Ian Gilley's colts club records set during a summer stay in England, and even better marks since his return to South Africa. When the last issue of the Belgravian went to print we were aware that some good performances from our younger members had not reached the editorial office but we didn't realise that the missing marks put up by South African born Ian Gilley, during his stay in this country last Summer, were quite so remarkable. Well, Ian's father Rod has now provided us with a summary of Ian's English results. He competed in 17 colts events, all of which he won,2 youths events placing 2nd and 4th and 1 senior event, placing 3rd. His best performances amongst these were 100m-12.1, 200m-25.5, 400m-58.6 and Long Jump-5.08m - all of which established new club records. But apparently we hadn't seen anything, for, on his return to South Africa, Ian has recorded the following astonishing marks:- 9.90(80m) 12.0(100m) 18.04(150m) 24.6(200m) 56.6(400m) and 5.41(Long Jump)!!! Ian's family plan to bring him to the U.K. during the Summer of 1986 to compete in the Boys Age Group when doubtless we shall see more records tumble to this exceptional young man. items.s: DUNLOP YOUNG ATHLETES LEAGUE Jim and David Mote's review of Belgrave's 1985 young athletes season: the four Dunlop Young Athletes League matches (2nd at Battersea Park, Worthing and Redhill, 3rd at Ewell Court; 8th of 16 overall), victory in the H.A.C. Memorial Trophy at Battersea Park, the Thameside League, and tributes to leading young athletes. This was another year when we promised so much as a team but eventually had to be content with outstandingly consistent individual performances. Once again we suffered because we were unable to cover all events and to a degree this was caused by lack of control by management. We needed more helpers both in the lead up to matches and in management of the three sections on the day. However, we hope we will learn by our mistakes and they will not be repeated next year. I have been asked to take charge of the Young Athletes Section again next year and would welcome help in contacting athletes and organising them at matches. We have a considerable depth of talent in our section and it is up to us to make the best use of it. The season was to comprise of five matches, but in fact was reduced to four because the final meeting at Redhill was called off because the track was flooded. The following are short reports covering the four matches, highlighting the outstanding performances from these meetings. 12th MAY 1985 BATTERSEA PARK MATCH 1 In preparing for the opening meeting we were full of confidence in our ability to crush all opposition but were dismayed to realise on the day that the Surrey Championships were to start on the following day and for obvious reasons many of our middle-distance runners declined to compete. As some of these athletes also double up on field events we found ourselves with more gaps in our team. Nevertheless we were able to give a good account of ourselves and scored 28 wins, 13 seconds, 8 thirds and 4 other places leaving 24 events not covered and a consequent minimum loss of 24 points. This time 'A' level studies reduced our team and again we had to be content with second place. There were, however, two outstanding features in this match in that we won all but three track races A and B in the Boys and Youths teams, but missed out where we had no competitors and Festus Ogwuda cleared 14.17 metres in the Youths Triple Jump to win the Dunlop Award for the outstanding feat in the match. We were of course delighted that so many of our athletes were honoured by selection for their Districts, but it played havoc with our League team. Not downhearted the rest of the section competed with commendable spirit, doubling up wherever possible and achieving a very good result in the face of adversity. Special mention must be made of Festus Ogwuda who had competed in the morning session of the competitions at Crystal Palace and then made his own way to Redhill and arrived in time to add his considerable talent to the efforts of our depleted team. Nevertheless it was sad at the end of the day to find that we (who boast the fastest Youths 4x100 Relay Team in the South of England) had insufficient athletes available to enter a team in this event. Our achievements were 20 wins, 13 seconds, 8 thirds and 2 other places. We had no competitor in 34 events. THAMESIDE LEAGUE This very popular competition again gave our Boys & Colts plenty to aim for. As a team we did not have much success, but individually the athletes competed with great spirit and many surprised themselves with their achievements in events where they had not hitherto considered themselves accomplished. It was interesting to see middle distance runners hurdling, sprinters jumping, and nearly everyone having a try at the field events at one time or another. In summing up, having already mentioned the exploits of Festus Ogwuda. Mention must also be made of our Youths first choice sprint squad of Gavin Warr, Joe Minetti and Mark Dooley who competed whenever possible and were never beaten in the Young Athletes League sprints. When joined by Clive Gardner who is primarily a hurdler, but is also a class sprinter, they made up the relay squad that won the Surrey AAA, Youth 4x100m and ran the remarkable 44.9 at Ewell Court. Julian Mole also competed unstintingly providing valuable back up to Clive in the hurdles and Festus in the triple jump and taking over the 'A' competition when they were not available. Julian never missed a Young Athletes match and won every hurdles race and triple jump competition in which he competed 'A' and 'B'. Finally, I will commend one boy who competed in every match - Young Athletes and Thameside Leagues - always completed three events and stood by for the relay if required. I of course refer to our middle distance hammer and discus throwing hurdler - John Coy. Well done all of you, we look forward to another exciting season in 1986. items.s: ROAD AND COUNTRY Introduction to the Road and Country section reviewing a mixed 1984-85 cross country season, with Oliver Foote and Andy North the standouts. Like the Curate's egg the Cross Country season was good in parts, initially promising a lot with a win in the South of Thames Junior, but turning out to be a lame effort with only Oliver Foote in the Seniors and Andy North in the Juniors showing impressive improvements with high placings in the National CC Champs. Reports by Bill Laws. LEAGUE DIVISION 1 Match-by-match report and results of Belgrave's 1984-85 Surrey Cross Country League Division 1 season, in which injuries left the team 4th in the final table behind AFD, HHH and Ranelagh, avoiding relegation. With John Gladwin, Stu Paton and Gary Staines injured at various times through the winter we never turned out teams which could challenge the might of Aldershot. In the end we settled for avoiding relegation. Oliver Foote was on schedule to lead the individual championship but was on holiday for the last match. Notable improvements from Andy North, Martin Lake and Francis Ward. 13th OCTOBER 1984 WIMBLEDON MATCH 1 A very average start for our home fixture. items.s: UNIQUE RECORD WIN Report and results of Belgrave's record-breaking team win (16 points) in the South of the Thames Junior Cross Country Championship at Windsor on 10 November 1984, led by individual winner Oliver Foote. 10th NOVEMBER 1984 WINDSOR SOUTH OF THAMES - JUNIOR The South of the Thames 'Junior' Cross Country Championship is a senior event with barring conditions. Of our top men Pete Gilbey and Stuart Paton were not eligible. With Gary Staines injured we still felt we had enough fire power to worry the opposition. And so it turned out. Although the 5½ mile course was wet the stoney paths helped the faster track men to a good start and after 2 miles the 250 strong field was led by 4 Belgravians - Oliver Foote, Mark Sinclair, John Gladwin and Dave North, with Andy North and Francis Ward not far behind. Oliver opened up a gap from John with about 1 mile to go and won by 8 seconds followed by John, Mark in 6th and Dave 7th. The winning team's point score of 16 was the lowest ever beating the 19 pts record set by Belgrave in 1945 and the lads are now barred from this race. But the backing team could well repeat the victory next year with Andy North finishing a fine 13th and Francis Ward in 28th place. So a great day for Belgrave and Oliver having the satisfaction of adding his name to a cup with such greats as Chris Chataway (1949), Tim Johnson (1959), Dave Holt (1964), Pete Standing (1968), Dave Clarke (1977) and Roger Hackney (1978). items.s: SURREY COUNTY CHAMPS. Report and results of the Surrey County Cross Country Championships at Brockwell Park on 5 January 1985, where Oliver Foote took senior silver after Richard Partridge's disqualification, the seniors were 4th team and Andy North 5th junior. 5th JANUARY 1985 BROCKWELL PARK SURREY COUNTY CHAMPS. Richard Partridge and Bob Treadwell had their own private battle for first. Partridge won on the day but was later disqualified as it was found that his residential qualification was not yet valid - so Oliver gained Silver - our best performance since Gerry North's days. Our senior men's team looked good for Bronze but fell away over the last 2 miles. In the Juniors Andy North almost ran up to the form he had displayed in the Surrey league as he finished 5th to get a Surrey vest. Again the Juniors got 4th team and with a bit of luck could have got Silver. items.sum: Report on Belgrave's Surrey representatives at the 1985 Inter-Counties Cross Country at Braunceston Park, Leicester.
items.s: INTER COUNTIES Report on Belgrave's Surrey representatives at the 1985 Inter-Counties Cross Country at Braunceston Park, Leicester. Two weeks after the Surreys our County representatives travelled to Braunceston Park Leicester to contest the Inter-Counties. In the Senior race a few overseas competitors added a bit of spice while Steve Cram was running to a fine 6th place to confirm his new winter training programme. Oliver Foote finished 46th in 37.07 but not finding the snow and ice to his liking. In the Junior race Andy North proved he should have had a Surrey medal as he finished in 55th place with 33.27 to be the second Surrey Junior man home. In the Youth race Simon Maynard was well in the 20's but faded to 45th in 20.31 as his lack of winter preparation showed. But what a promising young man he looks. items.sum: Report and results of the 1985 National Cross Country Championships at Milton Keynes, where Oliver Foote was 59th senior and Andy North 20th junior.
items.s: OLIVER AND ANDY EXCEL Report and results of the 1985 National Cross Country Championships at Milton Keynes, where Oliver Foote was 59th senior and Andy North 20th junior. 3rd MARCH 1985 MILTON KEYNES NATIONAL C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP It was cold, wet and unbelievably muddy at Milton Keynes as nearly 2000 Senior runners tackled the toughest race of the winter season. Each season the field gets bigger and this year saw 194 teams completing the course with Belgrave managing 45th place. Mike Hayes again gave an indication that he is over illness as he moved steadily through while Dave North who had succumbed to 'flu the week before battled gamely through to finish. Martin Lake too ran brilliantly on a reported 30 miles a week training schedule. Leo Lyons missed the start! But pride of place went again to Oliver Foote. Not known to like muddy courses he had a battle royal with Karl Harrison (who was to feature so well in 10k Road Races in the summer) with Karl finishing in 56th place and Oliver in 59th. And as for the Juniors - what can you say of Andy North's run. While others sank to their knees Andy floated across the mud and reminded many of us who were fortunate to see his run of another great North of some 30 years earlier! His 14th in the Southern should have equated to around 60th in the National (indeed local rival Mark Slowikowski finished 65th) but Andy seems to do better the harder the race. And so it was 20th place and some well known scalps to his credit. items.sum: Report and results of the Cambridge Harriers road relay at Bexley on 17 March 1985, where Belgrave were third and Gary Staines ran the fastest time of the day.
items.s: CAMBRIDGE H ROAD RELAY Report and results of the Cambridge Harriers road relay at Bexley on 17 March 1985, where Belgrave were third and Gary Staines ran the fastest time of the day. 17th MARCH 1985 BEXLEY CAMBRIDGE H ROAD RELAY Mike Hayes was the only member of last year's bronze medal team to return to Bexley and it is a measure of our increasing strength that we again came third narrowly failing to pip Aldershot for silver. Gary Staines was eager to run leg 1 and it soon became clear that he is moving into excellent form as at 2 miles he stretched away to record 15.42 for this near 3½ mile course and in so doing ran the fastest time of the day. Andy North took over 16 seconds in the lead and ran 32 seconds faster than last year (he was in the 'B' team then) to hand over still 14 seconds clear. Junior, John Warren, showed that he has now overcome illness and injury to record an excellent 16.53 and kept us in contention as we slipped to 3rd place. Steve Smullen, who a week earlier had run a 1.57 800m, slipped further back to 4th, but Stuart Paton pulled us back with a useful 16.27. As Mike Hayes took off 51 seconds behind the second placed Aldershot man he waited to see if he would be caught by the clan following Windsor and Invicta men. Imagine the surprise as he came into view of the finish breathing down the neck of the Aldershot man. Alas his early effort proved too much. But we had some first class performances to look back on. Particularly noteworthy was Chris Millbank's 'B' team run following his previous days win in the 5¼. With a rejuvinated Belgrave Hall we were able to provide a worthy base for this year's race and it is to be hoped that we will be honoured with this event in the years ahead. Andy North proved fastest of the short leg runners with the amazing 53 year old Laurie O'Hara second best. On the long leg Oliver showed little sign of his previous days 10km p.b. while Mike Hayes again ran exceptionally well. items.label: October 1985
items.h: AND WHERE WAS THE CROSS COUNTRY CAPTAIN THIS WINTER ?
items.sum: Cross country captain Don Anderson's account of trekking to Annapurna base camp in the Himalayas after injury, being robbed on the descent and cycling and hitching back to Delhi.
items.s: AND WHERE WAS THE CROSS COUNTRY CAPTAIN THIS WINTER ? Cross country captain Don Anderson's account of trekking to Annapurna base camp in the Himalayas after injury, being robbed on the descent and cycling and hitching back to Delhi. Having not run for most of 1984, due to injury, I decided something positive was needed to "Bump start" my body back into action, so I chose to go trekking in the Himalayan mountains. This would be of little benefit for the road or track, but would be a good reminder of what hard work and endurance was all about. So off I set from Pakhora, a village in the valley, with tent, sleeping bag and back-pack weighing 26 kilograms, to Annapurna base camp, some 17,000 feet above sea level. Food and chlorinated water were essential items, as the area was rife with hepatitis, spinal meningitis and amoebic dysentery, not to mention sickness and diarrhoea; after all I was here to gain fitness not lose it. The first two days were a pleasant trek up to 3,000 feet, but the map I used was very inaccurate. It led me up the creek, so I scaled the mountainside in order to reach the village of Kanre, some 5,400 feet above sea level, to put me back on the right course. After that it was steady trekking to Tikedhunga. The paths were well used by donkey trains - the only means of transporting supplies to outlying villages but they carved the paths up making the going uneven and difficult. Back in the Khala valley it was nice to stop for a bath in the glacier fed river. It was cold, but certainly refreshed the parts that weren't often reached. Pressing on to the village of Shorepani, 9,300 feet above sea level, the snow settled on the tent at night and made the inside freezing. On to the village of Shanrung, which is above 10,000 feet. The view was breathtaking with the morning sun radiating the snow capped Annapurna peak and Machapuckhie (fish tail) mountains like forbidding gods. The next was the village of Chomrong, still climbing. By this time I was running short of time, so I decided to leave my kit at one of the lodges and run up to Annapurna base camp wearing only running kit. The view from the mountain was again breathtaking, and well worth the 5,000 mile trip. The adventure was by no means over, for during my descent to Kathmandu, I was robbed of my money and passport. The British Embassy refused to help me and so I had to resort to my own initiative to get back to Delhi, India. So I borrowed a bicycle and cycled hundreds of miles relying solely on local hospitality to provide me with food and accommodation. After some wheeling and dealing I crossed the border into India. From there to Delhi I hitched a lift on the footplate of a steam train, where we had tea and chapaties cooked on the train's boiler. The British High Commission in Delhi were more sympathetic to my cause and issued me with an emergency passport and lent me some cash whilst I waited for my flight to London. It was a very interesting trip, but in future, I shall limit my altitude training to Box Hill! Don Anderson Don Anderson Don Anderson cross country captain; injured most of 1984; trekked to Annapurna base camp. items.s: ALL TIME TOP 100 OVER THE 5 3/4 Steve Williams's updated list of the 100 fastest runs on the club's 5 3/4 mile road course, headed by Geoff North's 27.14 in March 1966. It is now over 10 years since the Belgravian reproduced the top 100 performances over our 5 3/4 mile road course. And there is good reason why this particular bunch of statistics has laid dormant for so long - there have been hardly any runs inside the 100th best mark of 10 years ago! In fact, just one run apiece from Messrs O'Hara, Weller, Stow, Duncan, Bicourt and Foote. So in case you didn't realise what represents a good run round the course, here is the list updated - perhaps we can anticipate a greater number of changes in the coming decade! Still shown are runs from the 50's from Charlie Walker, Pat Newell and Ron Linstead and, as you would expect, Laurie O'Hara retains the largest single share of the list with 15 runs. For your information, and to set a target for some of you, another list, showing the all time top 100 individuals, has been produced in preparation for publication in our centenary year. This includes all your old favourites - Tom Carter, Arthur Penny and Ted Stimpson to name a few - and the present 100th spot clocks at 29.50 - so get cracking if you're hovering on the 30 minute mark, items.s: 29TH WELLINGTON INTERN. RELAY Report and results of the 29th Wellington International Relay at Ostend on 31 March 1985, where a young Belgrave team finished third of 53 teams. 31st MARCH 1985 OSTEND 29TH WELLINGTON INTERN. RELAY For a variety of reasons only Dave Mote, Guy Sagar, Mark Sinclair and Derrick Williams of last years winning 12 made the return journey for this years International Relay held on the Wellington race-course at Ostend. We took the opportunity to "blood" the youngsters and new members. With Oliver Foote and Mike Hayes adding experience over the longer legs and superb runs from Steve Smullen and Mark Sinclair we finished in bronze position. A truly splendid performance in this elite company with Aldershot and Blackheath left trailing. Every run was impressive and it was great to see our new 400m squadies - Mike Bazire and Will Willson doing so well. Dave Mote looked as though he's over injury and attacked into gale force winds. Guy Sagar produced his usual gutty run- while Junior, Simon Maynard made a fine debut at this level of competition. The team was grateful for the vociferous encouragement from 13 loyal supporters who were rewarded with fine sunshine, but gale force winds which managed to suit a Hovercraft at Dover!! And thanks to Don Anderson. Forced to work nights he travelled over on the day of the race just to cheer on the team, and then rushed straight back well satisfied with our efforts. items.s: FRANCIS IMPROVES Note on Francis Ward's races in Ireland in 1985, including 12th of 500 at a Straffan 10k and fourth in the Irish Universities 10,000m in a track p.b. FRANCIS IMPROVES Francis Ward, back in Ireland for a 6 month University training course, used the opportunity to get in some high quality races. On March 24th at Straffan in a 10k Road Race he finished 12th out of a field of 500 in a creditable 32.49. Two months later in the 1985 Irish Universities Championships he lowered his track 10k p.b. to 31:33.2 just missing out on a bronze medal as he finished a tired but happy fourth. items.sum: Introduction to the issue's track and field section reviewing a record-breaking year, with a list of report writers.
items.s: TRACK AND FIELD Introduction to the issue's track and field section reviewing a record-breaking year, with a list of report writers. An eventful 12 months with many individual and team successes plus a considerable number of personal best performances. Almost all of our senior Club Records were under threat and several fell; with John Regis taking Ernest's 200m time, John Gladwin bettering his own 800m time, Ken O extended his discus record and Gary Staines became our first sub 4 minute miler. Ernest became our first AAA's track champ winning an exciting 100m in a year when he has given unstinting support to our British League Side. If you're of an excitable nature skip this Section ! Reports by:- Bob Bridges, Leo Coy, Steve Williams and Bill Laws. items.label: October 1985
items.h: INDOOR ROUND-UP - GREAT SPRINTING FROM ERNEST OBENG AND JOHN REGIS
items.sum: Steve Williams's review of the 1985 indoor season, led by Ernest Obeng's 6.63 60m club record and John Regis's AAA Under 20 200m win, with a UK all-time indoor 200m list.
items.s: INDOOR ROUND-UP - GREAT SPRINTING FROM ERNEST OBENG AND JOHN REGIS Steve Williams's review of the 1985 indoor season, led by Ernest Obeng's 6.63 60m club record and John Regis's AAA Under 20 200m win, with a UK all-time indoor 200m list. With the middle distance boys giving the indoor season a miss, it was mainly the sprinters who kept the Belgrave name to the fore on the boards in 1985. Ernest Obeng began what must be his most significant indoor campaign on 12 January at the Cosford Games when he sprinted to a fine p.b. over 60m - 6.68 - just shaded by the eventual European Champion, Mike McFarlane but ahead of some useful domestic competition in Watson, Asquith and Sharp. Phil Lovell was another Belgravian in 2nd place with a 4.70 pole vault behind Jeff Gutteridge. Two weeks later, Ernest lined up again at Cosford to defend his AAA's title. Amongst those alongside him were McFarlane again and Desruelles of Belgium and although he was away as well as these two, he lost out in the pick up from 30 metres and had to be content with the bronze medal. Nevertheless his time of 6.71 was still faster than he had run prior to this season. Mike Alleyne had also travelled up for this event and recorded 7.18 in the heats. Unfortunately, Phil Lovell no heighted in the vault this time. Ernest then departed for a short visit to the continent and took advantage of the better indoor surface at Sindelfingen, W.G., where, on 1st February, he won the 60m event in a fabulous new club record of 6.63 which is one of the fastest times ever in the World - the third fastest by a Commonwealth athlete before McFarlane's European run! Two days later Ernie backed this up with a 6.65 at Karlsruhe. Great sprinting! The Juniors next took the stage at Cosford on 17 March at the AAA Under 20 Championships and more medals fell to the claret and gold as our new sprinter, John Regis, demonstrated some real quality with a tremendous victory at 200m in a CBP of 21.93, which is some sprinting round the tight bends of an indoor track. In fact, this run placed John as the 8th fastest ever UK indoor performer! John had previously placed 2nd in the 60m championship in 6.90 and although 200m seems his specialist distance we can anticipate some good things from him over 100m as well. Phil Goedluck, in his first year as a Junior recorded 7.07 and 22.63 in the heats, which made him the fastest 17 year old, and Phil can look forward to two more attempts at these titles! At the other end of the age range, our 'new' Vet, Snowy Brooks, was in good form at the British Veterans Championships held at Cosford on 23 March. Snowy won the 60mH in 9.3 and the Long Jump in a new UK Best performance of 6.14. He also placed 5th in the 60m in 7.8 (7.7ht) and recorded 25.4 in the heats of the 200m. items.sum: Round-up of Belgrave early-season track bests in spring 1985, led by Michael Allayne's sprinting and Mark Sinclair and Mike Hayes in the steeplechase.
items.s: EARLY BIRDS Round-up of Belgrave early-season track bests in spring 1985, led by Michael Allayne's sprinting and Mark Sinclair and Mike Hayes in the steeplechase. EARLY BIRDS Following several low key performances last summer it seemed as though Michael Allayne was approaching the 1985 Track and Field season with renewed enthusiasm. We first spotted his 7.18 sec. 60m effort in the 1985 AAA's Cosford Indoor Champs. This was soon followed by an excellent 35.1 300m at an open meeting at Dartford. In March he ran a p.b. 49.5 sec 400m at an open meeting at the Crystal Palace and it is in this event that his many Belgrave fans believe he has the greatest potential. A sub 48.0 this season is a real possibility. Other impressive early season results are to hand. Several Belgravians have notched up p.b's which indicate a fine year ahead for many of our established Stars. On the 20th April at Battersea Park, Mark Sinclair ran his first 2000 S/C and won in 5.54.8 closely followed by Mike Hayes in 5.57.7. Four days later Mike won a Southern Counties Match 3000 S/C at Crystal Palace with a huge p.b. in 9.03.9 while the following Saturday Mark won the Surrey 3000 S/C in 9.12.0 at the Croydon Arena 'dust bowl'. Oliver Foote and David North - our mainstays for the British League 5000m - confirmed early season form with p.b's of 8.17.3 and 8.26.6 at the Southern Counties match while a week later in a graded meeting Mark Sinclair also ran a p.b. 3000 in 8.20.1. While this was going on 16 year old Graham Adams ran 60.7 for the 400H - again a big p.b. while 20 year old John Warren lowered his 3000 p.b. to 8.37.2. items.sum: Note that Belgrave were awarded the 1984 Nike Blackheath 25 x 1 mile relay after Sale's disqualification, with Gary Staines fastest in 4.06, and a call for runners for 22 September.
items.s: NIKE BLACKHEATH H 25 x 1 MILE - 1984 Note that Belgrave were awarded the 1984 Nike Blackheath 25 x 1 mile relay after Sale's disqualification, with Gary Staines fastest in 4.06, and a call for runners for 22 September. NIKE BLACKHEATH H 25 x 1 MILE - 1984 The official results of the 1984 25 x 1 Mile Relay were a long time coming and with good reason. After extensive debate between Blackheath and sponsors Nike, Sale were disqualified from 1st spot as a result of some runners competing without Club vests while others were paced. As a result Belgrave repeated their 1983 victory and the winning team each received a pair of Nike Transit trainers while Gary Staines, who recorded the days fastest time with 4.06 also won a pair of spikes. With so many up and coming youngsters it should take 4.35 to make the team this year. The date is Sunday, September 22nd at Crystal Palace and a UK record by Belgrave is on the cards if everyone turns out. Gary Staines Gary Staines fastest time of the day, 4.06 Blackheath 25 x 1 Mile Relay Crystal Palace Blackheath Sale

items.label: October 1985
items.sum: Introduction to the 1985 Southern League season, thanking the 68 athletes who competed and noting club records by Andy North and Glynn Tieoran.
items.s: SOUTHERN LEAGUE ROUNDUP Introduction to the 1985 Southern League season, thanking the 68 athletes who competed and noting club records by Andy North and Glynn Tieoran. SOUTHERN LEAGUE ROUNDUP First of all, I would like to thank all those who turned out in the Southern League this season, all 68 of them ! I think this proves that we are giving as many people as possible competition at this level. With the strong likelihood of a 'C' team next season there is room for even more. So never think you are not good enough. We try to fit every one in somewhere and don't forget there are non scoring races at 200m and 1500m at every meeting. A look through the results will show who did what and where and quite a few of the 'A' team will be looking over their shoulders at the quality of some of them. Those that stand out are the two club records that were set; Andy North's junior 5,000 record of 14:55:8 at Battersea on 25th May and Glynn Tieoran's 1500 youth record of 4:02:8 also at Battersea on 3rd August. There were also a host of p.b.'s set throughout the season. So with a few more people willing to travel to away matches and prepared to "race" on cinder, we may have two teams in their respective premier divisions in our centenary year. items.s: Full-page photograph by David Cocksedge of Gary Staines winning the Southern Counties 1500m title, with a caption on his 1985 season. Photo: David Cocksedge. Gary Staines seen here winning the Southern Counties 1500m title became our first sub-4 minute miler and ended a race packed season when in September he joined John Gladwin on an under 23 tour of mainland China. Gary also ranked 12th in the world with his 5.02.57 2000m. items.s: SIMON MAYNARD'S FIRST TITLE Report and results of the club championships at Battersea Park on 8 May 1985, where 17-year-old Simon Maynard won the 5000m on his debut at the distance. SIMON MAYNARD'S FIRST TITLE 8th MAY 1985 BATTERSEA PARK CLUB CHAMPIONSHIP Our first Club Championship of the season coincided with the 40th Anniversary of VE day and for 17 year old Simon Maynard his 5000m debut turned into a dream. Showing great maturity he sat on the leaders throughout taking the lead only in the finishing straight as he eventually overcame the strength of Martin Lake while the first five home all recorded p.b's. The supporting events were all well attended. In the 800 John Booth looked impressive as he followed Steve Smullen through the bell in 56 secs and also recorded a p.b. In the throws Ken, Tony Featherstone and Mike Small came together for the first time confirming our growing strength in the field events. 5000m: 1.S.Maynard (J) 15:21.6; 2.M.Lake 15:22.4, 3.L.Lyons 15:37.5; 4.D.Clack 15:42.0; 5.C.Millbank 15:46.0; 6.E.Boytler 15:47.0; 7.M.Donahue 16.01; 8.M.Bizio 16.08; 9.B.MacRae 16.29; 10.L.Coy 16.50, 11.E.Bird 17.06; 12.A.Pollit 17.11; 13.D.Maughan 17.26; 14.C.Howard 17.35; 15.A.Stone 17.36; 16.A.Grant 17.46; 17.S.Smith 17.56; 18.T.Eden 18.00; 19.R.Bale 18.05; 20.L.Mclean 18.06; 21.J.Rayner 18.55; 22.L.Mann 19.01; 23.D.Davies 19.13; 800m 'A': 1.S.Smullen 1:55.7; 2.J.Booth (Y) 1:58.3; 3.A.Painter 2:01.0; 4.S.Williams 2:03.0; 5.K.Green 2:03.0; 6.A.Gayton 2:03.1; 7.M.Leeson 2:03.9; 8.D.North 2:06.0; 800m 'B': 1.P.Halliday 2:02.7; 2.M.Johnson 2:04.0; 3.A.North 2:05.8; 4.A.Ludlow 2:08.6; 5 - 2:10.3; 6.B.Hall 2:15.4; DT: 1.K.Onuaguluchi 51.34; 2.A.Featherstone 43.76; 3.M.Small 41.46; 4.M.Hill 35.82. items.s: SURREY COUNTY CHAMPIONSHIPS (PART 2) Report and Belgrave results from part two of the Surrey County Championships at Motspur Park on 13-18 May 1985, highlighted by Glyn Tiernan's championship best in the youths 1500m. 13-18th MAY 1985 MOTSPUR PARK SURREY COUNTY CHAMPIONSHIPS (PART 2) With several members chosing not to compete we were nonetheless splendidly represented with a host of medals. Mark Sinclair failed by a whisker to win the 1500m where heats and final were run within 2 hours due to the earlier heats being washed out. Mark Shippen finally got it together in the pole vault. Derrick Williams showed some impressive speed and looks set for a best ever season. Oliver Foote too surprised with a fast last 800m in the 5000 being recorded at 57 secs for the final 400m as he gained a silver in a p.b. But pride of place must go to the Youths with Gavin Warr clocking a fine 23.1 in the 200m final and Glyn Tiernan breaking a 15 year old Championship Best Performance to win the Youths 1500m by a huge margin. (Historians may note that the previous record was held by none other than Belgrave's Bill Custin who ran 4:07.1 in 1970). items.s: BRITISH LEAGUE - DIVISION 3 RESULTS - MATCH 1 Report and results of British League Division 3 match 1 at Enfield on 11 May 1985, where Belgrave finished second, two points behind WSE. BRITISH LEAGUE - DIVISION 3 RESULTS 11th MAY 1985 ENFIELD MATCH 1 With last years visit to Enfield in mind - bad weather and a third place - we hoped that both would improve in this the first match in Division 3. Sadly, the weather was much worse, but our performances warmed everybody as we achieved a solid second place - having led Windsor by two points with one relay to go! Bels had eight individual wins - Ernest, having been caught by St. Louis in the 100, won the 200, Stuart and Gary had fine double wins in the 800, Mark Sinclair outkicked the field to win the 1500 and he was backed up well by Steve Smullen, who won the 'B' event. Pete Gilbey won the 'B' S/C, having avoided the elbow to elbow tactics of Large (S & E) and Mike Hayes. Ken won the discus in very unfavourable conditions and our 4x100 team had a comfortable win. Mike Bazire and Tony Featherstone made their BAL debuts, in a very satisfactory start to the season. items.s: MATCH 2 Report and results of British League Division 3 match 2 at Windsor on 1 June 1985, where Belgrave were third after being pipped by Windsor in the last relay. 1st JUNE 1985 WINDSOR MATCH 2 Glorious weather was the order of the day at Windsor and hopes were high of a repeat of last years fine win. Unfortunately Southampton and Windsor turned out very strong teams and we had to be content with third place. We again headed Windsor by two points with just the last relay left and they again managed to pip us at the post. Ernest, thought that he had nicked the 100 from Todd Bennett as they crossed the line together, but the S & E man was given the verdict. Gary almost caught the England Captain on the line in a fine 800 metres race. Stuart won the 'B' event and John Regis made his BAL debut by winning the 'B' 100, but unfortunately an injury kept him out of the short relay, despite this the 4x100 team equaled the Club Record. In the Long Jump Derrick Williams led the field with a good 7.15 metres and he also won the 'B' TJ. Ken again triumphed in the discus and almost sneaked a win in the shot. Will Willson, Dave Catling, Leo Lyons and Nigel Clarke competing in the BAL for the first time, all performed exceptionally well. items.sum: Report and results of British League Division 3 match 3 at Brighton on 30 June 1985, which Belgrave won by half a point to go top of the division.
items.s: MATCH 3 Report and results of British League Division 3 match 3 at Brighton on 30 June 1985, which Belgrave won by half a point to go top of the division. 30th JUNE 1985 BRIGHTON MATCH 3 At the half way stage in the League, the promotion battle was between Windsor, Bels and Southampton while Enfield, Brighton and local rivals HHH all had to fight to avoid the drop. Brighton, the home club had never finished lower than second in all their previous home BAL Matches. Southampton were getting their act together following their win at Windsor and WSE were determined to keep their lead at the top of Div.III. It promised to be a great day and that is how it turned out. We were always in the first three throughout the afternoon and did not lead until very late. Our double wins in the 5000 (Olly and Mark both with p.b's) and the Pole Vault (Phil and Mark) pushed us into the lead that we did not lose although it was very close with just ½ a point between Southampton and ourselves after an exciting final relay. Enfield did us a favour by tying with Windsor and this resulted in the Bels heading Div.III after a memorable day. Individual performances that should be mentioned are Mark Lindsay-Bayley who filled in for Derrick Williams in the Triple after Derrick had injured himself in the first round of the Long Jump. Derrick was also a key member of the Relay team and Aham volunteered to run in his place and he also had a go at the High Jump! Andy Paton came along as a spectator and in borrowed gear ran a storming first leg in the Long Relay. Mike Bazire pushed himself to the limit as he gave all in both relays. With this tremendous team spirit we won a match where we could have easily finished third. The other heroes of the day were the throwers - they really excelled. Mike Small in his first BAL Match for us had a great afternoon. Ken threw the hammer for the first time and Tony Featherstone threw 46 metres in the discus, to get a p.b. by a large margin. Ernest broke Peter Radfords ground record in the 100 and left Todd Bennett for dead as he scorched to a fine win. MLB and Dave Sheldon ran p.b's in the Long Hurdles and Alan Benn made his debut in the BAL. items.sum: Report and results of British League Division 3 match 4 at Southwark Park on 10 August 1985, won by Belgrave with 256 points and a club and league record 41.1 in the 4x100 relay.
items.s: MATCH 4 Report and results of British League Division 3 match 4 at Southwark Park on 10 August 1985, won by Belgrave with 256 points and a club and league record 41.1 in the 4x100 relay. 10th AUGUST 1985 SOUTHWARK PARK MATCH 4 This last match was switched from Tooting and despite protests was held at Southwark Park. The afternoon got off to a stormy start as most of the vaulters refused to take part as the conditions were dangerous. The match followed the same pattern as before with the Bels never out of the first three and we took the lead with just a few events to go. It turned out to be a memorable day for the Club and its many supporters - they drowned the other teams supporters with their noise. Our throwers were again magnificent - out of eight events they recorded 4 wins, 3 seconds and a third place. It was good to see Vincent Cornibert again and he certainly shook-up the Javelin competition. 16 year old Graham Adams came into the team at the last minute and ran really well to finish 3rd in the 'B' 800. Tom Taylor also made his BAL debut for us and had two splendid second places. Chris Cornwell equalled the Club Record and became our first 2.00 High Jumper in BAL Competition. Another performance that went unnoticed was that of Derrick Williams in the Triple Jump. Both he and Aham were struggling below their best when with one jump left he produced a magnificent 14.75 to completely change the points position for the event. Pride of place must go to the 4x100 Relay team who recorded a new Club and Div.3 League record with a spectacular 41.1 with a good second in the 4x400 Relay it rounded off a marvellous afternoon for the Club. Our winning points score of 256 was the highest of the 4 matches despite the absence of the pole vault result in which we normally amass around 20 points. items.s: From Brian Pritchard Letter from Brian Pritchard congratulating the club on winning British League Division 3 and thanking team managers Leo Coy and Bill Laws. LETTERS From Brian Pritchard I would like to congratulate the Club on their achievement of winning Division 3 of the British League. Having followed our team very closely during the past five years, I believe our rise in consecutive seasons from Div.5 to Div.2 is quite remarkable considering the very high standard of the British League. I would firstly like to congratulate the team on their superb achievement and in the way they have responded when asked to turn out for the Club, and secondly to thank Leo Coy and Bill Laws for the magnificent way they have managed the team, and I can not think of anyone else who could have done the job as well. I look forward to next season with anticipation. I am sure I speak for all the supporters who have turned up at the meetings, in wishing the team, Leo and Bill the best of luck for next year. Brian Pritchard Brian Pritchard Leo Coy Leo Coy British League team manager Leo Coy Leo Bill Laws Bill Laws British League team manager Bill Laws Bill British League

items.sum: Letter from Derrick Williams describing a day in Watford filming a long jump coaching video with Lyn Davies, with a photo of him jumping.
items.s: From Derrick Williams Letter from Derrick Williams describing a day in Watford filming a long jump coaching video with Lyn Davies, with a photo of him jumping. From Derrick Williams As promised a few lines about my latest filming exploits. The saga starts one Friday morning, going about my usual days work when I received a 'phone call from Jim Alford who wanted to know if I was available for a few days, as they were in the process of making a series of videos for coaching consisting of all the events in track and field. My involvement was slightly different in that with the other video they had an experienced athlete e.g. Seb Coe, David Hemery etc. to both demonstrate and talk about the techniques involved in their events, but I came into the story because for the long jump they had Lyn Davies who was quite able to coach, but because of a long-standing injury didn't feel able to run and jump. So a replacement was called for. Not being able to get an exact double they searched for the next best thing - a tall very handsome and capable athlete. But failure again left them with just one option ... me. So my day began at seven thirty a.m. Taxi to wisk me off to the film location which was not L.A. as I had hoped, but sunny Watford. Arrived at around 8.45 a.m. and met everyone involved; the director Tony Maylam who made the "Super Milers", the film crew, Lyn Davies and the young athletes who were all still at school. The day began with Lyn breaking down the preparation for any session, warm up stretching, drills etc. Then with the aid of the youngsters he did the approach run, take off, movement through the air and landing. All the youngsters performed very well. They were of different standards which was lucky as they showed common faults any beginner would have. By 3 o'clock they had done the maximum work their tired bodies would allow. So I was told to make ready for my entrance. I had been sitting to one side up to this point watching and learning all the little points Lyn Davies mentioned. I was supposed to be the finished article, with the technique the youngsters should hope to one day emulate, so for the next three hours I was running flat out and jumping into a pit littered with camera men and equipment. They were filming with three different cameras so I was at it time after time after time and at around 6 o'clock I was wondering how much longer when those magic words sung out "Just one more take Derrick". I thought we'll have to make this a good one. So using my 'fabled speed" I sprinted to the board and launched myself high into the air and to the horror of the camera men landed less than six inches from the cameras sending sand over everyone. Thankfully they saw the funny side. And so ended a memorable days work, very hard but also very rewarding, meeting Lyn Davies was an honour. With best wishes to all. Jumping With style! Derrick Williams immaculate technique has now been captured in a series of coaching videos made for the I.F.A. which is to be distributed to over 140 Countries.
