items.s: THE STEVE WILLIAMS' ROUND-UP Steve Williams's round-up of Belgrave international, championship and representative performances in 1985, including Ernest Obeng's AAA 100m title, Gary Staines's first sub-4-minute mile by a Belgravian and John Regis's European Junior medals. THE STEVE WILLIAMS' ROUND-UP ROUND-UP OF THE BEST OF BELS INTERNATIONAL, CHAMPIONSHIP AND REPRESENTATIVE PERFORMANCES As has become usual in recent years, we were well represented in the early SCAAA matches at Crystal Palace. On 24 April, Olly Foote (8.17.3) and Dave North (8.26.5) ran pb's over 3000m while Mike Hayes placed 2nd in the 'chase in 9.03.9, also a fine pb; Phil Lovell won the Pole Vault at 4.80 and Ken Onuaguluchi placed 2nd in the Discus with 51.34. On 1 May, Stu' Paton was 2nd over 800m in 1.53.5, Mark Sinclair 2nd in the Southern 'Standards' 3000m in a pb of 8.20.1, and Phil again won the vault with 4.80 and, this time, Ken, the Discus with 49.88.// AAA's representative vests were won by four Bels on 15 May at C/Palace where John Regis won the 200m in 21.8, Gary Staines was 4th over 1500m in 3.47.5, Mark Sinclair 6th in the 2km 'chase in 5.57.2 and Phil Lovell 3rd in the Vault again at 4.80.// On 21 May Stuart Paton was over in Norway where he ran what turned out to be a seasons best 1500m in 3.48.57. * * * UK Championships - Antrim - 25/26 May - JOHN REGIS shares 200m title:- A trip over the Irish Sea paid handsome dividends for John Regis, Gary Staines and Phil Lovell who all collected medals. John brought home Gold from his dead heat with Linford Christie in the 200m in a magnificent 21.59 (club jnr. rec.) despite carrying a hamstring problem, and backed this up with Silver in the 100m in 10.5, also a club jnr. rec. A feature of John's running was his remarkable finishing speed. Gary took Bronze in the 1500m in a typically gutsy run (3.44.22) and Phil found his consistency at 4.80 bringing Silver in the vault - a fine performance in miserable conditions. Also competing were Mike Hayes - 9.12.4 for 14th in the 'chase and Stu' Paton 3.54.17 in the 1500m heats. * * * At the Glasgow Games on 9 June, Ernie Obeng held off Sharp and Watson over 100m in 10.3 and, representing Loughbro' against AAA's, three days later, won at 100m in 10.45w and placed 2nd over 200m in 21.22w. * * * SCAAA Championships - C/Palace - 14/15 June - GARY STAINES wins 1500m:- Our highlight was undoubtedly Gary's win in the 1500m. It was his first major championship outdoors and his determined final 200m in a closing lap of 56.9 showed improved finishing. Well done Gary. Medals were also won by Stu' Paton - close to his best time over 800m but too far off the pace when the winner jumped the field; Phil Lovell, 3rd in the Pole Vault and Ken Onuaguluchi 2nd in the Discus - a medal in these championships is becoming a nice habit for these two. Results:100m D Williams 11.15ht 200m M Alleyne 22.47ht, P Lyttle 23.03ht 400m G Sagar 52.30ht 800m 3rd S Paton 1.49.03, 5th J Gladwin 1.50.35(1.49.85sf), N Clarke 1.55.39ht-pb 1500m 1st G Staines 3.42.89 5000m O Foote 14.53.26 3000mSc 12th M Hayes 9.14.54 PV 3rd P Lovell 4.80 LJ 8th D Williams 7.03 TJ 10th A Amadi 14.34 SP 6th K Onuaguluchi 14.89pb DT 2nd K Onuaguluchi 54.56. * * * On 21st June, JOHN REGIS became the latest Belgrave International when selected to run 200m against the USA at Birmingham. This was something of a firey baptism for an athlete still a junior and John should not be too unhappy with his 6th place (21.68) in company which included the Olympic Bronze medallist, the World Silver medallist and a 20.07 performer in the US team! *** GARY STAINES ran 3.44.77 in Poland on 24 June. *** On 30th June, STUART PATON was an International winner for Scotland against Ireland and Catalonia, using that great acceleration to swamp Paul Forbes amongst others in the 800m in 1.50.97.*** At the World Veterans Championships in Rome at the end of June, SNOWY BROOKS was a match for the best with a Silver Medal in the Long Jump (6.42) and Bronze in the Pentathlon (3475 pts). * * * Surrey v Army v Hants - Aldershot - 3 July: 3000mSc 5th M Sinclair 9.24.0; 110mH 3rd T Taylor 15.3, 5th M Lindsay-Bayley 15.4; PV 1st P Lovell 4.60; LJ 1st T Taylor 6.99; TJ 1st A Amadi 14.42; SP 3rd D Dawson 14.18, 4th P McKay 14.15. * * * English Schools Championships - Hull - 12/13 July:- Snr Boys 200m 2nd M Adams 21.9(21.6sf) 5th P Goedluck 22.3(22.1sf): Inter Boys 200m G Warr 23.0sf TJ F Ogwuda 13.57qual. ERNEST OBENG AAA'S CHAMP. AAA Championships - C/Pal - 13/14 July - ERNEST OBENG 100m CHAMPION:- Third in 1978, second in 1981 and now first in 1985, Ernest Obeng has become only the second Belgrave runner to win a Senior AAA title by taking the 100m championship this year (his only predecessor being Bill Nankeville who won the Mile in 1948). Coming comfortably through his heat and semi-final in 10.51 and 10.42 respectively, Ernie looked an obvious medal prospect, although the American 10.10 performer, Darwin Cook, who had already beaten Ernie in the Ulster Games, must have been favourite. And it was Cook who got the best start in the final with Ernie, suprisingly one of the last away. So with what is usually the best part of Ernie's race over, observers could have been forgiven for thinking our man would be run out of it - but, maintaining his form wonderfully through the last 20 metres in a storming finish, Ernie just edged ahead when it counted. Only 5/100ths covered the first 5 across the line but Ernie was in no doubt he had made it, celebrating with one arm raised aloft as he ran through. Well done Ernest! The full result for posterity:-1st E OBENG 10.44; 2nd D Cook(USA) 10.45; 3rd Imoh(Nig) 10.46; 4th L Asquith 10.49; 5th B Watson 10.56; 6th D Reid 10.72 (McFarlane 10.46 disq.,Christie dnf) The wind was 1.4m/s against./// Our other top men in action were John Gladwin - first Briton home in the 800m in 5th place with 1.47.08, the start of a great series of runs from him, lasting to the end of the season; Gary Staines - a pb of 3.41.48 in qualifying for the 1500m final where he placed 10th in 3.44.45; Phil Lovell =8th in the Vault with 4.80 and Ken Onuaguluchi 6th in the Discus with 51.88. Also Mike Alleyne - 400m ht of 49.32 and Stuart Paton - 1.50.01 800m ht. * * * At the Peugeot Talbot Games at C/Pal on 19/20 July Ernest Obeng confirmed his AAA form with Imoh and Asquith, winning the 100m in 10.39 while John Gladwin was the winner of the 1000m from a good domestic field in 2.19.69. It was also at this meeting that we saw the FIRST SUB 4 MINUTE MILE BY A BELGRAVIAN when Gary Staines chased home Steve Cram in a time of 3.59.24. Stu' Paton ran 4.07.89. * * * Edinburgh Games-23 July:100m E Obeng 4th 10.48 * * * The Bislett Stadium again did the trick for JOHN GLADWIN, who reduced his 800m best to 1.46.11 in the process of winning the Oslo Games event on 27 July in a dip finish with Moussa Fall, following the disqualification of Mack. And John's verdict on the new surface is that it's not as fast as the old one! * * * At the Inter-Counties Championships held at Thurrock on 28 July, Ernie Obeng retained his 100m title from McFarlane in 10.9 into a strong wind as did Gary Staines in the Mile with 4.12.3. And, going one better than in the last two years, Ken Onuaguluchi made it a great Belgrave hat-trick by taking the Discus with a throw of 52.20. * * * At the IAC Grand Prix at C\Palace on 2 August, KEN ONUAGULUCHI just missed his own club record in the Discus with a fine throw of 55.18 in 4th place. * * * Budapest Grand Prix-4 Aug:Ernest Obeng maintained his good form with a 10.36 clocking behind Nagy and Lara, while John Gladwin ran what he admitted was probably his worst ever tactical race, placing 6th in 1.47.92. Then, over 2000m, there was an outstanding run not only from Steve Cram but also from Gary Staines who finished 6th in a remarkable 5.02.67, indicating that whatever Gary has achieved so far, he can surely reach greater heights over 3000m and 5000m eventually. * * * SCAAA v Comb. Serv. v Welsh AAA v Achilles - 7 Aug - C\Pal:3000mSc 3rd M Sinclair 8.56.9 - a great personal best from Mark who can make a big impact in this event. PV 1st P Lovell 4.90 - equals Phil's own club record. LJ\TJ T Taylor 1st\5th 7.43\14.37 SP\HT 4th\6th P McKay 13.91\46.54 DT 1st K Onuaguluchi 53.34. Kodak Classic - Gateshead -9 August:100m 2nd E Obeng 10.58;DT 3rd K Onuaguluchi 54.62 U\20 Inter County Match-11 August: Jnrs: 100m'B' 1st P Goedluck 11.2; 200m 1st M Adams 22.1;3000m 4th A North 8.50.7. Yths: 100m'B' 2nd G Warr 12.0; 200m'B' 5th M Dooley 23.8; 1500m 3rd G Tiernan 4.11.8; 3000m 7th M Kinane 9.14.7; TJ 4th F Ogwuda 13.50. * * * At the AAA's U\20 Championships in Birmingham, John Regis placed a magnificent 2nd over 100m in 10.46w (10.45w ht) a run which clinched his selection for the European Junior Championships. Equally impressive was Marcus Adams with 3rd over 200m in 22.08 into a 4.56w!! And, backing these two up, we had Phil Goedluck running his fastest ever times - 10.79w for 7th in the 100 (10.75w ht) and 22.40 for 6th in the 200m (22.12 ht). Fast Juniors indeed! Our promising Triple Jumper, Festus Ogwuda placed 5th in the Youths event with 13.62, a fine performance. * * * At a Nottingham Open Combined Events meeting on 17/18 August, Festus Ogwuda completed a Decathlon with Junior implements in a club record score of 5010 points. * * * Home Junior International-Meadowbank-21 Aug: 100m 1st J Regis 10.87 200m 1st M Adams 21.54 (This was a further improvement in the Club Junior Record and an amazing run from a 17 year old into an unhelpful headwind!) * * * In one of the best kept secrets of the Europa Cup Final weekend, England 'B' were taking on France in Le Touquet. John Gladwin won selection for the 800m where he had a comfortable win in 1.46.88.*** Ernest Obeng ran a season's best of 10.28 in Zurich on 21 August, going on to 7th in the final in 10.43. * * * European Junior Championships, Cottbus, East Germany - 22/25 August - "Ein Kurzstreckenlauf Fantastisch": Well, what can one say about an individual Bronze Medal and Relay Gold by JOHN REGIS at these Championships. No doubt most of you were watching on TV and saw the way he ate up the ground in the last 30 metres of the 100m to come through to 3rd place behind Elliot Bunney and Havas of Hungary, in another Club Junior Record, after a cautious start because of a still tender hamstring. It was a fabulous run in any circumstances let alone those but perhaps John was even better on the final leg of the 4x100m where he brought the team home to the Gold Medal in a new UK Junior record of 39.80! I believe he must have come close to the club high jump record with that leap in front of the UK team in the stands at the end!! * * * At Crystal Palace on 26 August, JOHN GLADWIN completely dominated an International 800m for England against Poland, Hungary and Czechoslovakia, leading all the way to a time of 1.47.77. What with a victory lap in front of the home crowd and signing autographs afterwards, this was an afternoon for him to savour. * * * Tooting Bec Re-Opening Meeting - 24 August: KEN ONUAGULUCHI 56.08 - ANOTHER CLUB RECORD Leading Bels results:- 400m'B' 3. M Alleyne 49.2; 800m 5. S Paton 1.52.1 1500m 1. G Staines 3.42.7; 3000m 3. O Foote 8.17.4; 3000mSc 3. M Hayes 9.17.4; 110mH 7. M Lindsay-Bayley 15.6 SP 6. K Onuaguluchi 14.97pb, 9. M Kinane 2.01.8 * * * Whistlestop 100's from Ernie: Koblenz-28 Aug-6th 10.52: Riccione-31 Aug-3rd 10.53: Rieti-4 Sept-3rd 10.39.*** On 15 Sept at C\Palace Phil Goedluck won over 100m at the U\20 Inter Area match in 11.03. * * * John Gladwin and Gary Staines brought their most successful seasons to a close on a short tour of China with the England U/23 team. In Beijing on 8 September, John won the 800m in 1.47.35 with the European Champion in his wake, while Gary won over 1500m in a tactical 3.51.15. Then, 3 days later in Nanjing, John completed a fine double in his second fastest time - 1.46.42 with Ferner again behind, while Mark Rowland, this time reversed placings with Gary in the 1500m, Gary clocking 3.54.10 in another slow race. OLIVER SOUTHERN 10 KM SILVER It was inevitable that when Oliver Foote found himself in a higher class 10k field than the County Championships he would come up with something a little closer to his potential. And so it was at the Southern Counties Championship at Crystal Palace on 11 September where he ran to a fine Silver Medal and a time of 29.49.4 - fastest by a Belgravian for 17 years! It was also at this meeting that Matthew Kinane confirmed his progress this year by breaking the longstanding Club Youths Mile Record with 4.26.0 in 7th place in the Peter Coe mile. * * * International Youth Friendship Games - Crystal Palace - 29 September - JOHN REGIS 20.78!!! John Regis was really in a purple patch at the end of the season and his final race produced a brilliant 20.78 clocking over 200m to succeed Ernie Obeng as Club record holder; I believe that only 3 British Juniors have ever gone faster. And in case you didn't know it, John is still a Junior next season!! Another spectacular performance came in the 4x200m when Mike Bazire, Phil Goedluck and Marcus Adams joined John to clock a time that only 2 UK National teams and a Haringey club side, amongst British teams, have ever beaten. There were some other pretty good performances as well - if that's not an understatement - with Marcus Adams, Phil Goedluck and Youth Joe Minetti all sprinting magnificently. How the Club Mile Record Has Progressed Club records were not formalised until after 1950 and our early history is a little short on details such as times. items.sum: Harry Porter's winter report on the Belgrave women's section: first inter-counties representatives, county and Surrey League team medals, the walkers and winter training.
items.s: WITH THE LADIES Harry Porter's winter report on the Belgrave women's section: first inter-counties representatives, county and Surrey League team medals, the walkers and winter training. WITH THE LADIES It has been quite an exciting winter. This year was the first time we had had representatives (Rosemary Honeychurch, Vicky Mitchell and Jenny Webb) in the Southern Inter Counties and National Inter Counties Cross Country Championships. Also the first time we have gained team medals in County Cross Country Championships (the Surrey Intermediate Team of Jenny Webb, Gail Porter and Andrea Coore who finished 3rd team). The first time we had had an individual winner in the Surrey League Cross Country Championships (Rosemary Honeychurch) and also we had team winners in the same race (Rosemary Honeychurch, Vicky Mitchell, Jenny Webb and Debbie Hankins). We also finished a Senior Team in the National Cross Country Championships (37th). In the Surrey League Rosemary Honeychurch finished 3rd individual over the 4 races and in the Inters Jenny Webb was 5th and Vicky Mitchell was 6th. Our Walkers have been doing well with Gail Porter and Rachael Parrott (who won a race in the Cambridge Harriers Walking League) well to the fore. Our winter training has been quite well attended with good attendances on Saturday afternoons and Sunday mornings at Belgrave Hall, and Sunday mornings at Battersea Park and Wednesday Evening Circuit Training Sessions have also been well attended. items.sum: Profile of Rosemary Honeychurch, the women's section's leading middle-distance runner, and her big 1984 improvements at 1500m and 3000m.
items.s: 'DYNAMITE' ROSE Profile of Rosemary Honeychurch, the women's section's leading middle-distance runner, and her big 1984 improvements at 1500m and 3000m. 'DYNAMITE' ROSE ROSEMARY HONEYCHURCH: Alias "Dynamite Rose" is "Belles" leading middle distance star, and is a 21 year old student at Whitelands College where she is studying for a degree in sociology. How many of you have taken 32 secs. and 65 secs. off your P.B.s for 1500m and 3000m in one season? "Dynamite" did just that!! At the start of the 1984 season her best 1500m was 5.17 - at the end - 4.45. Her best 3000m was 11.07 - at the end - 10.02. Her coach (since last April), Derek Crookes says she is a "Dedicated trainer" who does everything laid down in training schedules, and is an out and out fighter. 1984 saw her win the Surrey County Senior 3000m and this was followed up by representing Surrey in the same event. Her winter "hobby" is trying to run her coach into the deck over a hard 3 to 4 mile run most Saturdays at Wimbledon. She represented Surrey in the Inter-Counties C.C.Champs 1985 but her best run was to chase Ann Ford in the C.P. 6km road race at the end of December. Rosemary Honeychurch ROSEMARY HONEYCHURCH student at Whitelands College; 1984 improved 1500m 5.17 to 4.45 and 3000m 11.07 to 10.02; won Surrey County Senior 3000m 1984; represented Surrey in Inter-Counties C.C. 1985 ROSEMARY HONEYCHURCH Dynamite Rose Dynamite Derek Crookes Derek Crookes Rosemary Honeychurch's coach since April 1984 Ann Ford Ann Ford Surrey County Championships Inter-Counties Crystal Palace Open Road Race Whitelands College Wimbledon Crystal Palace Surrey

items.s: SUMMER ROUNDUP Derek Jones's farewell summer round-up as Ladies Secretary: the women's team's promotion to Southern League Division 2, Wendy Dunsford's loyalty, the junior relay squad, and thanks to coaches and his successor Harry Porter. SUMMER ROUNDUP After the good winter season with the Seniors coming 2nd in the Surrey Cross Country League and finishing a team in the National, the start of the Track season was a bit disappointing. In our two warm up meetings we finished 5th out of 6 and 6th out of 7 and we were a disappointing 2nd in our first Southern League to put us in 9th spot in the table. Even after the 2nd Southern League we were 7th and in the next 3 matches we had to meet all the teams above us. However, everybody got stuck in and competed out of their skins in the last four matches with the result that we did what we wanted to do and got promotion to Division 2. So well done to all concerned. It really was a fantastic result, especially those last 4 matches in the Southern League. I would like to mention the determination of Wendy Dunsford who, over the 6 years has competed in a remarkable 44 Southern League meetings out of a total of 46. The September meeting was her 39th consecutive Southern League. In the Thameside League the girls finished 5th, but the Juniors were level on League points with Camberley and just lost out on insufficient match points (by about 7½). Just one mention which I almost forgot and that is the Junior Relay squad who in the last 2 seasons crossed the line in first place in League Races (Southern & Thameside) and Inter Club matches on no less than 22 occasions. (Unfortunately one resulted in a disqualification). They also gained a Bronze in the Southern Counties Womens AAA as well as coming 5th in the WAAA Championships. Finally, I would like to thank everybody who came along to give their help and support. Please keep it coming. I would also like to thank everybody who has contributed over the six years I have been Ladies Secretary. I think I can safely say that I leave the section in a healthy state, which is no thanks to me, but to the efforts of all the athletes and those who have helped. I would like to thank Frank Simmons and John Gould for their help and coaching skills. To my successor Harry Porter I wish Good Luck and thank you for the help you have given me over the past few seasons. I hope you get the same co-operation as I do. I will certainly be on hand with help and advice. Good Luck for 1986. DEREK JONES Wendy Dunsford Wendy Dunsford competed in 44 of 46 Southern League meetings over 6 years; 39 consecutive Frank Simmons Frank Simmons coach, women's section John Gould John Gould coach, women's section Harry Porter Harry Porter successor as Ladies Secretary Derek Jones DEREK JONES Ladies Secretary for six years, retiring 1985 Surrey Cross Country League National Cross Country Championships Southern League Thameside League Southern Counties Womens AAA Championships WAAA Championships Camberley

A good performance from Diane Bowen breaking the Club Record in the Junior Ladies Discus by nearly 4 metres, this could possibly put her among the top 20 Juniors. The other record breakers were Vicky Mitchell in the 800m (Intermediate), Joanne Hilliard in the High Jump and the 4x400m Relay Team of Rosemary Honeychurch, Gabrielle Collinson, Dezrine Conard and Vicky Mitchell. (I am afraid I have mislaid the split times of this, but I do know that Vicky's final leg was 61.8). Gail equalled her own 400m Hurdles record and the most notable personal best was Wendy Dunsford's 11.66 in the Shot pushing her team mate into the B string. Incidentally this was Wendy's 39th consecutive Southern League Meeting being present since June 1979 and since we started has only missed two Southern Leagues. Not a bad record and Wendy will always try whatever the circumstances. items.s: JOANNE HILLIARD Profile of New Zealand-born former GB high jumper Joanne Hilliard, who switched to the discus under Mike Winch and joined Belgrave in 1985, with her personal bests and club records. JOANNE HILLIARD Born in New Zealand on 1st March 1962 Joanne Hilliard moved to the U.K. at the age of 7. She became interested in athletics and started competing at club level at the age of 16, starting as an all-rounder before progressing on to training specifically for the high jump She trained with Ron Murrey for 5 years and gained her first International vest in July 1983 when she represented Great Britain in the G.B v France match. Further International appearances followed including a match in Norway in August 1983. It is perhaps surprising that with this background and a p.b. of 1.83 that the following April she should decide to give up the high jump. In September 1984 she decided to take up the discus and joined Mike Winches squad. She was among the first of Mike's group to start training in the Belgrave Hall gymnasium and set the travelling record by commuting three nights per week from St. Albans to Wimbledon for strength training. It was a natural progression when she moved to London early in 1985 that she should join Belgrave. Soon after she became engaged to another of Mike's squad- Blackheath Harrier and 80m+ javelin thrower Daryl Brand. Joanne has shown great promise in the discus and it is on the cards that both she and Daryl will see International competition in 1986. items.s: VETS. CORNER Vets Corner: Belgrave over-50s team gold at the Surrey Vets cross-country championships (Nov 1984), Laurie O'Hara's Vets A.C. 10 mile title and season of veteran successes, the S.C.V. AAA's 10 mile championship, and Snowy Brooks's seven club veterans' records. VETS. CORNER OVER 50'S WIN 11th NOVEMBER 1984 RICHMOND PARK SURREY VETS C.C. CHAMPS. Excellent runs by Pat O'Connor, Keith Sinclair and Tony Verdie in a star studded field, but it was the good packing by our over 50 men which provided the team gold over a hard undulating 10,000m course. M.40-49: 1.S.Warzee (Guild. & G) 32.04; 2.R.Gevers (SLH) 32.35; 3.F.Bell (Woking) 33.23; 4.D.Claxton (HHH) 33.51; Bels: 12.P.O'Connor 35.05; 17.A.Verdie 35.56; 18.K.Sinclair 35.56; 31.J.Wasbrough 37.29; 38.W.Laws 38.35; 40.F.Barrett 38.44; 44.M.Hanson 39.18; 57.A.Stone 40.52; 76.E.Thorpe 42.56. Bels: 9.C.Walker 39.16; 10.B.Stroud 39.58; 11.C.Henn 40.07; 27.G.Pearson 46.39; 32.C.Manning 49.35. Teams: 1.BELGRAVE 30; 2.SLH 33; 3.Ranelagh 42; 4.Mitcham 53. 11th MAY 1985 WIMBLEDON VETS A.C. 10 MILE Over 75 runners competed the Vets A.C. 10 miles Road Race Championship held over an accurately measured course around the road side and foot paths of Wimbledon Common. 53 year old Laurie O'Hara stuck to the two younger Hercules runners Kortenray and Fuller as the race hotted up over the final mile. Kortenray's finishing power gave him the verdict by seconds when he beat Fuller and O'Hara in a sprint to the line. However, Laurie took the Championship, as the first two were not qualified for the honour. Results: 1.M.Kortenray (HW) 54.46; 2.M.Fuller (HW) 54.48; 3.L.O'Hara (Belgrave) 54.50. Bels: 7.L.Mann 59.31; 9.J.Wasbrough 60.03; 12.T.Stone 60.15. 13th SEPTEMBER 1985 CRAWLEY S.C.V. AAA'S 10 MILE CHAMPIONSHIP Results: 1.L.Roberts (Blackheath) 50.43; 2.B.Buonvino (Dart) 51.52; 3.W.Davies (Hillingdon) 53.55. Bels: 13.P.O'Connor 56.15; 26.J.Wasbrough 58.13; 47.F.Barrett 60.43; 61.K.Duckett 62.43; 71.E.Stroud 63.27 p.b. 91.C.Cross 65.37; Teams: 1.Blackheath 14; 2.Hillingdon 20; 3.Cambridge 52; 6.BELGRAVE 86. THE AMAZING LAURIE O'HARA At the age of 53 do we detect that Laurie O'Hara is finally slowing down? Well only a bit. He's still managed to pull off track championships and on the road has troubled men 30 years his junior. For example:- Hillingdon ½ marathon - Open - 6th 1hr 13.02 Belgrave 1500m Champs - 4:14.0 Battersea 5¼ Mile 16.7.85. 1st Vet 27.36 Southern Vets Champs. Crawley 27.7.85. 1500 1st (o/50) 4.20 WL Vets Championship 31.7.85. 10,000m 1st o/50 33.20 West London Stadium - Open 3000m 7.8.85. 9:06.0 Alperton. 4¼ Mile Open Road Race 20.8.85. 12th. 22.31 Tooting Bec. Southern Vets Champs. 18.9.85. 1st (o/50) 33.19. And thats only a sample! He has decimated our Vets records this summer and seven of them now stand in his name. Steve Williams's updated Belgrave men's all-time top 10 lists for every track and field event (with year of each mark), starting on page 78 and finishing with the throws on page 77. ALL TIME TOP 10. Updated by Steve Williams The injection of new blood into the track and field team over the last four seasons, the unearthing of one or two more top performances from the past and improvements from already established members have meant a substantial number of changes to the Top Ten published in the April '82 magazine. Evidence of current track and field standards is provided by 72 new marks from the past four years, including 31 in the season just gone - not bad from a total listing of 212 performances. Those with eagle eyes wishing to compare this list with the previous one will note some imperial distance conversion amendments - these are now more accurate. As before, known wind assisted marks in the sprints and lateral jumps are excluded, as are indoor marks, and, to the best of my knowledge, only 1st claim members are listed. Continued on page 77. items.label: October 1986
items.sum: The new editor's opening ramblings, crediting Bill Laws's last mammoth issue, looking ahead to the centenary year, recalling sixty years as a Belgravian, and appealing for officials, fund-raising support and publicity.
items.s: EDITORIAL RAMBLINGS The new editor's opening ramblings, crediting Bill Laws's last mammoth issue, looking ahead to the centenary year, recalling sixty years as a Belgravian, and appealing for officials, fund-raising support and publicity. The Mammoth is not extinct!! It has in fact raised another mammoth edition of the Belgrave Bible. Bill Laws in his final fling as Editor dubbed the issue mammoth in the context of its bulk. He modestly failed to mention the mammoth task (not tusk) in the preparation of the tome, and I, because nobody else came forward agreed to try to keep things going and maintain the continuity. Bill has a very professional attitude in the jobs that he undertakes, and The Belgravian was no exception and I only hope that my efforts somewhat match up to his. This is Belgrave centenary year and a great deal of preparation work has been done by a band of members led by Clive Shippen to make it a real celebration and I am certain that if we all enter into the spirit of things and support all of the promotions to the utmost, it will be a year to remember. T.C.(Charlie) Jones and I are celebrating our 60th year as Belgravians as also I believe is Norman Dewberry (born 1902) and we have a vast store of memories and can well recall the halcyon days prior to World War II when the Walking Section, the Cross-Country and Road Relay Runners had won all of the National Championships plus many other major events whilst the Track and Field men had, with the exception of a few flashes of success, generally met with moderate success. Now the emphasis has gradually turned and the major successes have gone to the Track and Field men and this year has been stupendous for both Team and Individuals. Details, results for the year are to be found in this issue. For many years the club had, as compared with today, few summer inter-club committments. With men-only membership we had two annual inter-club fixtures - one with T.V.H. and Ashcombe A.C. for The Doris Shield which was one of the highlights of the season and also a triangular match with Mitcham AC and Croydon A.C. plus inter-club matches with such clubs as L.A.C. and Cambridge Harriers and invitations to the Kinnaird Trophy and Waddilove Bowl, all of these events were more or less limited to 6 or 7 flat events with 2 jumps and sometimes a couple of field events, but now it is reaching saturation point - multi team leagues for male and female - all age groups and whole gambit of track and field disciplines. We have a large active membership and we usually meet our committments but these very heavy fixtures require considerably more people to organise and officiate. So thats the rub - we have the athletes, but we need many more members to do the official and supernumerary jobs. The athletic success of the club is one thing, but the financial success is another. Ron Severn our intrepid Treasurer does a super job balancing the accounts, but to perform the miracles demanded of him we need a lot more hard cash, so we earnestly ask you all to support to the utmost, any of the fund raising schemes that will be launched for the club's benefit. Then to publicity. The club has 3 Press Officers who regularly send reports etc. to up to 10 different newspapers, but the number who take any notice is very small and whilst enhanced reports are agreeable, fair comment is always acceptable, so if anybody out there knows the way in - let's hear from you. Advertising time on television is very expensive to hire, but if all our athletes who are fortunate enough to be appearing at events shown on colour television would wear the Claret & Gold - when at all possible, that would be a bit of free advertising for the Club. items.h: WHY NOT BECOME A TECHNICAL OFFICIAL?
items.sum: Appeal for members to train as track and field technical officials, with Clive Shippen as the contact.
items.s: WHY NOT BECOME A TECHNICAL OFFICIAL? Appeal for members to train as track and field technical officials, with Clive Shippen as the contact. Our Club is suffering from an acute shortage of technical officials. Our track and field programme each summer covers young athletes, ladies, and men's fixtures in a variety of leagues and other competitions. In every case we have an obligation to provide technical officials. Why not try your hand at helping in this way? No previous experience is necessary and you may choose from the pre-season fixture list those meetings at which you are prepared to assist. All judges are only too happy to help newcomers learn the ropes. The following categories are used in track and field athletics :- Track Judge Field Judge Starter Marksman Timekeeper In November each year the Surrey County AAA give an evening's introductory lecture in Wimbledon for newcomers in all these disciplines. If you wish you may take a Grade 4 test the following week, but it is not necessary. All you need is a copy of the A.A.A. rule book, which all officials need to refer to from time to time. Officiating can be a most rewarding and enjoyable part of the athletics scene. Why not give it a try? For all the advice you need telephone CLIVE SHIPPEN on [phone number withheld]. Clive Shippen CLIVE SHIPPEN contact for would-be technical officials Wimbledon Surrey County AAA

items.s: grapevine Grapevine column of club news: births, Graham Macky's marathons, Jimmy Green's centenary gift, a letter from Indian journalist Rangit Bhata, Brian Pritchard's handicap, Kevin Sturman's season and the Honeychurch-Howell wedding. Congratulations to Ann and Guy Sagar on the arrival in February of a baby daughter. Congratulations to Debbie and Graham Macky on the arrival of a baby daughter - Bridie - born on Christmas Day. Graham ran a 2.16.17 marathon in Hiroshima in October '85 and lowered the club record to 2.16.11 a month later in the Beizing (Peking) marathon. No news yet on whether he's made the New Zealand Commonwealth Games Team. Graham also writes to say that while in China he met Alan Storey who is spending a year or so out there coaching. Alan said that the Chinese were still talking about the GB U'23 squad's visit last September. Gary and John caused quite a fashion/cultural shock! Anybody remember P.W.(Jimmy) Green? Jimmy a stalwart of Surrey A.C. since 1924 was the founder of Athletics Weekly. He also became associated with The Bels during, and for a time after, the war when he used the Belgrave Hall facilities for training, as 2nd Claim. He sends greetings to all those he trained with which includes Tom Carter and Charlie Smart. Jimmy is due to have a hip replacement during October and we wish him a quick and good recovery. In with his letter was an unsolicited gift to the Club Centenary Fund for which we sincerely thank him. Rangit Bhata came to Britain this year as a accredited journalist to cover the Commonwealth Games for an Indian newspaper but owing to the boycott of the Games by India, had to return home early. Here is a copy of a letter he sent to Clive Shippen. Oxford July 23 '86 Dear Clive, Today I should have been on my way to Edinburgh to cover the Games for our athletes, but the turn of events has made this a very unhappy trip for me. As I write, I am trying to change my flight so as to go back to work in Delhi, since the whole thing has now gone sour. Hopefully I would be able to plan a proper visit next year, to join all of you in The Centenary Celebrations. It was lovely to meet so many old friends at Belgrave Hall last Saturday. I think there were no two opinions when Don Maclean, Bob Taylor and I agreed that Belgrave Harriers embody what might be regarded as the best aspects of Athletics from every point of view and one hopes very much that the Club would continue to thrive as it has done in the past hundred years. I was also delighted to meet the elders of the Club who had done so much to encourage me in my running, nearly thirty years ago, and thanks to whom I have managed to stay in the world of runners. Please do convey my warmest regards to all the Bels and assure them that anyone coming to Delhi at any time would be assured of a warm welcome and sufficient running. Rangit P.S. Please let me have the schedule of events in order that I am able to plan my 1987 trip, as a runner in the Bels 100 years celebrations. Brian Pritchard is already working on his 1987 Yacht 3 Miles Handicap. Not only can he be seen hobbling painfully from a recurring knee injury, but we hear that he is due to become a Grandad in the New Year. Congratulations to Jane and Chris. Kevin Sturman travelled back to the U.K. with his charming wife Anita for a lengthy holiday this summer and raced for the Club whenever possible setting seasons bests of 14.23.13 for the 5000m and 29:48.2 for the 10,000m. items.s: IN MEMORIUM: GEORGE E. BENTLEY Obituary of race walker, RAF pilot and Metropolitan Police commander George Bentley, who died in Dorset in March 1986 aged 67. IN MEMORIUM GEORGE E. BENTLEY Passed away in March 1986, in Dorset aged 67. Joined Bels. 1939. One of a good number of Metropolitan Policemen who have served Belgrave well - brother of the renowned Fred Bentley he walked in many of our club teams and in 1947 he finished 5th in National Junior 10 Miles in which Belgrave finished 2nd team. Served with RAF during the war as a pilot and attained the rank of Flight Lieutenant. By a coincidence on the boat en-route for Canada for training he met up with brother Fred who, unbeknown to him, was also on his way to Canada to be trained as a navigator. George was a Grade I Race Walking Judge and on many occasions had been Chief Judge. He retired from the Met. Police in 1980 at the rank of Commander, he was also a Past Chairman of Met. items.s: LEN (GINGER) COLEMAN Obituary of race walker Len 'Ginger' Coleman, who joined in 1929, dead-heated for the 1938 National Junior 10 Miles walk title and died in Londonderry in January 1986 aged 72. Died at his home in Londonderry, Northern Ireland on January 26th, 1986 aged 72 years. Joined Belgrave Harriers 1929 as a runner and competed on track, road and cross country - transferred to Race Walking in 1933 and won many "Open" handicaps on the track in the years preceding the war. He was also a member on numerous occasions of our winning Road Walking teams which several times was made up by two pairs of brothers, i.e. Chas. and the late Harry Churcher and himself and brother Joe. In 1938 he dead-heated with brother Joe to win the National Junior 10 Miles (Garret Cup) Championship and with Colin Sutton (who was murdered by terrorists in Malaya) and Reg Elson to win the team title with a record breaking 16 points. Represented Surrey County on Track and Road and gained First Class Standards Medals in AAA 2 and 7 miles Walking Championships. Served in the Army from 1939 most of the time spent abroad with West African Frontier Forces, was torpedoed off South Africa on way to Burma and returned to W.Africa to complete second tour of duty there. At the cessation of hostilities he was seconded to the Indian Army as catering advisor and remained there until Independance 1947. On his return to Britain he attempted to get racing fit but too much tropics showed their effects and he finally satisfied himself by jogging with Frank Webb and Norman Dewberry on Wimbledon Common. He spoke fluent French and when in 1937 the Paris Club U.S.Metro visited us he surprised many club members with his bilinguel prowess when he acted as interpretter. He was a Club Life Member. (CHARLIE) MUNRO Obituary of Charlie Munro, a former Ashcombe St.Georges member and long-time inter-club official and Past President of the South of the Thames association, who died at Teddington in February 1986 in his early 90s. Passed away in February 1986 at a Nursing Home at Teddington. He was in his early 90s and had been becoming more ill with failing sight and deafness to add to his other discomforts. Charlie was originally a member of Ashcombe A.C. which later amalgamated with St.Georges Services to become Ashcombe St.Georges A.C. and joined Belgrave Harriers when his old club closed down. He had had a long association with the Bells through out inter-club events at which he was always a keen official and continued to do sterling work in other organisations, such as South of the Thames and Southern Counties Cross Country Assoc. of which he was a Past President until failing health took its toll. Charlie was cremated at Kingston Cemetary and many club members attended. C.F. (Charlie) Munro C.F. items.s: W.G. (Bill) True Obituary of race walker, club committee member, walking handicapper and Grade I walking judge Bill True, who joined in 1935. Bill joined the Club during 1935 when he came to Belgrave Hall to give a hand to his pal Charlie Churcher with the decorating, maintenance of the hall. He took up race walking and competed regularly in all club and open events. He served in the Army during the war and after the war resumed competing and was in the scoring team with George Bentley in The Garnet Cup race in 1948. He served on the Club committee for many years and was Club Walking handicaper for about 14 years, was a R.W.A. Grade I Walking Judge and officiated regularly until recently when his health deteriorated. Bill had a droll sense of humour and we will miss him. W.G. (Bill) True W.G. items.sum: Gordon Biscoe's profile of centenary-year president Bill Lucas: recruited in 1936, wartime Pathfinder and D.F.C., 1948 Olympic 5000m runner, cross country secretary, club president and national administrator.
items.s: 'Belgrave Centenary Year' W.E.LUCAS D.F.C. PRESIDENT Gordon Biscoe's profile of centenary-year president Bill Lucas: recruited in 1936, wartime Pathfinder and D.F.C., 1948 Olympic 5000m runner, cross country secretary, club president and national administrator. 'Belgrave Centenary Year' W.E.LUCAS D.F.C. (The 'W' stands for 'BILL') PRESIDENT It was in the early days of 1936 that Belgrave's spies first reported on a young runner of exceptional promise employed in the Insurance world, and it was Ernie Duffett, one of our past Presidents and Cross Country Secretary for 25 years, who undertook the task of trying to sign him on for Belgrave. This was done with good effect, and Bill Lucas became a member in February 1936. Bill's first test in Belgrave's colours came within a few weeks of joining, when he ran in the Southern Junior C.C. Championships and finished 32. (The race incidentally being won by Ted Stimpson). This effort resulted in the Belgravian scribe of the time writing, "Lucas, a newcomer ran well in his first important race in our colours and clearly has great potential." (Cont. p.8.) THE PRESIDENT - W.E.LUCAS D.F.C. The following December, in the Club 7m Championship, Bill finished 13th out of 24 finishers and took second prize in the handicap. Also about this time he finished 3rd in the Club Junior 5 miles Championship and scored in a winning Surrey Junior Cross Country team. In the Spring of 1937, Bill was brought in as a reserve for an Olympic runner, Jim Ginty in the London - Brighton Relay and ran a splendid sixth stage to maintain the lead we then held, and which was only lost in the last few yards at Brighton. It was obvious then that our young runner was destined for the highest class of competition. So he continued to improve, particularly on road and track. His long striding action was not too well suited to the country and his sympathies were not in that direction, but nevertheless they were very fine performances that were recorded in the years that followed. In 1939 came the war which was to change the course of so many lives. Sgt.Pilot W.E.Lucas became the official title of our young man, who later transferred from fighters to bombers and still later became Pilot Officer and eventually Squadron Leader, a member of the elite Pathfinder Group and a holder of the D.F.C. Bill was back with the club in 1946 and quickly found his running. He represented Surrey, won a South of the Thames Junior race and figured in a large number of successful teams. It was in 1948 that Bill reached the peak of his career for, although never having won a Belgrave Championship, a third place in the AAA three mile Championship gained him selection for the Olympic Games 5000 metres held in London. Following the games his running career continued with great personal success until 1954. During those years Bill won Surrey County titles at 1, 3 and 6 miles, represented Great Britain v. U.S.A. and Benelux countries, figured in a winning Southern Counties Cross Country Championship team as well as numerous Surrey County Championship teams and victorious road relay teams. Truly a great athlete, his career was such that it is not possible to itemise it here in detail. As Bill's active career drew to a close so his administration career began, first coming to the Belgrave committee in 1949 for which we have had his services ever since. Perhaps his first important role was to take over as Cross Country Secretary in 1954 from the man who brought him to Belgrave, Ernie Duffett. This post he held until 1969 when he handed over to Gordon Biscoe. For many years he was honary handicapper and has been of special assistance to our finance sub-committee and at our social gatherings. He was first elected President of Belgrave in 1963 and became a trustee some years later. Outside of Belgrave Bill's activities have been just as impressive. His voice became known to thousands, possibly millions, as the clearest and most competent announcer at the former White City meetings. In the ensueing years his efforts have earnt him continued recognition. He served Surrey County as a team manager and has at various times been President of: Surrey County A.A.A. Southern Counties C.C.A. South of the Thames C.C.A. Southern Counties A.A.A. Insurance A.A.A. and is a Vice-President of the A.A.A. Now retired, Bill lives happily with his wife Sheena (also a loyal friend and stalwart supporter of Belgrave) in Cowfold, Sussex and keeps in trim by playing golf and tending to his estate. He is of course still active on committees at area and national level and is currently member of a working party studying the possibilities of a single body for amateur athletes. More recently he was rated by the Southern Counties as their nomination for President of the A.A.A. In spite of his activities in the higher echelons of athletes Bill still maintains his Club activities and has been a Track Judge for over 30 years. As an athlete or administrator, Bill Lucas has never been one to settle for second best, always setting himself high standards and to anyone in athletes who is not prepared to apply himself with similar dedication, Bill's somewhat forthright manner sometimes leaves them in no doubt as to his feelings. So it is then some fifty years on we may still congratulate outselves for Bill signing in 1936 when now by virtue of his athletic career, administrative ability, personal integrity and competiveness he has been unanimously elected as our Centenary President and the man to lead Belgrave Harriers forward to its next hundred years. We could have no better figure head. GORDON BISCOE W.E. items.label: October 1986
items.sum: Centenary President Bill Lucas's message to members, recalling the club's past dominance and urging every section to make 1987 a great year.
items.s: From the President. Centenary President Bill Lucas's message to members, recalling the club's past dominance and urging every section to make 1987 a great year. Belgravians, In 1987 the Club is 100 years old and on September 25th, 1986 the members were kind enough to elect me as their President to cover the whole of the Centenary Year. This is the ultimate honour which can be bestowed on any Belgravian and I am deeply touched that it should fall upon my shoulders to lead Belgrave into a new era. This Club has made its mark on athletics in many ways and has lived to survive a whole century during which we have had two World Wars which deprived us of many excellent athletes. In my own opinion, and this I know will be shared by all the older members, our greatest achievements were in the period immediately before and after the last war. We were then predominant in all sections of the sport as shown on our Honours Board proudly displayed at Belgrave Hall. Our track runners were feared; our walkers held sway at all distances and our cross country and road runners devastated their opposition. It is the natural cycle of events that the predominance of any club should wane from time to time, but Belgrave has been fortunate to remain near the top and now we are enjoying a gradual return to fame by the achievements of our track and field team in rising from Division 5 of the National League to Division 1 in successive years and we all hope that we may win that division in 1987. We have in the Club many athletes of high calibre backed up by an excellent nucleus of above average performers and it would be my hope that in 1987 we can concentrate our efforts not only to win top track and field honours, but to return to those halcyon days of the 30s and 40s when we won National, Area and County championships on the country and the road. Other clubs manage to raise teams for all these events and it is time Belgrave deposed such clubs as Aldershot Farnham, Birchfield, Gateshead, Thames Valley and Tipton. We have been on the fringe for a number of years, but have failed at the last hurdle. My thoughts go to the Belgrave 12 Stage Road Relay of 1986 which is also the Southern Area Championship - we finished sixth but it would have needed only two of our good athletes who stood by on the sidelines to have won that race and to have gone on to contest the National title. I have not forgotten the stirling achievements of the Race Walkers who kept Belgrave at the top for a long period of time. I hope they also will concentrate their efforts to make 1987 a bumper year. To our Juniors Youths and Boys I commend you to dedicate yourselves to your sport - you will be the backbone of our future teams when our present stars are no longer active. As for the Ladies, I am full of admiration for the progress you have made in the few short years since the section was formed. You have a nucleus of over one hundred members mostly active in some form or another. You also can help to make Belgrave the top athletic club in 1987 and for many years thereafter by selecting a goal and devoting yourselves to its achievement. We are fortunate in having a first class team of sectional Secretaries, Committee Members and workers behind the scenes who are there to help you all. They blend together with the one object of showing the claret and gold vests to the British public and even to the world. Do not let their efforts go to waste by any lack of support. As for myself, I will devote my energies towards the same objective and will do everything in my power to assist any member who is in any way in doubt as to his or her future in Belgrave. Thank you all for your confidence in electing me as your President for the most prestigious year of our long history. We are not the first club to have existed for 100 years, but with a little extra help and devotion from you all we may well become the greatest. BILL LUCAS Bill Lucas BILL LUCAS elected Centenary President on 25 September 1986 National League Southern 12 Stage Road Relay Belgrave Hall Aldershot Farnham Birchfield Gateshead Thames Valley Tipton

items.s: OUR PATRON Eddie Kulukundis Esq.. Article on the club's revival of the patron tradition, tracing past patrons from the club's founding to 1939, announcing that Eddie Kulukundis became Belgrave's patron in November 1985, and profiling his support for theatre and athletics (signed WRL); its last two paragraphs on page 10 are printed twice. OUR PATRON Eddie Kulukundis Esq.. Early tradition revived as Centenary year approaches The Patron Tradition When Belgrave was founded 100 years ago competitive athletics was in its infancy and mainly took the form of handicap racing with prizes for the winners. Entry fees went some small way towards meeting costs and it was club patrons who contributed towards the finances needed for the high quality prizes. A Club's prize fund was the most important part of its assets and successful clubs relied heavily on benefactors. In the early days Belgrave was particularly fortunate in attracting many eminent patrons. No doubt aided by its location in the Belgravia/Westminster area, these included; General Sir H. de Bathe J.P., the Hon. Lord Monk, the Rt. Hon. G. Goschen (M.P. for Westminster), the Rt. Hon. George Cubitt (later to become Lord Ashcombe) and W. R. Burdett Coutts of banking fame. From 1919 to 1939 our patron was Lt. Col. Sir S. Hoare Bt., M.P. The advent of World War 2 curtailed the activities of many athletic clubs and sadly after 52 years the tradition of patronage came to an end at Belgrave. The growth of athletics from the 1940's onwards saw more emphasis on track and field and road events with prizes often being donated by businesses. More recently we have seen the advent of big money for the very best athletes, the setting up of trust funds, and race promoters rumoured to have bottomless purses for the largest televised meetings. With these developments the function of a patron is now very different from that of a century ago. A modern day patron is most likely to be a person able to add to the standing of a Club through his or her pre-eminence in the sport. The relationship between Patron and Club has been likened to a marriage and when the idea of re-establishing an old tradition was first mooted a careful study was made of likely candidates. Eddie Kulukundis' name came top of our list and we were delighted when in November 1985 he accepted our invitation to become Belgrave's Patron as we move into our second Century. With these developments the function of a patron is now very different from that of a century ago. The relationship between Patron and Club has been likened to a marriage and when the idea of re-establishing an old tradition was first mooted a careful study was made of likely candidates. Eddie Kulukundis' name came top of our list and we were delighted when in November 1985 he accepted our invitation to become Belgrave's Patron as we move into our second Century. Eddie Kulukundis EDDIE KULUKUNDIS Who's Who devotes over 40 lines to Eddie and at first glance you would be forgiven for believing that his predominant hobby was the theatre. Chairman and director of several theatrical organisations including the Royal Shakespeare Theatre Trust, Eddie has supported a large number of London productions over the last 17 years. Balancing this interest in the arts is a passion for athletics formally represented by his Directorship of the Sports Aid Foundation, Vice Patron of the AAA's and more recently by his participation in U K team management involving GB Junior teams at European and World Junior Championships. In 1986 he was part of the official U K squad at Athens for the World Junior Championships. There can't be many members in the Club who have attended every day of every Olympics since 1960. Eddie has (well almost) and in 1984 at Los Angeles he was trackside as part of the Press Corps following his production of a series of coaching films for the IAAF. His knowledge of our sport is considerable and it is amazing how he can recall people and performances from practically any meeting you care to name. It would be a brave man who pitted his knowledge of athletics and athletes at world level against that of Eddie's. Since 1974 Eddie has quietly provided assistance to literally hundreds of promising young athletes struggling to reach their full potential. Earliest to benefit were Brendan Foster and Steve Ovett and Eddie recognised the needs of their coaches too providing help whenever needed. He has been unofficial patron to the U K junior squads since there early days and the majority of the U K's top juniors over the past 10 years owe a great deal to the practical support and kindness of Eddie Kulukundis. Eddie tells of how his great enthusiasm for our sport was converted to a practical involvement by 1968 400 m H Olympic gold medallist David Hemery. The occasion was the Munich Olympics when on being congratulated on a bronze medal David could only express his sadness that he had let everyone down. It was David's sportsmanship that kindled Eddie's interest in helping but it was not until the two met again at the 1974 Commonwealth Games in Christchurch that practical plans evolved. From that day Eddie's enthusiasm and help for up and coming Juniors has taken the tangible form of providing financial assistance for those in need. Undoubtedly he has got a great deal of pleasure in seeing so many achieve successes at the highest International level. Several of our up and coming Juniors have benefitted from his direct support over the last year with warm weather training for our sprinters and support via Mike Winch for our throwers. We hope that the special excitement of being part of Belgrave at this important time will provide a new experience for Eddie and that he will enjoy a greater involvement with the grass roots of our sport. We are certainly proud and honoured that he should have accepted our invitation to be our Patron. We aim to make him proud to be part of us in the years ahead. items.s: The A.G.M. Report of the Annual General Meeting of 25 September 1986, covering subscription increases from July 1987, Ron Severn's election as Vice-President, the election of Bill Lucas as President and the full list of club officers and section captains for 1987; the attendance figure is left blank in the print. The A.G.M. ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING The A.G.M. was held at Belgrave Hall on Thursday 25th September 1986 and attended. At the E.G.M. which preceded the meeting the amendment to Rule 5 (b) was carried unanimously with little or no discussion. The main meeting then proceeded with the usual business procedures. Joe Coleman gave the Hon.Gen.Secs. report with particular mention to the necessity for more club officials, particularly in the Track & Field section also for more coaches and the outstanding performances of teams and individuals during the Track season. Ron Severn rendered his report as Hon. Treasurer and explained many of the facets of the balance sheet which received and accepted with a vote of thanks to him and the two Auditors Ken Miller and Ron Conway. The next business was the election of Ron Severn to the Vice-Presidents list. This was to honour him for services to the club which, although being a Club Member for a few years had given us much considerable assistance using his professional know-how. He was elected unanimously. The meeting then considered the committee proposal that the club subscriptions should be increased to the following scales: Seniors £15, Juniors (u/20) £10, Young Athletes £6, 2nd Claim and Associates £10. Bill Lucas proposed the motion and spoke of the club's real need for increased finances, this was followed by a short discussion and the motion was carried - only one voting against. The new subscription rates take effect as from July 1st 1987. The election of the Club Officers for 1987 then followed. The committee nomination for W.E.(Bill) Lucas for President was unanimously accepted and after exchanging niceties with outgoing President - Gordon Biscoe - Bill Lucas then took over as Chairman and the other Officers were then elected, viz: Hon.Gen.Secretary: Joe Coleman Hon. Treasurer: Ron Severn Section Secretaries: Walking - Carl Lawton Cross Country - Colin Pearson Road Running - Colin Pearson Track & Field - Leo Coy Veterans - Tony Stone Coaching - Bill Laws Official - Derek Crookes Hon.Sec.Hall & Social: Eric Crutcher Membership Secretary: Carl Lawton Young Athletes: Cross Country - Reg Hopkins Track & Field - Jim Mote Ladies: Track & Field - Harry Porter Cross Country - Harry Porter Trustees: - Tom Carter Frank Webb Bill Couzens Bill Lucas Hon. Auditors: Ron Conway, Ken Miller Press Secretaries: Sue Parrot, Geo Piddington, John Wasbrough Hon.Handicapper: (Running) Arthur Bruce - Hon.Starter: Arthur Penny Committee: - K.Duckett, Sue Parrot, J.Morris, A.Paton, D.Mote Hon. Editor Belgravian: - Joe Coleman The following were elected as Section Captains - Track & Field - Mark Lindsay-Bailey Cross Country - Dave North Road Running - Olly Foote Ladies Track & Field - Rosemary Honeychurch Ladies Cross Country - Rosemary Honeychurch Walking Section (Yet to decide) Any Other Business: The Club Centenary was discussed and Clive Shippen gave details which are announced in more depth in article on other pages of magazine. Bill Couzens reported on both this year's Dinner & Dance and also the Centenary's Grand Dinner & Dance. The meeting closed at 9 p.m. approx. and a large proportion of the attenders retired to the bar to heed the Hon. Treasurer's appeal - I will not put it in writing, but Ron will give you a demonstration anytime, but only at Belgrave Hall Bar, and at Bar hours also bring a container - He will also explain as to why a container!! items.sum: Profile of Belgrave race walker and administrator John Keown on his appointment as President of the Race Walking Association for the club's Centenary year.
items.s: PRESIDENTS ELSEWHERE R.W.A. John Keown. Profile of Belgrave race walker and administrator John Keown on his appointment as President of the Race Walking Association for the club's Centenary year. PRESIDENTS ELSEWHERE R.W.A. John Keown. It is with great pleasure that in our Centenary year that the parent body of Race Walking in this country should honour a Belgrave Harrier with its highest office for the ensuing year, thus carrying on a tradition of previous Belgravians like Frank Thomson, Alf Harley, Syd Roberts, John Goswell who held this high office. John joined the club in August 1954 and although never reaching the top echelon of walkers, turned out to be a first class club man, a true Belgravian, always to be relied on to back up our teams in any event. Walked his first Belgrave Open November 1955, finishing 122nd out of 200 starters in 67.20. But his true forte was eventually in distance events, and he holds the unique Belgrave record of finishing in twenty-six consecutive London to Brighton Open Walks 1959 to 1984 when it was discontinued owing to traffic and members decreasing problem. He won his first Brighton Winning Team medal in 1961 as fourth club man home in 15th position in 9:26.08, and in the last two years of this Open Walk, has won the Club Long Distance Championship and holder of the Brighton Cup being the only Belgravian to finish. This year he annexed the 'Jimmy Belchamber Cup' and Club Championship in the National 50 Kilometres, being again the only Belgravian to finish in this event. He gained his Centurion's Badge No.473 in the 100 miles at Ewhurst, Surrey in 1971, finishing in 20 hrs 49mins 27secs and so joined this illustrious band of Walkers, and he has also run and finished in a London Marathon. Besides his unique racing career, John is a first class administrator. Co-opted to Southern Area R.W.A. Committee when he took over the Editorship of Race Walking Record in December 1962, which he edited until February 1968, he has served on both Area and Main Committees ever since, and was R.W.A. Assistant Secretary 1980-83. He has been responsible for drafting and amending rules of the Association for many years, was elected Trophies Secretary in February 1978 and is still responsible for all R.W.A. Trophies, attends all Championships and ensures Medals and Trophies are available for presentation, besides walking in most events. He has organised the S.A.R.W.A. Track Walk Competition since its inception in 1972. Notwithstanding all this, you will still see John selling programmes outside Belgrave Hall before the start of the Open Walk, then at last minute, dash in, change, and then walk in the event. He will assist in any way he can. A true Belgravian, a credit to the sport, which has brought him an honour he richly deserves. We wish him well. May he have an enjoyable and great year in office. items.s: S.T.C.C.A. Derek Crookes. Short tribute to Derek Crookes, President of the South of the Thames Cross Country Association this year, listing his many club and county offices and his running career (part of the 'Presidents Elsewhere' feature). S.T.C.C.A. Derek Crookes. Derek must be one of the greatest collector of "jobs". In the club, which he joined in 1954, he has been Road Running Secretary, Coaching Secretary, General Secretary and President 1981/82. In Surrey County AAA he has been Assistant Secretary, Road Running Secretary and President 1984/85. In the South of the Thames Cross Country Assoc. he has been Sec. for many years and finally this year is President. Other than these "jobs" he finds time literally to act as timekeeper at Track, Road and Cross Country and occasionally Race Walking events. He is a very creditable organiser - and has been responsible for our 20 Miles Road Run for many years likewise in County Athletics he has been a very active worker. He had a very fine record as an athlete and competed in all running events from sprints through middle distance to cross country and road and eventually to marathons. Well done Derek, sorry if any "job" has been overlooked but if rumour has it right, as soon as you got the chain off your neck there's another in the offing. Mary - buy another tin of metal polish!! Derek Crookes Derek Crookes joined 1954; club President 1981/82; Surrey County AAA President 1984/85; South of the Thames XC Assoc. items.sum: The Hon. Treasurer asks members to donate the odd pence (or the difference to a multiple of five pounds) from their bank balances to club funds.
items.s: RON'S MASTERPLAN The Hon. Treasurer asks members to donate the odd pence (or the difference to a multiple of five pounds) from their bank balances to club funds. RON'S MASTERPLAN Donations: Some members of the Club would like to make donations to its funds from time to time, but feel than an amount they could afford would, perhaps, be too little to be worthwhile. This is fully understood. At the last A.G.M. I made a suggestion which all members may like to adopt. I put forward the idea that when a member gets his or her bank statement from the bank, they might send me a cheque, made payable to the Club, for the odd pence in the final balance. Thus, if that balance were, say, £118.76 their cheque would be for 76p. A further suggestion on this is that if they felt able to, their cheque could be for the difference between the balance and the nearest multiple of 5. In the example I have given, the cheque would be for the difference between £120 and £118.76 namely, £1.24p. If, however, the balance were to be, say, £116.50p the cheque would be for the difference between that figure and £115, i.e. £1.50. These may not seem very large amounts in themselves, but I am sure you will appreciate that if enough members did it, the gain to the Club would be quite substantial. It would also, I hope, be painless for members. I look forward to receiving hundreds of cheques from you. Don't bother with covering letters. Perhaps I can thank you in advance? [address withheld] RON SEVERN Hon. Treasurer Ron Severn RON SEVERN Hon. Treasurer Wimbledon

Look-back column reprinting notes from 25 years ago (Belgrave retaining the R.W.A. 50 km team title, Ray Middleton second to Don Thompson) and 40 years ago (the first post-war cross-country season in which Belgrave won every open championship, including the English National). From THE BELGRAVIAN ..... 25 years ago .... BELS. RETAIN R.W.A. 50 KILOS Having narrowly lost two of their three National titles our boys were determined to hold on to this, the last. And hold it they did. For although they were without Bailey, McGreechan and Yescombe they had three men home before any club could finish two. There was no doubt about this team result! Once more honours go to Ray Middleton who moved up yet again in his National placings finishing second to Olympic Gold Medallist Don Thompson, and setting a new Club record in his first 50 kilos! Ray was the only walker to make Thompson look beatable, and now has placings of 5th, 3rd and 2nd in the year's three premier events. He is surely on the threshold of achieving high honours. Ray Hall and George Beacham were always well placed and provided the backing for team honours. John Keown walked well to complete our scoring four and was closely followed by D. Bartliff and J. Morris. These three had had a rare battle for 4th place and it was only in the last mile that John asserted his position. & 40 years ago .... The first post-war Winter season was a memorable one for the Belgrave Harriers. Our cross-country runners won every open championship. In November we had the first two teams home in the South of the Thames "Junior" and the first three individuals. This in itself was a remarkable feat as all of our pre-war "cracks" cannot run in this race owing to the barring clause. In the New Year we won the Surrey County Title, whilst our Middlesex members, running for Cadogan A.C, took the Middlesex title. This was not regarded as very extraordinary as it had been done on various occasions before the war. The South of the Thames "Senior" Race resulted in another win for us. Here again, a large number of our best men are "barred". The Southern Counties' Cross-Country Championship 7½ miles, instead of the usual 10, was held from Belgrave Hall. Our Captain, Tom Carter, gained a well-earned and popular victory. With David Main third and four others in the first 20 positions, we gained a 99 points margin over the second team. In fact, our team of 12 was home before any other team had finished its six scoring men! Then to the much-awaited English Championship, of which we were the proud holders. On March 9th our lads travelled to Leamington Spa and had another battle royal with our famous Midland rivals, Birchfield Harriers. Our team finished in the first 24 positions, and after a breath-taking adding up of the scores we were acclaimed winners with a ten-points margin. We are indeed truly the Champion Club. items.s: CENTENARY CELEBRATIONS Account of the club's founding at the King's Head, Pimlico, on 7 October 1887 and its century of achievement, followed by the diary of planned Centenary events for 1987. CENTENARY CELEBRATIONS It was on Friday, 7th october 1887, that a group of athletics enthusiasts met in a room at "The Kings Head" Ranelagh Road Pimlico and formally decided to launch a new harrier club. There was much deliberation about the name it should carry. The West of Pimlico was in marked contrast to the high social status of Belgravia to the North and residents in the better parts of Pimlico were wont to call their area South Belgravia. For several reasons, the meeting decided to name the club BELGRAVE HARRIERS. The catchment area was Chelsea, Battersea, Westminster, Pimlico and Belgravia; an area which included Buckingham Palace itself! Within that area several other clubs existed, for it was a time when Victorian society was witnessing a boom in sporting activity. The clubs waxed and waned with startling frequency. Many died after short lives. Their fortunes depended entirely on the calibre of their officials and their ability to raise money for attractive prize funds. BELGRAVE HARRIERS suffered many vicissitudes and misfortunes as a club during its early years, but each time there was someone prepared to step into the breach and inject a new lease of life. As other clubs faded and died, Belgrave fought on with a spirit that has never left the club to this day. Those founder members, seated together in that little room at the King's Head 100 years ago, could never have foreseen where their actions would lead a century later. They could never have imagined that their successors would one day master the giants of that Victorian era - Birchfield, SLH, Finchley and Salford. But master them they did, at one time or another. The Club has had much to celebrate during its 100 years. National champions at both running and race-walking, and gold, silver and bronze medals for its members in the Olympic, European and Commonwealth Games. As we enter 1987 we rank in the top eight UK clubs with our position in Division 1 of the British Athletics League. We have a history of which we can be justly proud, and a future of exciting possibilities. We have much to celebrate and a great deal to look forward to. Our Centenary has arrived at the right time! It is hoped that all of our members, however distant or remote from our activities, will be able to attend at least one of our celebratory functions during 1987. We want to see everyone who has played a part in Club affairs return to the fold during the 12 months of our celebrations. The following diary of events has been planned. 31 Dec/Jan - New Year's Eve Party at Belgrave Hall. Centenary mementoes unveiled and available for purchase. Food, drink, music. 17 January - Cross-country match from Belgrave Hall versus English Cross-Country Union, Surrey County, Middlesex County and other clubs also celebrating their centenaries. After-match reception and buffet. 4 April - Belgrave 12-stage relay (incorporting SCAAA Championships). 11 July - Centenary Club Championships - Battersea Park. Special programme. Fine opportunity for re-unions. 18 July - The 36th Belgrave Open '20' - Souvenir programme. 25 July - River-boat trip on Thames. Food and music. Capacity for 300. Evening function. 7 October - Club birthday (Wednesday). An evening get-together at Belgrave Hall. Un-veiling ceremony. 11 October - Centenary London to Brighton Relay. A special once-only revival of the famous race featuring other centenary clubs and previous winners. Reception in Brighton. 14 November - Centenary Dinner at The Gloucester Hotel, Harrington Gardens, SW.7. South Kensington. Tickets £25 each. Number limited to 200. 28 November - The 68th Open '7' Walk. Special Centenary event. Souvenir programme. 26 December - Fancy dress handicap races on Wimbledon Common with special re-staging of the 1887 120 yards handicap sprint. 11 a.m. start. 31 Dec/1 Jan - Closing New Year's Eve party at Belgrave Hall to "see in" the Club's second century. It is apparent from the above diary that 1987 is going to be an expensive year for the Club. We are still paying for the recent modernisation of Belgrave Hall and our Treasurer is obliged to keep a tight hold of the purse strings. However, a Centenary fund has been opened which we hope will help to defray the substantial costs of our programme. We therefore appeal to all members to send the Club a Centenary birthday present preferably before the programme commences. A word of warning about the Centenary Dinner. The number is restricted and the demand could be great. You can reserve your places NOW and help the Club financially if you send in your cash order right away. 1987 is a special year in the Club's history. As a Belgrave Harrier you have much to be proud of and a great deal to celebrate. Do not let it slip by without making an effort to join in. CS. CS. CS. items.s: Hall and Social. Eric Crutcher's report on his first year running Belgrave Hall and the social programme, with thanks to helpers, plans for winter events, a notice that the New Year's Eve centenary party is by ticket only, the list of socials for 1986-87 and a note on club places in the 1987 London Marathon. Hall and Social. HALL AND SOCIAL - Eric Crutcher Having just completed my first year as Hon. Gen. Sec. (Social) and Hall Manager, there have been times when I wondered how Bill Couzens ran the show single-handed! Certainly without the assistance of Keith Duckett to clean the pipes (which produce immaculate pints), order/collect bar stock and assist on socials when working hours permit, my task would be much more difficult - thank you Keith. I would also like to thank all those members who have served on the bar rota during the year and at the same time appeal for more volunteers now. The duties are not onerous, involving about 3 hours work every 4 weeks or so and, as the accounts show, the bar is an important source of income in helping to fund club activities. In addition, Brian Gorman's efforts in providing the Saturday afternoon refreshments should not go unrecognised and Fred Paget's teas on Sunday mornings are much appreciated. Looking back briefly over the past year probably the best evening was a darts match between the under 35s and their seniors. Fought over 15 legs the match was perfectly balanced at 7 each going into the final leg where all 8 members of each team played. Tension and excitement were running very high but Mark Sinclair kept a cool head to produce the winning double. We'll certainly have a return match in the winter. The other notable feature of these last few months has been the reintroduction of suppers at the Hall which have proved very enjoyable. At this point I must say a big thank you to Sue Parrott who, in addition to helping at all the socials, (and officiating at meetings) has been tireless in whipping up support for these supper evenings. This was obviously for the first couple of events, but it was significant that neither Sue of I approached people directly for the October evening (relying instead on 3 posters in the Hall) and attracted less than half the numbers necessary for a successful evening, resulting in cancellation. We have planned more suppers for the winter but it would be much easier on the organisers if people wishing to support the suppers contacted us by the preceding Monday at the latest. Looking ahead, in addition to the darts challenge and suppers I have fixed dates for a table tennis tournament and a couple of extra darts evenings. The latter events are intended as less serious evenings than the "challenge match" and the Denmark Pot but I hope they will be equally well supported. In addition we will be holding a pre-Christmas disco and a Valentines Disco and I hope to fit in a "Music of the 60s" evening somewhere along the line! IMPORTANT NOTICE: NEW YEARS EVE You will be aware of the plans for a celebration at Belgrave Hall on New Year's Eve to mark the beginning of our centenary year. There will be live music (not a deafening disco!), a buffet and champagne up until 1 am. The centenary draw will be made during the evening for which you have already been asked to sell some tickets and may I ask you again to make every effort to raise money through this draw to help finance our special centenary events. Admission to the New Years Eve celebrations will be by ticket only. Although this does not sound very satisfactory for such a momentous occasion I am sure you will appreciate that with a Hall capacity of 140 and a club membership of over 700 it is unlikely that we would be able to accommodate everyone that would wish to be there. If we were to allow entrance to more than 140 then the Hall becomes overcrowded, uncomfortable and consequently unfair on those who booked their tickets well in advance. At the time of writing (23 October) we already have bookings for 70 tickets, so please ring Sue Parrott ([phone number withheld]) or myself ([phone number withheld]) as soon as possible to make sure of your place. YOU WILL NOT BE ALLOWED ENTRANCE WITHOUT A TICKET. I should be grateful if those who have already indicated that they wish to attend, forward payment for their tickets by early December please. LIST OF SOCIALS (all events start 8.00 pm) These events will only be successful if there is a good response from you. Please make every effort to support the club, especially in its Centenary year. With best wishes. 1987 LONDON MARATHON I have applied for an allocation of places in the 1987 London Marathon out of the 2,000 reserved for club runners who receive rejection slips. If you are one of those unfortunates but would still like to run, then please forward your rejection slip to the Hall as soon as possible. If there are not enough places then a draw will be held during early December.
