CENTENARY MEMENTOES I would like to start off with an apology to those of you that have posted order forms but have yet to receive goods. Unfortunately we have encountered problems with the supplies of the clothing and towels who have proved very slow in meeting our orders. We are pressing them to move as quickly as possible. Obviously this is not very satisfactory but I hope you will appreciate that we are dependent on the suppliers for action. If you are awaiting delivery of an order then please ring Sue parrott ([phone number withheld]) or Eric Crutcher ([phone number withheld]) to check on the situation. The items that are in stock at present are selling fairly well with the tee shirts (£3.35) and mugs (£1.50) in particular proving to be very good value. The umbrellas (£13.50), sweat shirts (£7.50) and bags (£8.00) have also proved popular. The china wallplates are very attractive and orders for these (remember it's a limited edition of 100 plates) have passed the half-way mark. Eric Crutcher's Hall and Social column appealing for bar staff, thanking helpers, giving the centenary draw winners and promoting the riverboat trip, club birthday and centenary dinner. Hall and Social. HALL AND SOCIAL - Eric Crutcher MORE BAR STAFF NEEDED! - a plea made last October and which obviously fell on deaf ears. Many thanks to those of you who have served on the bar rota over the past few months but the numbers are slowly dwindling and I would like to see some newcomers volunteer to help share the load. Just 2 or 3 hours once a month is all that is needed. In particular, I must again thank Keith Duckett for not only fitting in several sessions between his shiftwork each month but also cleaning the pipes every fortnight, ordering the beer and helping out at every social. He does a great job for the club. The centenary year kicked off with the New Year's Eve party which proved quite an occasion. Whilst the music may not have been to everyone's taste (I've learnt in this job you can't please all of the people all of the time!) the food certainly was, thanks to Sandra Tiernan and Sue parrott who co-ordinated the efforts of several of our ladies to produce a magnificent spread. The centenary draw was held at about 10.30pm but in view of the number of tickets sold (we raised £1800 profit) it was hardly surprising that none of the winners were present that evening! I hope that everyone who sold tickets received a copy of the results but should I have missed anyone the winners are shown below. My thanks again to those who sold tickets and/or made a donation towards the fund. Moving on to forthcoming events tickets are now available for the centenary riverboat trip on 25 July. The boat has a resident disco and buffet for the very reasonable price of £10 per head. We are hoping to fill the boat to capacity (300 places) and well over 200 tickets have now been sold so if you'd like to come along then contact Harry Porter ([phone number withheld]) or Eric Crutcher ([phone number withheld]) as soon as possible. The boat leaves Putney pier at 8.30pm and returns at 12.30 am. It should be a great evening. The Club's actual birthday will be celebrated on 7 October at Belgrave Hall to which all are welcome. The evening will be fairly informal with a birthday cake to mark the occasion. The centenary dinner at the Gloucester Hotel on 14 November is another event where the tickets are selling very quickly. If you intend going but haven't yet contacted Bill Couzens ([phone number withheld]) then do so quickly to avoid disappointment. Tickets at £25 each for what will be the highlight of the year. items.s: HALL AND SOCIAL Further Hall and Social notes by E.C. (Eric Crutcher) on catering at the invitation cross-country event, helpers, the under/over-35s darts match, a silver wedding surprise party, poorly supported suppers and hall roof repairs. HALL AND SOCIAL The invitation cross-country event saw another catering triumph when Margaret Stroud and Sue Parrott took responsibility for providing runners and officials with a meal after the race. The arctic conditions certainly made the chilli an appropriate meal (in name and nature!) and it actually received a mention in the AW! This is an appropriate point for me to thank Sue for her support behind the bar, mainly in serving refreshments. However, Sue has also helped me out at every social and especiallly put a great deal of effort and energy into planning New Year's Eve. I'm pleased to say that Margaret has also become heavily involved in helping out on the refreshments side (particularly during the week) for which I am grateful. In addition Brian Gorman has continued to look after the Saturday afternoon runners which is much appreciated. Mention must also be made of the efforts behind the bar of Brian Gorman, Keith Duckett and Bert Stroud in helping to make the catering such a success on all fronts. The return darts match between the under 35's and over 35's took place in February and it looked at first as if the over 35's were going to average last year's defeat when they led 5:3 after the singles. However, the 4 doubles matches saw a change in fortune and the score was 6:6 going into the foursomes. Any hopes of a repeat of last year's cliffhanger were dashed when the under 35's won both foursomes to take a winning lead. However, the over-35's salvaged some pride by winning the final leg. An enjoyable evening but despite playing as a member of the winning team I must say that the disruptive tactics used by some of my team mates against the opposition would certainly upset the AAA if they ever reached track and field! However, the most memorable evening was a surprise private party held in March to celebrate the silver wedding anniversary of Dave and Margaret Davies. Their daughters had asked months in advance to book the hall and outlined a plan to hold a "This Is Your Life" style reception. The end result was Dave and Margaret walking into an empty hall (apart from the disco equipment and a bottle of champagne!) whilst 80 friends from their wedding day onwards crammed into the bar area and did their best to keep quiet! Julie did an excellent job as narrator with Tina co-ordinating the guests and by the sound of the delighted exclamations greeting each arrival it was clear that the idea was an enormous success. It was superbly planned and organised and was certainly an evening with a difference. A disappointing aspect has been the lack of support for the suppers which were reintroduced last year. Despite publishing dates in the last Belgravian for suppers in January, February and March there were only a couple of approaches to Sue Parrott or myself to book tickets. Only the March event went ahead as a result of Carl Lawton rustling up support from the walking section. As with previous suppers, everyone had an enjoyable evening whilst Don Anderson and Val Tanner slaved over the ovens to produce a super Italian meal. If all goes according to plan the section of roof covering the ladies changing room and kitchen should be renewed this summer. Following this we shall be redecorating so if anyone is willing to lend a hand could they please let me know. This area is by far the most pressing concern but other areas will need remedial action in the forthcoming years. I owe my thanks to Arthur Penstone who despite having a serious knee injury which was curtailed his running has continued to help maintain the hall, particularly the electrical side. E.C. E.C. items.sum: Extracts from The Belgravian of 1962 (AGM and Ken O'Kell's honours boards, the youths' fourth in the National cross country, Ray Hall and Ray Middleton's walking) and of 1947 (the first post-war season, the National cross country at Apsley and the AAA Championships).
items.s: From THE BELGRAVIAN ..... 25 years ago .... & 40 years ago .... Extracts from The Belgravian of 1962 (AGM and Ken O'Kell's honours boards, the youths' fourth in the National cross country, Ray Hall and Ray Middleton's walking) and of 1947 (the first post-war season, the National cross country at Apsley and the AAA Championships). From THE BELGRAVIAN ..... 25 years ago .... The AGM of 1962. "In attendance were the best part of a hundred faces, young and old, the familiar and the almost forgotten. Many of us were introduced for the first time to a member of 40 years service, Ken O'Kell, a man with a genuine and fond affection for the Belgrave Harriers. Ken was present largely for the purpose of handing over to the Club two honours boards, one recording Past-Presidents and the other International athletes. These boards, one of which is already in place, are to grace the walls of our Headquarters." Youths Excel in 1962 National C.C. "Our youngsters gave a most heartening display of running and although Ken Redwood hit a bad patch to slip out of the scoring four, his place was taken by "Noddy" Edwards who made up positions at a rapid rate and flogged himself right through to the funnel. Initially, Belgrave were announced as third but Sale Harriers handed in a late result and the team were bitterly disappointed to find themselves relegated to 4th. This was the first occasion in the season that the team had been out of the medals. We were, however, first Southern club home. Positions : 22. D. Cocks, 30. J. Hampshire, 47. A. Morrison, 50. P. Edwards, 70. K. Redwood, 254. H. Satchell." Walking Review 1962. "Our two Rays of sunshine, Hall and Middleton, have certainly turned on the heat this summer. Their second and third place in the National 50 Kilos at Luton behind Olympic gold medallist Don Thompson was great stuff and earned them well-deserved places in Britain's European Games team for Belgrade. Ray Hall's magnificent win in the Stock Exchange London to Brighton walk earned him a headline of his own in the "News of the World" (back page of course!) "Record Walk for Ray (28)" glared the heading, but the write-up didn't mention that his time of 7 hours 58 minutes and 33 seconds had enabled him to enter that very select band of walkers who have beaten 8 hours for this journey. These are, Harold Whitlock, Don Thompson, Tom Misson and now Ray Hall. Three of them have represented Great Britain in Olympic and European Games - two winning titles in the Olympics and the third winning important International walks abroad. We wish number 4 on the list good fortune and the opportunity of proving himself the equal of those other three distinguished men." & 40 years ago .... APRIL 1947 "We are now at the end of what can be termed the first full post-war winter season. From the afternoon of the season's opening meeting at Belgrave Hall the atmosphere was set: time seemed to have slipped back and the years of the war became, in many minds, non-existent. As one who "arrived back" that afternoon not having been near Belgrave Hall since 1940, it was a startling joy to see again so many well-remembered faces and to be greeted with such a warmth of welcome. Many things have changed these past seven years and this club has lost some of its dearest and best members, but we are still a club with enthusiasm and unity about us. At present most things are opposed, or unhelpful, towards the pursuit of Athletics. This country, unlike many others, gives no official or material support to Amateur Sports Clubs of any kind. Whether this is for better or for worse is a debateable question, but it is is our heritage that such clubs as ours should be free to control and run their pursuits without any outside interference or aid, therefore what we achieve can verily be called our own. We have much to achieve, both for the benefit of the Athletic world in general and for the glory of this Club. The task of this Club in the future must be to build a strong, ALL ROUND Club." 1947 National C.C. "Held at Apsley over a course almost knee-deep in snow, this was definitely not a fair test to the runners. Len Herbert finished 6th and so gained yet another international vest, while Albert Frost ran in great style to finish 17th and so gain his club Honours Badge. Sutton Harriers the Northern champions, beat us for the team championship, although we retained the "Finch-Wayte" Cup awarded to the first Southern Club to finish. 6th L.W. Herbert, 17th A.E. Frost, 31st R.W. Tobin, 37th V.S. Blowfield, 51st E.S. Stimpson, 65th S.R.J. Eales, 80th E.H. Herbert, 92nd A.F. Mitchell. Teams: 1. Sutton H. 160, 2. BELGRAVE H 184, 3. Reading AC 187, 4. Blackheath 255." 1947 AAA Championships. "We had quite a good entry for these championships and our men put up a most creditable show. Charlie Smart ran an excellent race in the 6 miles event and although short of training finished a good third behind Chivers (Reading) and Peters (Essex B). Harry Churcher set a thrilling pace in the 2 miles walk, but was pipped by Hindmar of Sweden. Then Willie Nankeville set us roaring by making the pace in the 1 mile final, and he eventually finished 3rd to Garay (Hungary) and Slykhuis (Holland) in the record time of 4 mins. 10.6 secs. Len Marchant had to be content with fifth place in a fast-run 880 yards and George Lucas ran well to gain third place behind Lataster (Holland) and Olney (TVH) in the 3 miles, Len Herbert coming through late to finish sixth." J Marshall 32.36; 14 March 1987 Ham National and Inter Counties 10m for Men and National 5kms for Ladies This was the first senior national promoted by Belgrave for many years and thanks are expressed to all of those who responded to the call to come and help. Those that helped in some ways as timekeepers, recorders, judges, catering were all appreciated. Thanks must also go to the pupils and staff of Christ's school of Richmond for their help in distributing leaflets and helping on the day. Generally it turned out to be an excellent day and an extremely accurate course with only a minor traffic problem on one section. Unfortunately as a team we did badly. We finished a lowly 8th, well out of touch of placings, even without Paul Warburton's disqualification we would have not improved. The County Team was no better and left a lot to be desired. items.h: Surrey County x/c Championships - Report by Colin Pearson
items.sum: Colin Pearson's report and results from the Surrey County cross country championships at Frimley on 13 December 1986, where John Gladwin won the senior title and Belgrave took team silver in the senior and junior races; boys' and colts' results follow.
items.s: Surrey County x/c Championships - Report by Colin Pearson Colin Pearson's report and results from the Surrey County cross country championships at Frimley on 13 December 1986, where John Gladwin won the senior title and Belgrave took team silver in the senior and junior races; boys' and colts' results follow. Surrey County x/c Championships - Report by Colin Pearson A good result for the Juniors. We packed in well, but it was not quite good enough to beat Aldershot and Farnham with their scoring four in the first six places. They certainly deserved their fine win. Glyn came through well to finish second. He also looked the stronger at the finish. Graham, Martin and Andy showed the sort of backing which could give them a place medal in the Southern and possibly the National Junior races when Matt and Justin Chaston come into the team. Richard, Simon, Matt and Garry could have got a medal most years previously. Adam and John finished well but probably found the course rather tough. Thanks for your support. In the Senior Championship John Gladwin got his revenge over Clive Hensby for a couple of years back when Clive beat him in the Junior race. As they went out on the final big lap Clive was about 50 metres up on John but when they came into the playing fields with about 800 metres to go John changed into overdrive and went by the Woking to win by 8 seconds with Bob Treadwell about a half a minute further back. I am sure that Bob and Clive wish that John would stick to 1500 metres track running. Congratulations to John on winning his first Surrey Senior x/c title. John Wright was our second man home in 8th place and should earn him his first Surrey County Vest. Well done!! It was then a case of its and bits, Andy North, third Bels man home was struggling and we could tell by the look on his face that he was not happy with his own and knowing Andy he will be seeking revenge in the Southern and National. Frank Ward also showed that he intends to remain in the "A" team. We did have some good cheer when we collected our Silver team medals but we were lucky because if Olly or David had dropped out we would not have finished in the frame. They did themselves no good by running with the after effects of flu. Well done Seniors - and thanks again everybody for your support. 13 December 1986 - Surrey x/c Champion Frimley 1. items.sum: Report of the Belgrave Centenary cross-country race on Wimbledon Common on 17 January 1987, won by Surrey's Bob Treadwell with John Gladwin first Belgravian in 7th, followed by a two-page photo spread by Mark Shearman.
items.s: CENTENARY CELEBRATION CROSS-COUNTRY Report of the Belgrave Centenary cross-country race on Wimbledon Common on 17 January 1987, won by Surrey's Bob Treadwell with John Gladwin first Belgravian in 7th, followed by a two-page photo spread by Mark Shearman. CENTENARY CELEBRATION CROSS-COUNTRY 17th January 1987 - Wimbledon Weather conditions had been appalling during the preceding week, with heavy snow in Eastern Counties from Kent to Yorkshire. Rotherham Harriers, who had been particularly keen to take part in this fixture, found most of their team were snow-bound and were unable to travel South. Newham & Essex Beagles had similar problems but managed to find three members well to the west of their territory so at least made an appearance. Wimbledon Common was not too badly affected and the old revived course down the cemetery horse ride and up the Queensmere Hill presented no special problems. The ECCU, Surrey and Middlesex County Associations had done us the honour of bringing representative teams to celebrate our Centenary and in addition to the Beagles runners Derby and QPH also fielded teams. The race itself produced a clear-cut win for Surrey's Bob Treadwell who revelled in ideal conditions for him, leading from gun to tape. However, the ECCU strength soon made itself felt in the chase and they finished 4 of the next 5 runners home. John Gladwin ran carefully to avoid unnecessary injury, particulary on the frozen horse-ride section, but came through strongly to finish 7th. Young Justin Chaston ran particularly well to beat two of the ECCU team and finish 15th leaving a trail of good quality runners behind him. The team result was predictable of course, but that was not the most important part of the day's proceedings. Fifty runners had commemorated our 100 years of existence and each was awarded a Belgrave Centenary bone-china tankard as a memento of the occasion. Good quality prizes also went to the first three individuals. Hot chilli-con-carné, french bread, buns and tea were served up after the race, thanks to the stirling efforts of Sue Parrott and Margaret Stroud, whilst Brian Gorman and the bar staff kept the spectators in good fettle with their usual refreshments. It was a pity that of our six surviving England cross-country internationals only four could be present, weather conditions keeping Len Herbert and Gerry North away. Nevertheless, to join the ever-present Carter, Penny and Stimpson we were delighted to receive Verne Blowfield who was visiting Belgrave Hall again for the first time in 37 years! Many other guests were present, including the Mayor of Merton and representatives of the various cross-country organisations. In response to our President's welcoming address, words of appreciation were expressed by Barry Wallman (ECCU) and Alan Domleo (Derby) who felt sure that everyone had enjoyed both the racing and the hospitality. The cost of staging such a fixture, including the commemorative awards and the souvenir programmes, was considerable. The Club was especially fortunate therefore to enjoy the generous sponsorship of TOM CARTER who underwrote the total cost of this memorable occasion. BELGRAVE CENTENARY X/C RACE 17.1.87 (Photos by Mark Shearman) Above — John Gladwin finishing 7th. items.s: Indoor Round Up. Steve Williams' round-up of Belgrave's 1987 indoor season, led by John Regis' European Indoor 200m bronze and UK record, with John Gladwin, Ernie Obeng and Marcus Adam, and a note of ratified UK records. Indoor Round Up. (compiled by Steve Williams) The outstanding performance this season was John Regis' tremendous Bronze Medal run at the European Championships in Lievin, France in February. His third place came in the fastest ever indoor 200m race and his startling time of 20.54 was just 2/100ths away from the World Record as it stood beforehand. It was also the third time John had improved the UK Record. Continuing a remarkable season, John made the 400m men raise their eyebrows as firstly he slipped in an electrifying 45.6 relay leg against the USA and then set a Commonwealth best over 300m two days later, leaving two good American one lap specialists well beaten. Our other main man in the media, John Gladwin, made his indoor debut at the end of the season. John adapted readily to the tight bends, despite his 6' 3" frame, with a sub 4 minute mile win against the USA, showing an impressive burst of speed in the last 50 metres, and he followed that up by collecting a UK Indoor 2000m record behind the World 3000m Champion at the Dairy Crest Invitation. Ernie Obeng continued the fine sequence of 60 metre runs he has set up over the past four years with a 3rd place in the National Indoor Championships and International wins against Hungary and the USA. In Budapest, Ernie shaved one hundredth off his pb to record a fast 6.62 in an invitation run at the International meeting. Life begins at 30 Ernie! Marcus Adam made up a quartet of Belgravians in the same England team for the match against the USA for his Senior International debut, beating the American 'B' string. Marcus later retained his National Under 20 title in a Championship Best Performance and took the Silver medal over 60m in a pb. Timewise over 200m though Marcus's best was a nippy 21.76 in the Senior AAA's Series when still over a month away from his 19th birthday! Records Ratified John Regis's 200metres in 20.54 secs and the England team in the 4 x 400m Relay (John Regis, K Bentham, S Heard, P Harmsworth) time 3mms 7.04 secs at the European Indoor Champs at Lieven (France) have been ratified as UK records. items.sum: H.P.'s Ladies Section report on the 1986 league season (seventh in Division II), farewells to Tracy Denton (injured), Jo Hilliard (returning to New Zealand) and Frances Guy (leaving for the Middle East), a plea for more cross-country support, and a target of Division I in 1988.
items.s: The Ladies. H.P.'s Ladies Section report on the 1986 league season (seventh in Division II), farewells to Tracy Denton (injured), Jo Hilliard (returning to New Zealand) and Frances Guy (leaving for the Middle East), a plea for more cross-country support, and a target of Division I in 1988. The Ladies. After the good summer had by all in 1985 when we were promoted to Division II, I hope that everyone enjoyed the better competition we had in 1986 when Belgrave Ladies finished seventh in their first season in the new League. Well done by all. However, three sad things to report. First, Tracy Denton (javelin) will be sadly missed in 1987 as she has had to have surgery on her back. I am sure that all will wish her well and a speedy return for 1988. Come on Tracy, 46m +? Good Luck, H.P. Secondly, we have had to say Bon Voyage to Jo Hilliard who in December 1986 decided that it was time to return home to New Zealand. I think we have all enjoyed her company in her short stay with us and will miss her presence in the team. She wished me to say thanks to you all in the section for making her feel welcome and that she enjoyed very much competing and being part of the Ladies Section. She wishes the Ladies Section every success in 1987 and the future. I am sure with me you will all wish her well and hope that she enjoys her athletics back home. Good Luck, H.P. Thirdly, another lady we shall miss for four years from the end of September this year will be Frances Guy, who will be going to work in the Middle East. We all wish her good luck in the future and thank her for her support. Also the joy and fun it gave the Ladies Section to see her win the Poly Ladies and Belgrave Marathon Championships. Thanks, Frances - we hope to see you compete for us again on your vacations back in the UK. Again Good Luck, H.P. As you can see, Ladies, the results for the winter season were very disappointing over the country. First I must say well done to those few who turned out, and thank goodness they did. However, just a few is not enough and very disheartening for those who did. After all, running over the country surely is the basic training and stamina work for all middle distance runners and gives one a break from the long and full track season running on hard tracks. (The legs enjoy the break too). So let's see a few more new faces training at Belgrave Hall on Tuesday and Thursday evenings, Saturday afternoons and Sunday mornings during the winter. As we are lucky enough to have such a facility for goodness sake let's all use it. Next year, maybe, we won't have so many knee and leg problems. In 1988 I would like to see us go for Division I and I think the time will be ripe for most of you and for the Section. That's what I would like for you and the club to achieve. So Ladies it's all down to you - if you want Division I competition, go out and get it. Good Luck for 1987 - H.P. H.P. H.P. items.sum: Harry Porter regrets the small number of members who help at ladies' track meetings, thanks the officials and parents who do, especially 80-year-old starter Arthur Penny, and appeals for more helpers in the centenary year.
items.s: Footnote to all Belgravians: Harry Porter regrets the small number of members who help at ladies' track meetings, thanks the officials and parents who do, especially 80-year-old starter Arthur Penny, and appeals for more helpers in the centenary year. Footnote to all Belgravians: I am very disappointed in the support within the club. In the track season there are but a few, and they are a few, who come along to each and every meeting to help. There are some 800 members in the club and the same small group turn out. You do not have to be qualified to assist or help those people who are, who are now very few and some getting on in years. I would like at this point to thank those few officials, and the helpers who are mostly parents of the girls, for coming along and helping. One gentleman I would like to thank is our one and only starter Mr Arthur Penny, who is some 80 years of age and still my "man of the match". Thanks Arthur from all of us. I would like to be able to say the same for many more people next year. So come on all of you that are Bels, we all need your help to keep this the great club that it has always been. Especially as this is our Centenary year. Harry Porter Harry Porter Harry Porter Arthur Penny Mr Arthur Penny the ladies' only starter, aged about 80 Mr Arthur Penny Arthur

items.sum: Boxed appeal for members to become technical officials, describing the categories, the Surrey County A.A.A. introductory lecture each November, and Clive Shippen as contact.
items.s: WHY NOT BECOME A TECHNICAL OFFICIAL ? Boxed appeal for members to become technical officials, describing the categories, the Surrey County A.A.A. introductory lecture each November, and Clive Shippen as contact. WHY NOT BECOME A TECHNICAL OFFICIAL ? Our Club is suffering from an acute shortage of Technical Officials. Our Track and Field programme each summer covers young Athletes, Ladies and Men's fixtures in a variety of leagues and other compotitions. In every case we have an obligation to provide Technical Officials. WHY NOT TRY YOUR HAND AT HELPING IN THIS WAY?. No previous experience is necessary and you may choose from the pre-season's fixture list those meetings at which you are prepared to assist. All Judges are only to pleased to help newcomers to learn the ropes. The following Categories are used in Track and Field athletics--- TRACK JUDGE, FIELD JUDGE, STARTER, MARKSMAN and TIMEKEEPER In November each year the Surrey County A.A.A. give an evening's introductory lecture at Wimbledon for newcomers in all these disciplines. If you wish you may take a Grade 4 Test the following week, but it is not necessary. All you need is a copy of the A.A.A. Rule Book, which all officials need to refer to from time to time. Officiating can be a most rewarding and enjoyable part of the Athletics scene WHY NOT GIVE IT A TRY?. For all the advice you need Telephone --- CLIVE SHIPPEN [phone number withheld]. Clive Shippen CLIVE SHIPPEN contact for would-be technical officials Wimbledon Surrey County A.A.A.

items.sum: Report and photographs (by Joe Coleman) of the club's Boxing Day fancy dress run at Wimbledon in 1986, where Brian Pritchard's 'Boat Race Four' coxed by Bill Laws won the prize, followed by Biscoe Punch and mince pies at Belgrave Hall.
items.s: Boxing Day, Wimbledon 1986. Report and photographs (by Joe Coleman) of the club's Boxing Day fancy dress run at Wimbledon in 1986, where Brian Pritchard's 'Boat Race Four' coxed by Bill Laws won the prize, followed by Biscoe Punch and mince pies at Belgrave Hall. Boxing Day, Wimbledon 1986. This year's Fancy Dress Run was blessed with a nice bright, sunny and mild day and despite the fact that there is no public transport on Boxing Day there was a very good entry and a good following of supporters. There was a wide range of ideas on what is deemed as Fancy Dress and the photographs above and on the following page of those who caught the camera's eye indicates that there was no lack of originality. The prize for the best entry, judged by a panel led by Mrs Sheena Lucas, was awarded to Brian Pritchard's Boat Race Four ably coxed by Bill Laws. The photograph does not do justice to the entry - the four oarsmen with their back to front heads, 'dummy' arms and legs to simulate the correct rowing stance was very unique and bearing in mind that the origins of Belgrave Harriers was with the rowing fraternity, it was also very topical. After the run it was back to Belgrave Hall for what is now the traditional "Biscoe Punch" and lashings of mince pies. Those appearing in the photographs amongst whose disguise can be seen through are:- Johnny Morris, Lionel Mann, Tootsie Gannon, Bob Bridges, Andy Paton, Ron Severn, Jackie Smiter, Geo Flanagan, Ben Cooper, Bill Laws, Olly Foote, Ross Bros, Matt Kinnane and Rin Tin Tin. Our thanks to all those volunteers who always seem to be there behind the scenes preparing the food, doing the washing up etc and often finishing up without a bite because it's all gone. Thank you very much. Boxing Day, Wimbledon 1986.
